News.title: Harry’s Invictus Games challenge in Kenya is helping veterans battle physical and mental scars
News.content:
Wounded veterans from 10 countries have gathered in Kenya’s Great Rift Valley for a week of endurance challenges, organised by the charity behind Prince Harry’s Invictus Games.

Twenty-five serving and former personnel, among them a Ukrainian who survived a direct bomb hit in Donetsk and a Danish combat engineer who cleared roadside bombs in Afghanistan, will run, hike or cycle up to 120km across the area on Saturday October 10, World Mental Health Day.

The Invictus Games Foundation, the charity the Duke of Sussex founded in 2014 for wounded, injured and sick service personnel, has organised the event.

For Vasyl, a Ukrainian soldier, it will be his first time in Africa and his first long-distance challenge.

After three weeks of military training in the UK, the 34-year-old joined a brigade in Donetsk as a reconnaissance squad commander, spending more than 19 months on the front line. He was wounded when a drone dropped a grenade three metres from him, and the shrapnel still causes frequent pain in his leg which can sometimes make walking difficult.

But he said the physical injury was easier to bear than the loss of the friends he made in the trenches.

“There is a level of kindness between comrades in a trench that you will never find in civilian life,” he said. “If someone made a mistake or said something wrong, we immediately forgave them and thought nothing more of it.

“For me, the pain of loss is the hardest thing the war has left behind.”

News.title: From Yale to the Congo: The mathematician who became one of Africa’s most intrepid reporters
News.content:
Sundaram has a lot of experience with the Rwandan methods of control. After spending 17 months in DRC, he moved to Kigali and he is eloquent about the convoluted effects of dictatorship. “Living in Rwanda taught me so much about how dictatorships function internally and how counter-intuitive they can be. A friend of mine who was working in public health told me ‘When we ask people in India to wash their hands we get a 30 per cent success rate from a campaign, but when we need people in Rwanda to wash their hands, we just need to slip a line in one of Kagame’s speeches and we get a 90 per cent success rate. That’s fantastic isn’t it?’

“And I said, ‘well is it? It’s great for short term health outcomes but what does that say about society? Isn’t democracy about people choosing freely? What if the government tells them to do something bad – like what happened in the genocide when people were told to kill all the Tutsis?’

“Kagame and his army stopped the genocide, and he has restored peace, but he governs using the same system that was used to perpetrate the genocide.”

In Bad News: Last Journalists in a Dictatorship, the book Sundaram went on to write about his time in Rwanda teaching journalists, he describes a more extreme version of this phenomenon, recalling how Kagame once commented that thatched roofs on huts were primitive. “And the local authorities took that as a sign that he didn’t like thatched roofs, and that they should get rid of them. And without replacements being built, people climbed up and dismantled their own thatched roofs. And I saw these villages with houses which just had mud walls without roofs, and the families were sitting outside with their children and their goats, the thatch strewn on the ground. In the rain, quite often. The children would get sick, and it was like a war zone.

“At the end of my time in Congo, I was at a UN base and they were digging latrines, when they found some human bones. They stopped digging and alerted the press, and I happened to be in Goma nearby.” He subsequently found out that it was one of a series of mass graves containing the bodies of Congolese killed by forces controlled by Kagame. “And so when I arrived I had a sense of what Rwanda had done in Congo, but I didn’t fully appreciate the extent to which it was totalitarian. I’d heard that the country was a shining example of progress – aid programs were successful, and poverty reduction programs. The streets were clean, public services functioned. I was living in a nice house with a big garden provided by the journalism programme I was working in.”

Many European governments, including Britain, are enamoured with Rwanda, because, says Sundaram, “dictatorships can be very efficient”. But it is a “mirage of a country”, he says.

The teaching programme he was running was briefed not to challenge the government on any level, and an embassy official told him that if any of the journalists mentioned repression they would be expelled.

“Layer by layer, as I began to talk to the journalists I was training, the true story unravelled. The first instance was when one of them left the programme, and I heard him on the radio one day praising the president, but with a degree of flattery that was completely exaggerated, and I didn’t understand why. The rest of the class were reluctant to talk about it but eventually I learned that another student had been beaten to a coma on the day he criticised the president.

“I started to realise that my class contained some of the most courageous journalists in the country.” As a foreigner, if he transgressed, Sundaram could have his visa cancelled or get kicked out, or even locked up for a couple of days, but for the Rwandan journalists, everything was at stake. They could be killed or their families threatened.

“But still they persisted, and they took me around the country and showed me all the things the government didn’t want anyone to see – things they couldn’t report on because it was too dangerous, so they wanted to show me because they wanted somebody to speak up. It’s really a book about them – they’ve been my greatest teachers in journalism.”

News.title: I tried Amazon’s new iPad rival – and there’s one standout feature
News.content:
Amazon says that this tablet has three times the computing power and nine times the graphics power of any previous Amazon tablet, so this is a significant boost in performance to previous models.

That will make light tasks, such as crunching through emails, browser-based activity like online shopping and document work. With a keyboard factored in, it could work as a laptop alternative for some. The same could be said of the iPad Air, although with recent price increases from Apple and the matte screen, for my money, this is a better proposition.

The premium makeover that comes with the Alexa Tablet Pro includes a slim aluminium design, with flattened edges, so it looks like an iPad or Samsung tablet, only 6.5mm thick. The Pro version only comes in the Graphite colour seen here. All models in the new line-up feel more grown-up and less like kid’s tablets than the Fire range. Plus the switch to proper Android over Fire OS is welcome and will result in better app compatibility (although I noticed that these tablets were running Android 16, which is now an old version).

It has a battery that’s good for 16 hours of video playback and supports 27W charging. There are cameras front and rear although like any tablet, these won’t be as good as your phone, while there’s support for Dolby Atmos from the speakers, so your movies will sound decent.

The AI capabilities are a step up

As the name suggests, Amazon is keen to promote the AI element here. It has customised the interface slightly with access to Alexa+ meaning you can utilise Amazon’s AI at any time to ask about what’s on the screen, to control smart home devices or search for content. If you are a keen Alexa user, then that will be a plus, but for me it’s not the headline news.

Sports.title: Celebrations that saw footballers sent off including star putting shorts on head and striker headbutting dugout
Sports.content:
Next

CELEBRATIONS have become a prevalent part of the modern game, with elaborate routines and signature moves now a regular fixture at matches.

But some players have allowed their joy to get the better of them over the years, and forced the referee to step in to keep it in check.



Though officials are giving increasingly long leashes to teams cheering on a goalscorer, Law 12 of the IFAB Laws of the Game still prohibits “excessive” celebrations, and the referee has the power to caution players for “gesturing or acting in a provocative, derisory or inflammatory way.”

While it is not common to see the Law invoked – beyond handing out bookings for taking a shirt off – the regulations have produced some incredibly bizarre instances of players receiving their marching orders after getting overzealous with their celebrations.



Neymar

Brazilian superstar Neymar is known for his performative flair, which was in full force when the then-19-year-old Santos star took on Colo-Colo in the Copa Libertadores.

In typical Neymar fashion, the winger picked up the ball on the edge of the box, flicked it over an opponents head and dinked the onrushing keeper, before heading towards the crowd and picking up a paper mask of his own face.

He proceeded to put the mask on (upside down) before celebrating with his team-mates – only to turn around and see the referee showing him a second yellow card.

The Laws of the Game specify a yellow card for anyone “covering the head or face with a mask or other similar item” while celebrating – a detail which a furious Neymar must have missed, but the official certainly did not.

Mario Gjurovski

Macedonian international Mario Gjurovski was the recipient of one of the silliest red cards the game has ever seen thanks to his bizarre celebration for Muangthong United.

The Belgrade-born forward, 40, neatly chipped the ball over the opposing keeper, before peeling off to the side of the pitch and pointing to the crowd.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

But he took things further when he made the bonkers decision to take off his shorts and place them on his head, before pretending to spray the crowd with mimed gunfire.

If the celebration wasn’t overly dignified, being shown a second yellow card as he tried not to trip over while putting his shorts back on was surely a wake-up call that some celebrations should never make it onto the pitch.

Riolo Terme forward

An attacker for amateur Italian club Riolo Terme took that idea a step too far, however, as his energetic celebrations after tapping home a scrappy winner led him off the pitch and into the technical areas.



The player had poked the ball over the line after the opposing keeper spilled a tame free-kick effort, and then took off down the sideline in jubilation.

It appeared as though he was going to celebrate with the substitutes and coaching staff, but when he reached the group he feinted past them and inexplicably headbutted the plastic siding of the dugout, smashing it to pieces and throwing almost his entire body through the hole he created.

Somehow he still appeared shocked when the referee showed him a straight red card as a result of the outburst, though the shocked expressions and awkward laughs of his team-mates following the incident suggested they were more clued in on what was about to happen.



Carlos Tevez

Premier League icon Carlos Tevez could not contain himself after scoring an 88th-minute strike for Boca Juniors to make it 2-1 on aggregate against fierce rivals River Plate in a 2004 Copa Libertadores semi-final.

The star immediately whipped his shirt off and ran towards the side of the pitch, where he then tucked his arms in and began to flap them as though mimicking a chicken – a derogatory term used to refer to River Plate.

The referee was not impressed with the display, and showed the star a straight red for unsportsmanlike conduct, while mimicking the dance in his face for good measure.



River Plate equalised on aggregate barely five minutes later, but Boca were able to get the tie over the line on penalties, before losing to Colombian side Once Caldas in the final.

Sports.title: Fifth tier side sold to £5.3BILLION US company days after they sacked Premier League icon as manager
Sports.content:

NATIONAL LEAGUE club Gateshead have agreed to a deal to be sold to an American private investment company worth more than £5.3billion.

The club sit bottom of the fifth tier having lost six in a row and sacking manager and former Premier League star Lee Cattermole last Sunday amid a failure to pay players and staff their September wages.



Gateshead looked to have hit rock-bottom after director Mark Nellist’s resignation and withdrawal of funding support.

However, in a dramatic twist the Tynesiders could be bankrolled into becoming an English football juggernaut after a Wrexham-style takeover offer was accepted.



On Friday the club announced they had agreed a sale in principle to US-based private investment firm, Flacks Group, subject to approval by the Independent Football Regulator.

The company, headed by 59-year-old, Manchester-born businessman and billionaire Michael Flacks who appeared in the 2026 Sunday Times Rich List ranked 98th in the UK, specialises in purchasing distressed companies and assets.

They are based in Florida but work in cities including Miami, New York, Tokyo and Paris, and billionaire Flacks alone is worth £1.681bn, having been founded by Flacks in 1983.

The deal will ensure Gateshead players and staff are paid their overdue wages following the delays last month.

Gateshead’s Stephen Paylor – who was announced as the club’s joint-owner in April but will now be a minority owner – said of the deal: ” I am thrilled to be able to announce an agreement in principle with the American based and globally active Flacks Group, who has a global asset value exceeding $7billion.”

Paylor confirmed wages would be paid immediately to bring an end to an “incredibly challenging period” and expressed his thanks to billionaire Flacks, Flacks Group spokesperson Phil Forster and the wider Flacks team for “acting quickly and in the best interests” of the club.

“Gateshead has a tremendous history and we look forward to moving the club forward and to see it realise its true potential.”

Gateshead will take on Halifax under interim and club legend Ben Clark, who managed the club through a similar crisis in 2019.

It has echoes of the deal that saw actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney takeover Wrexham in 2021 for £2million, albeit without the added Hollywood flair.

The Welsh club have risen through the leagues following the takeover and are eyeing a play-off spot in the Championship to achieve their dream of getting promoted into the Premier League.

MANCHESTER UNITED have not ruled out the possibility of surgery for Benjamin Sesko amid his problematic shin injury.

Sesko has been sidelined since he came off in the second half of United’s League Cup defeat to Brighton on September 16 and will miss the visit of Tottenham on Saturday.



The 23-year-old sat out Slovenia’s March internationals to rest his shin but aggravated it in the 3-2 win against Liverpool on May 3 and did not play again for three-and-a-half months.

Sesko is unlikely to be ready for the away games at Atletico Madrid and Leeds next week and United coach Michael Carrick revealed it is not the same problem that has plagued Sesko for six months.



“It’s not the exact issue, it’s a similar area,” Carrick clarified. “But it’s not the exact same thing again.

“And we’re kind of still working through it a little bit to see how long the issue will be.



“We’re hoping that it’ll be soon, obviously, but at this moment it’s still not quite clear.

When asked if Sesko could go under the knife, Carrick said: “Yeah, there are different things to look at.

“I think he recovered really well actually from the initial one, and there was a lot of time, and sometimes things get thrown up.

“The body does certain things and we’ve got to react to that and try and get him back as quick as we can.”

Carrick has urged his players to play with more “fire” against Spurs after their poor start.

United won one of their first five Premier League games and lost two before the three-week international break.

Winless Tottenham visit Old Trafford on Saturday ahead of a testing October that also includes trips to Como and Chelsea as well as Bournemouth at home.

United have been widely lambasted for their dismal running stats, with the club ranked bottom of the Prem for distance at high intensity, time at high intensity, sprints and time sprinting.



The 20-day gap between games and seismic news about Manchester City cooled the scrutiny on Carrick, yet he wants United to turn up the heat on the pitch.

“We understand where we want to get to, how we want to get there, and what it takes to get there, and what we’ve done previously to prove we can get good results,” Carrick said.

“We need to have a little bit of fire moving forward in terms of how we play, how we perform, what that means, and getting the best out of each other.

“So we need to keep pushing for more.



“It’s not ideal. It’s a long break. Probably too long really, from my perspective, and it feels like a long time.

“But then of course we’ve made the most of it. Regardless of results, I think when you’ve had a period like this, international breaks in general are normally a time where you can have a bit of a review and a bit of a plan of what’s next.

“This one’s been extra long, and it’s certainly given us an opportunity to, like I said before, some of the good things that we’re still doing, to not lose that, and certainly think we need to clean up on other things to help us get better results.”

Carlos Baleba is set to make his United debut, having played in the behind-closed-doors friendly win against Lausanne last week.



Baleba, 22, was United’s most expensive summer signing at £70million and the team have lacked a defensive midfielder to shield their porous back four.

United have conceded eight goals in their five league games, as well as three in the collapse against Brighton in the League Cup.

“He’s certainly getting closer, Carlos,” Carrick added. “It’s been great to have him out on the grass and to see him up close really, and played a little bit in a training game that we had last week, so that was good for him to get some minutes.

“I think the other side of it, a little bit, he has missed a lot, and he’s missed crucial time in terms of, you know, the end of pre-season, and there’s a little bit of patience there for him to get up to speed.



“That’s up to us to kind of pick that right time for him as well, but he offers us a lot. The midfield that we’ve got we’re really happy with, and the selections and the options that we have, and he definitely adds to that.”

Meanwhile Carrick has said it was not a certainty JJ Gabriel would have been picked in the squad against Brighton.

It emerged that Gabriel, who turned 16 this week, wanted to leave United the day before Brighton eliminated Carrick’s side in the third round of the League Cup.

Gabriel played for United under 19s in the Uefa Youth League against Sabbah on September 10 and the club had planned to name him on the bench against Brighton six days later.

But Carrick revealed that Gabriel was not present for the pre-Brighton preparation.



“I think that was after the City game (on September 13), which he hadn’t been around for those days, really,” Carrick said.

“So things can change, we always have plans for certain things and certain ideas for younger players whether they’re involved in squads or whether not involved in squads.

“But nothing was concrete at that stage anyway.”

United are considering legal action against whichever representative engineers a move for Gabriel, who has generated interest from Barcelona, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: De Zerbi urges Spurs flops to take inspiration from Kulusevski as he travels to Man Utd clash after 517 DAYS out injured
Sports.content:
Next

ROBERTO DE ZERBI has told his Tottenham flops to take inspiration from Dejan Kulusevski’s comeback story to spark their own.

Kulusevski, 26, will have gone 517 DAYS without a game when Spurs face Manchester United – after suffering a kneecap injury in May 2025.



But the winger is closing in on a long-awaited return and is travelling with the squad for Saturday’s trip to Old Trafford, though it is unclear if he will be on the bench or not.

Spurs are currently bottom of the table and boss De Zerbi told his squad in a team meeting to take heart from how Kulusevski has battled back from adversity.



The Italian said: “He’s an inspiration.

“He reacted very well, with character, with courage, with passion. Yes, passion. It’s a good word, passion.



“We have to take inspiration from Deki. I said the same in the meeting to the players.

“He is an example for everyone, Dejan Kulusevski.

“Forget the player, but the example of how he reacted to the injury, the reaction to being unlucky, the character he showed this time, was an example, a reference for everyone.”

Asked if he had ever managed a player who had been out for as long as Kulusevski, De Zerbi replied: “No. But me as a player, I suffered many times from long injuries.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Injuries are bad because you lose football but it’s nice because you come inside of yourself and you know yourself better than before the injury.

“If you react in the right way to the injury, like if you react well and in the right way to this situation of our club, the table, this season, last season, two seasons ago, I think you become better as a player for sure, you become stronger as a player and you become better as a man.”

Kulusevski sustained the injury in an innocuous challenge with Marc Guehi when Spurs hosted Crystal Palace 17 months ago.

It has been a long road since but Spurs will be buoyed by the Swede’s presence at Old Trafford.

Whether he is named among the substitutes remains to be seen, though, as Pedro Porro, who is definitely injured, will also be with the team for moral support.



Spurs have missed Kulusevski’s creativity as they prop up the league table following five games without a win.

It puts pressure on big-spending De Zerbi heading to United, who have their own problems after a poor start to the season.

But De Zerbi believes his team have the capacity to emulate what Aston Villa did last season after the Midlanders failed to win any of their own first five league games.

Unai Emery’s side then won 12 of their next 13 and went on to qualify for the Champions League, as well as winning the Europa League.

Asked if his struggling side could emulate that kind of turnaround, De Zerbi added: “Yes, it’s possible. Why not? But to do what Villa did, we have to click.



“Yes (the first win can be transformative), but I think the first win is not a gift from God. You have to deserve to win. And we didn’t deserve to win so far.

“I don’t believe in lucky, unlucky. I believe in, if you deserve or not, if you push or not, if you believe or not, if you are a group or not, if you have the right spirit or not, if you have passion or not, if you are ambitious or not, if you have a big motivation or not. Unlucky is nothing.”

Meanwhile, De Zerbi said he had to manage 18-year-old “special talent” Luca Williams-Barnett carefully going forward.

SunSport revealed on Wednesday that Spurs are in talks over extending the whizkid’s deal.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

De Zerbi added: “He’s very young, and the management of the very, very young players is very complicated.



“(He is a) special talent. Special personality also. Because he’s arrogant, but arrogant (in a way that is) good for football.”

Sports.title: Man City charges news: Triple punishment agreement as Premier League chiefs speak out
Sports.content:
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca faced the media for the first time since the club were found guilty as they prepare to take on Liverpool in the Premier League

Enzo Maresca has ‘complete trust’ in Man City and says achievements not tainted

Welcome to Mirror Football's live blog for Friday, October 9, as Manchester City prepare to return to Premier League action for the first time since being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.

The club have already confirmed their appeal after an Independent Commission found them guilty on 114 of 115 charges levied against them between 2009-10 and 2017-18. They revealed that more than £830million of owner funding was used to inflate revenues through 'sham' agreements.

In addition to City's appeal, there is now also a punishment to await. The range of sanctions can go from a fine to a points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League.

Enzo Maresca held his first press conference following the news as he previewed City's clash against Liverpool. The head coach presented a defiant response as he was probed on his and the club's position.

City are set for a frosty atmosphere at Anfield on Sunday, with the Reds being one of four clubs to have reserved the right for a legal challenge against their rivals.

Follow all of the updates below...

Sports.title: Man City 'held settlement talks with Premier League' BEFORE guilty verdict on charges
Sports.content:
Man City 'held settlement talks with Premier League' BEFORE guilty verdict on charges

Manchester City were in dialogue with the Premier League ahead of their guilty verdict on charges

View 2 Images Manchester City have appealed the guilty verdict from the independent commission (Image: (Photo by Loannis Alexopoulos/Anadolu via Getty Images))

Manchester City reportedly held settlement talks with the Premier League prior to the independent commission delivering their guilty verdict last month. City, still strongly deny any wrongdoing and have appealed the decision after they were found guilty of all but one of the alleged charges.

‌



‌



Now, in a report by Bloomberg, the Premier League side held talks with the top-flight's governing body to discuss an 'early-stage settlement' but those discussions broke down. The report claims that any punishment would have been a hefty financial payment, rather than the stripping of titles and relegation, according to those sourced.

‌



It's claimed those talks quickly fell apart with City adamant about their innocence in the matter. The sheer amount of charges means the reported financial proposal would have only reduced the size of the case, rather than resolved it.

‌



It's claimed that any settlement agreement would also have been strongly opposed by the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United who missed out on titles during City's relentless run of silverware. It's worth adding that agreeing to a settlement would also not have meant any acknowledgement of wrongdoing.

‌



Man City are facing the prospect of severe penalties after the independent commission ruled they had "clearly intended to circumvent Premier League rules" across a nine-season spell.

City were found to have participated in an almost £1billion scheme designed to either artificially boost revenues or cut costs through a string of "sham" arrangements in a bid to sidestep league and UEFA financial regulations.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters branded the case, and the ruling, as "the most significant in Premier League history", with the league's probe having begun back in 2018.

‌



Over 100 charges were brought against City in February 2023, with the commission examining the case between September and December 2024.

View 2 Images Richard Masters has spoken out on the charges that Man City face (Image: Getty Images)

The same commission which has delivered its verdict will now determine what sanctions ought to be handed down, while the club swiftly confirmed their plans to appeal, claiming the decision "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe".

‌



City chief executive Ferran Soriano told staff on a video that the commission had bought into the Premier League's "conspiracy theory".

The club were found by the commission to have run a "disguised funding scheme" in which companies from Abu Dhabi paid a fraction of the amount recorded on the club's accounts, with the remainder settled by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), the company through which Sheikh Mansour controls the club.

The scheme was found to have artificially inflated revenue by more than £830m across the nine-season spell between 2009-10 and 2017-18. The club were also found to have exaggerated income from image rights by almost £74m, while understating liabilities for staff contracts by almost £17m.

‌



City lodged an appeal and in a statement said: "Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

"The Club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe. The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

"We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta makes Arsenal vow after signing new contract - 'We need to stay on top'
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta makes Arsenal vow after signing new contract - 'We need to stay on top'

Mikel Arteta has underlined his commitment to Arsenal by signing a new three-year deal with the Gunners and he is keen to add to the silverware that he has already won at the Emirates

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has penned a new deal with Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta insists he will get even better as a manager - and can lead Arsenal to a sustained period of success. Gunners boss Arteta, 44, has signed a new three-year deal which will take him to 2030 and mean he will be in charge for more than a decade.

‌



‌



Arteta has already delivered Arsenal’s first Premier League title in 22 years and he reached the Champions League final last season. But Arteta says he is more determined than ever to lead Arsenal to a dynasty of success and he also says he will get better as a manager himself.

‌



Arteta said: “We know what the level is right now, we know where the standards land, we know what the expectations are. But the good thing is the level of enthusiasm, passion and energy is even higher, and that's what we want to accomplish all together, and that's the opportunity ahead of us.

‌



“This is how we have to live this job. And as I said, I think what you have to do is enjoy the journey. I think it's the most important thing and probably the biggest lesson that I've had over the last seven years.

‌



“The biggest gift that I've had throughout this period has been the people that are around me, that have been around me to make me feel loved and allow me to enjoy what I do."

When asked whether he is also improving and if there is more to come, Arteta said: “A lot. I know that because that’s generally what I want to do but I know that the people around me are going to help me evolve as well.

“Starting from the ownership to everyone that I have around me because we have created people with a drive who constantly think about how we get better and make sure we maintain because we need to stay on top as well.”

‌



Arsenal face Leeds on Saturday looking to bounce back from their defeat at Brighton and also bring back players who got injured on international duty.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta helped to end Arsenal's long wait for a Premier League crown (Image: Getty Images)

Christos Tzolis is definitely out, Kai Havertz is a major doubt and looks set to miss out while Ezri Konsa is likely to be fit. Max Dowman is fit after a knock on England under-19s duty.

‌



Arteta said they will be driven by a determination to bounce back but stressed in-form Leeds carry a major threat. He added: “The pain is still in the tummy and tomorrow we certainly have to play with that because it was a lesson for us. It was a lot to learn from that game, especially when you don't hit certain basics in a football match, especially against a really good Brighton side.

“You become almost not recognisable and it can happen. But it's been more about learning from who we are and how thin the line is from being exceptional to becoming very average, and that's a reality.

“But as well, just realising with the difficult context that we had with all the internationals that we had, what we've done in the first 18 weeks, I think it's been remarkable. But, a big attention, because things change very quickly.”

Sports.title: Man City whistleblower Rui Pinto goes BACK into witness protection after 'fearing for his life'
Sports.content:
Man City whistleblower Rui Pinto goes BACK into witness protection after 'fearing for his life'

Riu Pinto was key in the process of levelling Premier League charges at Manchester City and he had previously appealed for help from the public in ensuring his safety

View 2 Images Rui Pinto has seen his protection restored by Portuguese authorities (Image: Getty Images)

Rui Pinto has had his protection restored by the Portuguese authorities in a rapid U-turn. Pinto’s Football Leaks website was key in Manchester City having 115 Premier League charges levelled against them.

‌



‌



City have since been found guilty of 114 of those, with a number of potential punishments on the table should their appeal be dismissed.

‌



Pinto in the meantime has also been left uncomfortable, having seen his witness protection revoked by the Portuguese authorities. He had previously received protection since 2020.

‌



But the 37-year-old whistleblower has now had that restored for the time being, with a statement signed from the Ministry of Justice stating that Pinto had not been adequately informed of the grounds for terminating the programme or given the opportunity to exercise his right to challenge the decision.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He now has 10 working days to review the original withdrawal. Taking to social media in the aftermath, he said: “I express my appreciation for the action taken by Portugal's Minister of Justice, Rita Alarcão Júdice, who restored legality by overturning a decision made by the members of the Commission responsible for Portugal's Witness Protection Programme, who acted in clear violation of the law and in a manifest abuse of power.

“This is a particularly serious situation, all the more so because, given their roles, the members of this Commission have an increased responsibility to uphold the rule of law and safeguard the rights, liberties and guarantees of citizens who, due to the specific nature of the Programme, find themselves in a particularly vulnerable and uncertain situation.

“Despite this restoration of legality, the way in which the members of the Commission have acted prevents me from placing any trust in them or feeling confident in their work. Such conduct is clearly contrary to the principles that should guide a witness protection programme, whose credibility and effectiveness depend, above all, on respect for the law, impartiality and the trust of those who rely on it.

‌



View 2 Images Rui Pinto's Football Leaks website was key in Man City being charged (Image: Getty Images)

“I would like to conclude by expressing my special gratitude to everyone who has shown their support and contributed to the fundraising campaign. To all of you, my sincere thanks for continuing to stand by me in this cause which, despite today's decision, is still far from being resolved.”

Pinto had previously appealed to the general public by attempting to raise €2.5m (£2.1m). He said: “Given these circumstances, I have no alternative but to relocate, within the next few days, to an undisclosed location for an indefinite period of time, due to the multiple death threats I have received and the serious risk of an assassination attempt against me.”

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher takes ANOTHER swipe at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo behaviour
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher takes ANOTHER swipe at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo behaviour

Cristiano Ronaldo has once again been in the headlines this week with his statement after walking out on the Portuguese national team following a row with boss Jorge Jesus

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has hit out at Rio Ferdinand (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has slammed Rio Ferdinand for ‘embarrassing’ himself with his defence of Cristiano Ronaldo. The veteran forward has been at the centre of a storm this week after walking out on the Portuguese national team camp following a row with Jorge Jesus.

‌



‌



His former Manchester United teammate Rio Ferdinand has been one of his biggest defenders during the ongoing argument. And in assessing the situation, Carragher has hit out at Ferdinand for his behaviour.

‌



Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender said: “People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem.

‌



“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

‌



It is not the first time that Carragher has slammed Ferdinand, with the pair having been drawn into a bitter social media spat back in May this year ahead of a clash between Liverpool and Manchester United.

Carragher’s colleague Gary Neville has also given his take on Ronaldo’s situation and suggested that his lengthy statement might actually have made things worse - albeit believes Ronaldo could yet get supporters back onside.

He said: “My view was that I would never criticise Ole Gunnar Solskjær because he conducted himself with great class, whether he was winning or losing. With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He [Ronaldo] has to be pulled up on that and told [that it isn’t acceptable].

‌



View 2 Images Ronaldo is now back in action for Al-Nassr after walking out on the Portugal national team (Image: Getty Images)

“The problem is, who is going to tell him? He isn’t going to listen to me or you [Jamie Carragher], but I can’t approve of that statement or pretend it was a good thing to do. If you love Ronaldo, it makes him more difficult to like; if you don’t like him, it makes you dislike him even more.

“I don’t think it’s irretrievable. In another year, when he has retired, we will look back at his greatness and his football, and people might not remember this ending.

Article continues below

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable. You think you can dictate to a federation or a manager what they should say. I’m glad the manager stood his ground. If he had read those eight points out [in Ronaldo’s social media statement], he [Ronaldo] would have lost a lot of his soul.”

Sports.title: Premier League executives name one Man City punishment they're 'not expecting'
Sports.content:
Premier League executives name one Man City punishment they're 'not expecting'

There is a lot of talk over potential punishments for Man City after they were found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules

View 2 Images City are appealing against the guilty verdict on 114 breaches of financial rules. (Image: Molly Darlington - WSL/WSL Football via Getty Images)

Premier League club chiefs are not expecting Manchester City to be directly thrown out of the league if the guilty verdict against breaches of financial rules is upheld. City are appealing the verdict, which rules them as guilty of 114 breaches over a nine-year period.

‌



‌



The three-person panel ruled that City artificially inflated their revenue through ‘sham’ sponsorship deals that were funded by the club owners, something that is now allowed under the financial regulations. It’s something that City strongly deny.

‌



There has been a lot of talk over what sort of punishment could be handed to City should their appeal against the verdict be unsuccessful. The sanction will be decided by the same three-person panel that delivered the initial verdict, with the Premier League able to give their recommendation.

‌



The Premier League handbook states that punishments can range from fines to points deductions and even expulsion from the league. But latest reports suggest that the latter is not expected.

Liverpool dealt double injury blow ahead of Man City clash as Andoni Iraola offers update READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The Athletic reports that several executives from Premier League clubs are not expecting the sanction to be direct expulsion, due to relying on the backing of clubs. For City to be thrown out of the Premier League, 14 of the clubs would have to vote in favour of the sanction.

‌



That would not be the case with other punishments, including fines or points deductions. Another option for the commission could be to recommend a deduction that would effectively guarantee relegation from the division and into the Championship, rather than kicking City out directly.

There is, however, a fear that a huge points deduction would undermine the league’s competitive integrity and reduce the television product on offer. It could leave City effectively playing games that won’t have an impact on their future, as they could already be relegated via the deduction.

View 2 Images Man City boss Enzo Maresca. (Image: Tom Flathers/Manchester City FC via Getty Images)

‌



There is also a worry in the Championship that a relegation for City would allow them to spend just one season outside of the Premier League before earning promotion back. That would therefore take up one of the promotion spots on offer to other clubs competing for a place in the top division.

Speaking about the possibility of managing City in the Championship, or League one, Enzo Maresca said: “I won the Championship with Leicester.

"So in case of League One, we’re going to see. We are thinking about something that we don’t know.”

Article continues below

There are some arguments from a Premier League club executive that City should receive a punishment that would see them handed points deductions over multiple seasons. That would therefore hamper the club’s chances of qualifying for European competitions over a few seasons, with financial implications.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta leaves more questions than answers with deafening Man City silence
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta leaves more questions than answers with deafening Man City silence

Football cannot afford to duck the biggest issue in the game right now as Manchester City lodge an appeal against their guilty verdict on 114 charges

View 2 Images Arteta batted away any questions on Man City during his press conference (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Sadly, we were left with more questions than answers.

‌



‌



Mikel Arteta is Arsenal manager but, having worked at Manchester City under Pep Guardiola, was always bound to be under the microscope.

‌



City have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s spending rules from 2009 to 2018 which covers two of the three-and-a-half years that Arteta was at the Etihad.

‌



Arteta is now manager of City’s biggest rivals and therefore it is totally unrealistic to expect not to be asked about the 115 case.

In fairness to Arteta, he gave some answers but largely avoided questions and tried desperately hard to steer clear of controversy because he said it was an “ongoing process.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Well, it is to a point. But the fact is that City have been found guilty and are now appealing the verdict. And that, in the real world, means you can have a say and an opinion.

Arteta ventured that the Premier League is still the best in the world. Well, right now, a lot of fans will be wondering whether we can say that any more.

‌



Certainly, on the back of a few managers - Michael Carrick, Oliver Glasner and Regis Le Bris to name but three Premier League bosses - they have got a lot of questions and criticisms.

Carrick said football and indeed sport is all about the glory in the moment. "In football, the strive to win, the emotion and the feeling about winning, a lot of it is in the moment.

”You can't take that back. It's the moment you strive for. That's essentially what we're all in it for. That's the feeling we all crave.

‌



View 2 Images Arteta was Pep Guardiola's assistant for three and a half years at Manchester City (Image: Getty)

"The beauty of trying to win trophies is a little bit the journey towards it and then the finale. Does it go for you, does it go against you? Once that's done, there's no getting that back in any direction.

"I'm not getting blasé about it, but regardless of anything, in any sport in history, if later on you get the medal, it doesn't bring the feeling of when you initially win or you don't."

‌



Glasner and Le Bris were very strong on the appeal needing to be concluded within the season otherwise the uncertainty will linger.

Some managers would not take questions. So, again, fair play to Arteta for answering any. But it is not enough to dodge the issue.

We have to be realistic on this and say it will damage the reputation and integrity of the Premier League.

‌



Michael Carrick takes Man City charges 'personally' as Man Utd boss makes appeal demand READ MORE :

Erling Haaland injury update given by Enzo Maresca before Man City's trip to Liverpool READ MORE :

Can you possibly imagine if City invoke a siege mentality, grow stronger and win a title in a season in which they have been found guilty of widespread Premier League charges.

That is the biggest danger for the English top flight. The punishment could be dished out while City are still going through the courts.

That is why we need strong voices and hiding behind the “process” will not dampen the anger and frustration from fans who will be wondering whether they can believe what they are seeing any more.

Article continues below

And it is why managers have to accept that is part of their responsibility to tune in and understand fans in this case. That is why it is deeply frustrating when managers and anyone in the game duck the issue.

Smith is chasing down the final spots in the European Championship race and the St Helens thrower beat Owen 6-4 to set up a meeting with Jermaine Wattimena for a place in Sunday's action.

Rob Cross was Friday's standout performer for the second event in a row, averaging 105.95 in his 6-3 success against Mario Vandenbogaerde and will take on Luke Woodhouse on the back of his brilliant opening round performance at the World Grand Prix.

Bradley Brooks also produced an excellent display of darting brilliance in his opening round contest against Niels Zonneveld, as the former World Youth Champion averaged over a ton in a 6-4 victory over the World Grand Prix quarter-finalist, in a game that saw both players average over a ton and hit 13 maximums between them.

Brooks has now won four out of a possible four round-one games in European Tour events this year, and will take on Chris Dobey for a place in the final day of action at St Jakobshalle.

Karel Sedlacek's hopes of sealing a spot at the European Championship continue into Saturday's action as he swept aside Sebastian Bialecki to stay alive in the race for place in Dortmund later this month.

The Czech star averaged upwards of a ton and came back from 4-3 down to defeat the Pole 6-4, which included a brilliant 86 checkout on the bull to break the throw for the first time in the contest.

Image: Stefan Bellmont defeated Andrew Gilding to send the Swiss crowd wild in Basel

Stefan Bellmont produced a brilliant display on home soil in Basel as he created history by becoming the third Swiss player to win a match at the tournament, as he beat Andrew Gilding 6-3.

The 37-year-old, who featured in his tenth European Tour event in his career, pinned five legs on the spin to defeat the former UK Open champion, and has his eyes set on a place in Saturday's action.

"Playing in front of your home crowd is very special and I wanted to win so much." Bellmont reflected, who managed to win only his third match on the European Tour and will face Krzysztof Ratajski in round two.

"There were quite a few nerves in the early stages of the match, but thankfully I was able to raise my game.

"I know I will have to play better tomorrow but for now I just want to enjoy this amazing moment."

Maik Kuivenhoven ended a losing streak of almost five years in Basel, as the Dutchman beat compatriot Raymond van Barneveld 6-3 to deny van Barneveld his first European Tour victory of the year.

Dave Chisnall and Tom Bissell both secured last-leg victories in their opening round contests against Alan Soutar and Joe Cullen respectively.

Cristo Reyes' first win on the European Tour since May came in style, as the Spaniard beat Scotsman Cameron Menzies with an average of 98 and will face Ryan Searle next.

The Swiss Darts Trophy continues with a bumper double session on Saturday, as the 16 seeded representatives enter the fray on Day Two in Basel.

Sports.title: Arteta says conscience clear over time at Man City
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has said he has a clear conscience over his former club Manchester City's serious breaches of financial rules.

An independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, City artificially inflated their revenue by £830m. The club have lodged an appeal and deny all wrongdoing.

The investigation covered two years in which Arteta was working as assistant to manager Pep Guardiola but, in an otherwise guarded press conference, the Arsenal boss answered "yes" when asked if he had a clear conscience.

Arteta, who this week signed a new four-year contract as Arsenal manager, faced a string of questions over the City verdict by journalists but repeatedly insisted he would not comment further until the outcome of City's appeal is known.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How Arteta and other managers reacted to questions about the Man City case

"The thing is that this has been going for various years," he said.

"The process is still not finished, so it's very difficult to express how I feel because it's not resolved. When it's resolved, I can talk with clarity and tell you exactly how I feel.

"I think that process has to be resolved in a way. And we need to trust that the people who are in charge doing that will do it in the timeframe that they believe is best for everybody."

Arteta spent three-and-a-half seasons working with Guardiola, including the 2016/17 and 2017/18 campaigns, when City won back-to-back Premier League titles, an FA Cup and two League Cups, before leaving the club to take charge of Arsenal in 2019.

Image: Arteta worked with Pep Guardiola at Man City

According to the independent commission, City artificially inflated their sponsorship income by £264.3m across the 2016/17 and 2017/18 seasons, a period during which their signings included John Stones, Aymeric Laporte, Bernardo Silva, Ederson and Kyle Walker.

Arteta refused to comment when asked if his memories of working at City had been tainted.

When asked whether he was pleased to have won the Premier League title for Arsenal before the verdict, he said: "I feel proud and very emotional when I think about how we won it, the moments that we had together. It's a unique and genuine feeling that I have."

Arteta: Premier League still best in the world

Arteta insisted the Premier League will "100 per cent" continue to be the best league in the world despite questions of integrity being thrown up by the City verdict.

"It's the best league in the world for many reasons," he added.

"I've been here for over 20 years and it will continue to be the best league in the world. I feel privileged to be where I am.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Premier League managers including Frank Lampard, Marco Rose and Daniel Farke have their say

"And there are a few clubs who have been extremely good and managed resources in an intelligent way. And we suffered from that a few weeks ago [with their defeat to Brighton]."

However, following comments by Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner, who said the Premier League has been "damaged" by City being found guilty, Arteta admitted he was unsure about the impact on the competition's reputation globally.

"I want to think that it doesn't [damage the Premier League] but I don't know," he said. "And certainly it's not in our control.

"In our control is to bring everything we can individually to the club, to maintain the position we have to be the best league in the world."

Sports.title: Wainwright opens Leicester account with Gloucester win in front of Prince Harry
Sports.content:
Wales back-rower Aaron Wainwright scored his first try for Leicester Tigers as they defeated Gloucester 38-31 in a forward-dominated contest in the Gallagher Prem watched by The Duke of Sussex, Prince Harry.

The hosts found themselves 14-0 down after just 10 minutes at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, but a sustained period of dominance led to them scoring 31 unanswered points that put them well on the way to their second straight win.

For the Cherry and Whites, this was a first league loss of the season as they fell short in a match that saw eight of the nine tries scored by forwards.

Image: Prince Harry (centre) was spotted in the stands

Prince Harry, who had a beer in his hand, is a keen rugby fan and was in attendance with Andrea Pinchen, the Tigers chief executive.

Harry returned to the UK with Meghan and their children in August after six years away in the US.

It was Leicester who quickly found themselves under pressure when they had fly-half Billy Searle sin-binned just three minutes in for deliberately knocking Ben Loader's pass forward inside his own 22.

The Cherry and Whites quickly made the most of their one-man advantage when Wales flanker Jac Morgan squeezed his way through after a succession of pick-and-goes from his fellow forwards.

Try number two for the visitors soon followed when a driving maul powered its way over, with loosehead Dian Bleuler grounding the ball. Caolan Englefield converted both early scores stylishly from out wide.

Shortly after Searle returned to the field, Leicester were on the board when Finn Carnduff managed to force himself over the whitewash from close quarters.

The Tigers began to dominate territorially and found themselves level after half an hour when England tighthead Joe Heyes blasted through from a couple of metres and Searle added the extras.

The turnaround was then completed in the 36th minute when Jamie Blamire scored off the back of a driving maul to give Leicester a 21-14 half-time lead.

Sports.title: Bowen's late penalty saved as West Ham held by QPR
Sports.content:
Jarrod Bowen saw his 91st-minute penalty saved as West Ham missed the chance to move top of the Sky Bet Championship after a 1-1 draw with QPR.

Nicolas Madsen put Rangers 1-0 up, rolling home a penalty awarded in highly controversial circumstances.

But the Hammers came alive as the conclusion approached, with Bowen slamming in his seventh goal of the season to equalise after his first shot was blocked.

In the 90th minute, Amadou Mbengue tugged the shirt of Pablo in the penalty area and Bowen had the chance to win it from the spot.

But Pierce Charles dived low to his left to keep out the initial effort, then reacted in a flash to tip Arne Engels' follow-up over the bar.

How a dramatic evening unfolded in East London

Nuno Espirito Santo's side thumped Wrexham 6-0 in their last home game, but found themselves nowhere near that level in the first half. The display was sedate - they had two shots, with a total xG value of 0.07 - and they found themselves behind after only 18 minutes.

Tomas Soucek - making his first appearance of the season after recovering from an ankle injury sustained at the World Cup - slid in on Paul Smyth as the QPR livewire looked to break into the box.

The Czech midfielder got the ball - but referee Ruebyn Ricardo saw otherwise and pointed to the spot. Soucek's reaction was one of sheer disbelief.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tomas Soucek was left in shock after he gave away a penalty

"That's definitely not a penalty. No way on Earth. This is an absolute howler," said Lee Hendrie on co-commentary.

Speaking at half-time, studio guest Rob Green added: "The referee didn't let the situation breathe. He didn't give himself a moment to think: 'hold on a minute, what's actually happened here?'

"He just saw the ball move, the player move, the player fall over and gave the penalty."

Madsen coolly tucked away the penalty - and until the 70th minute that was all that separated the sides.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jarrod Bowen brought West Ham level

But West Ham came alive and were level when Bowen darted away from substitute Tariq Lamptey, hit one shot that was blocked, then made no mistake with the second.

The captain was denied another by a sharp Charles save, but with 90 minutes on the clock, Mbengue's overzealous tug was spotted by the officials and Bowen had the chance to be the hero once again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pierce Charles was the QPR hero as he saved a last-minute penalty and the rebound

Instead it was Charles who took the plaudits with two brilliant quickfire saves to preserve the point that sees QPR climb to fifth.

Soucek: Ref has admitted he was wrong - but he didn't speak to me on the pitch

West Ham's Tomas Soucek speaking to Sky Sports:

"I was so happy I won the challenge and recovered the ball!

"Straight away, I didn't know what the referee was doing and, from my perspective, it's a massive, massive mistake.

"We are just disappointed because, when I saw it inside, it looks even worse. I can't change it, but I cannot accept it.

"After the game, he told me he was wrong, but during the game, he just didn't want to speak with me any more.

"I was disappointed he didn't even want to speak with me so he could explain to me what he saw.

"I am disappointed because it had a big impact on me, but even more on the team. It was tough to take, but at least we got a point."

Nuno: We have the quality to do much better

West Ham's Nuno Espirito Santo speaking to Sky Sports:

"We could have won in the end, but we didn't start the game well. Once again, we were not precise in our passing, the game didn't flow. The first half was not good.

"We were able to react from a goal down and we had chances to win the game until the end.

"We always know, after an international break, there's a question mark over the players, also the players that have been involved in national teams. It was maybe an explanation, but we expect much more. We have enough quality to do much better."

On the controversial penalty award: "Unfortunately, it's not a good decision. The ref didn't get it right in that moment. The images are clear. There's not much more to say about that."

Sports.title: White: Fury-AJ will be most lucrative gate in British boxing history
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua will generate the most lucrative gate in British boxing history, Dana White tells Sky Sports.

Tickets for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua's December 11 showdown at the Principality stadium in Cardiff went on sale on Friday, with the most expensive regular seats going for £13,128.

The Principality Stadium can hold more than 70,000 spectators and White revealed on Friday evening: "I think there's less than 700 tickets left. You can consider this thing a sellout already."

More than half a million people joined the Ticketmaster queue to snap up tickets for the long-awaited heavyweight bout on December 11, with thousands being sold within an hour of the launch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Johnny Nelson takes a look back at the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference and expects things to heat up as the fight gets nearer

"There were over 500,000 people in the queue. Incredible. But for our generation, two of the biggest, most famous heavyweights in boxing. And not even arguable it's the biggest UK fight ever between two British heavyweights," White told Sky Sports.

Before the sale commenced, Ticketmaster confirmed regular seats would cost between £88.50 and £13,128.

Those figures did not include VIP packages, hotel and travel packages, group or concession prices.

White anticipates the fight will draw the most lucrative gate in the history of British boxing. "Definitely. It will. I don't want to mis-speak here but we have this thing scaled for around $34 million," he said.

"The UK is the right place for this fight to happen but it will have done well anywhere."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Hearn says he was pleased with the 'respect' shown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua at their press conference

The most expensive tickets exceed face-value figures for some of the world's biggest sporting events, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, where some seats were listed for £8,333.

In 2015 Floyd Mayweather's bout against Manny Pacquiao sold out within a minute, with top-priced face-value seats costing fans £4,982.

Fury last fought in London in April against Arslanbek Makhmudov, where ringside seats at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium were priced at £3,000.

Comparatively, ringside tickets for his bout against Dillian Whyte at Wembley in 2022, were priced at £2,250.

The cheapest seats on the pitch for Fury vs Joshua were listed at £345, while others ranged from £700 to £900.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Joshua makes his predictions for his fight against Tyson Fury on December 11

Some of the lowest-priced tickets in the stadium's upper terrace were on sale for £205.20. Ringside seats were also being sold on StubHub for more than £8,000.

Ringwalks are expected to commence at around 1am local time to cater for an international audience.

No rematch clause has been included in the contract for the fight, but that does not mean a second bout cannot be negotiated.

When the December 11 fight was made it was announced that Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and American combat sports promoter Dana White were staging the contest. However Eddie Hearn, who promotes Joshua, has publicly claimed the American cannot be involved.

White, renowned for creating the UFC, said of his role in this event: "Helped them with the gate, putting everything together. We're going to do all the production, produce the show and do what I do every Saturday."
