Sports.title: Tottenham happy to be called name again after previous request to the media
Sports.content:
Tottenham happy to be called name again after previous request to the media

Tottenham have backtracked on their omission of 'Tottenham' from club branding - two years after requesting alternative names.

The north London club launched a new 'brand identity' in November 2024 that featured changes to their logo and signature font.



2 Spurs look as though they are heading back to being simply named as 'Tottenham' despite a past media request Credit: Getty

It was later revealed that they wrote to broadcasters asking for them to be referred to as either 'Tottenham Hotspur' or 'Spurs'.

'Tottenham' was seemingly brushed aside but, as per The Athletic, it could be on its way back.

Fans attending home matches are said to have seen signs that read 'This is Tottenham' upon arrival.



They also launched a short film during the summer called 'Tottenham 'Til I Die', with 'Hotspur' being dropped once again.

At the time of writing, the Premier League still call them 'Tottenham Hotspur' on their website, although this could change soon.



What did Tottenham want to be called?

The reintegration of 'Tottenham' comes after the new brand identity included a club request for what they wanted to be named as.

"When referring to the team or the brand, please use 'Tottenham Hotspur', 'Tottenham Hotspur Football Club' or 'THFC'," said a 'Brand Playbook'.



It addd: "Never refer to our Club as 'Tottenham', 'Tottenham Hotspur FC' or 'TH'."

Founded in 1882, they were originally named 'Hotspur Football Club' and based in Northumberland Park, which is in north Tottenham.

'Tottenham Hotspur Football Club' became their official name two years later.

2 'Tottenham Hotspur' was the preferred name used by the club, although it looks as though it will be toned down Credit: Getty



Spurs are back!

After the three-week international break, Spurs return to Premier League action this weekend.

They travel to Manchester United on Saturday evening in search of their first win of the season.

Spurs lost 3-0 at Brentford on the opening weekend before falling to a 2-0 home defeat against Newcastle United.

Back-to-back 0-0 draws with Nottingham Forest and Everton were then followed by a 3-2 loss to Aston Villa.



The results mean they sit bottom of the Premier League table with two points gained from a possible 15.

As things stand, Spurs could be battling against relegation to the Championship yet again.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes unwittingly giving goalkeepers penalty advantage unlike Harry Kane, says ex-Premier League star
Sports.content:
Former Premier League star Mark Crossley admits he would prefer to face a stutter penalty run-up as it gives goalkeepers an advantage.

The stutter is one of the most polarising things in modern football - like it or loathe it, it seems here to stay.

3 Mbappe missed a penalty against Morocco at the World Cup with a stutter run-up Credit: Getty

Some of the world’s best players use it to try and get a supposed advantage over goalkeepers.

Stuttering during a penalty run-up can give takers a boost of as much as 10 per cent compared to traditional methods.

That’s according to an analysis of five years' worth of Premier League penalties undertaken by leading football psychology professor Geir Jordet.

However, the World Cup bucked the trend. Just nine of the 19 spot kicks where a player used a stutter run-up were converted.

That’s compared to 71 per cent of the penalties without it.

The likes of Bruno Fernandes and Kylian Mbappe are well versed in the technique, compared the the likes of Harry Kane, who prefers a more direct approach.

Nottingham Forest legend Crossley, who famously was the only person to save a spot kick from Matt Le Tissier, believes the stutter gives goalkeeper an advantage.

When asked which he would prefer to face, he told talkSPORT: “I'd prefer not to face Harry Kane. I'd prefer to face the stutter because I think it gives the goalkeeper a better chance, personally.

“Going back in the day, I think from what I learned, Stuart Pearce used to take penalties against me every day in training. He used to tell me about five where he was going to put them and then five where he wasn't. That was his technique.

“Then he used to ask me questions. What do you prefer? What don't you prefer? So that's the way we used to discuss penalty taking.

3 Crossley saved a penalty from Gary Lineker in the 1991 FA Cup final Credit: Getty

“But in the modern-day game, when I'm watching it, and people are running up and stuttering to the ball, I believe that it gives the goalkeeper a better advantage.

“The more that the goalkeeper can delay the striker, that was the only tactic that I ever used, really, was trying to delay the taker as long as possible.

“Because the best penalty takers, in my opinion, like Harry Kane, if he puts the ball down, he steps back; I think a couple of times he's done the stutter he's missed a couple when he's done the stutter.

“But when he runs up to it and smashes it, it gives the keeper much less chance.”

Crossley wanted to coach strikers

Following retirement, Crossley went into coaching and had various spells at Chesterfield, including as interim manager.

The 57-year-old thinks a huge advantage could be gained from a goalkeeper passing on their wisdom to strikers.

3 Crossley made more than 500 appearances in his career Credit: Getty

He continued: “As soon as I knew my career was coming to an end playing, I kind of thought, I want to give it a go as a manager, having worked for some of the best.

“So I did all my coaching badges. But my thoughts were, I want to coach strikers. I want to coach the strikers that are not just goalkeepers because I believe strikers need to know what goalkeepers don't like.

“I think it can give them a massive advantage. For instance, I don't know, a thing at the moment I've been thinking about is, say, a penalty. Does the striker taking the penalty against the goalkeeper know which side the goalkeeper is strongest on? Has he done the research? Do they know that? Are they getting told that? Because every goalkeeper technically is better diving to one side than the other. Do they know that information?

“So I think coaching outfield players as a goalkeeper is something that passed me by. I mean I won't be voting in coaching anymore, but it's something that I can try to explain that I think is very important.”

Overlap Daily will air weekdays at 4pm from Friday 9 October.

Catch Mark Crossley alongside Duncan Ferguson every Thursday with episodes available on YouTube, Global Player and wherever you get your podcasts.

Sports.title: Man City winning Premier League title this season would be biggest shambles in history
Sports.content:
Manchester City lifting a ninth Premier League crown this season would be a nightmare scenario for the division.

That's the view of ex-Chelsea star Scott Minto as clubs and fans patiently wait for the outcome of City's appeal against their guilty verdict on all charges of financial breaches by an independent commission.



3 City are currently under a cloud of a guilty verdict relating to various financial rule breaches in the Premier League Credit: AFP

City face serious sanctions such as points deductions, relegation and stripped titles for numerous rule breaks, including inflating revenue by over £900million - a span lasting from 2009 to 2018.

The appeal process must take place within 12 weeks of when it was lodged, and a decision is due within 30 days of its conclusion.

Manager Enzo Maresca has insisted that he is 'very calm' about the situation and, speaking to the media on Friday, reiterated his trust in the club, who maintain the position they are innocent.



Premier League clubs have written to chief executive Richard Masters to stress that the City case is resolved this season.

talkSPORT's Manchester correspondent Micky Gray echoed this after attending Maresca's press conference, saying: "Somewhere down the line, these charges are going to come to Manchester City - whether it's this season as it's ongoing, or at the end of the season.



"But I think everybody now, really, wants an outcome of what the situation is going to be at Manchester City Football Club."

What has been said about Man City?

Former Premier League defender Minto was then asked about what would happen if City won this season's title, with the club already at the top of the table with five wins from five.



"I think it could be one of the biggest shambles in Premier League history, if they're then found to be guilty," he warned.

"But if you are Manchester City, that's the aim, isn't it?

"To kick the can down the road, to keep on asking the Premier League, to then go back to the clubs, to keep on spending the legal battles with it.

3 City have a 100 per cent record in the top-flight so far this season, and Minto has expressed worry for the league if they win the title Credit: AFP

"Do they take it to the High Court? Do the High Court accept it?

"How long will that take, even if they don't? And therefore it could go beyond this season, for sure."



talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook then weighed in on the debate, and talked about the impact it could have on the rest of British football.

"I think the Premier League will be desperate for that not to happen," he explained.

"Because, as much as they want Manchester City punished, I don't think they want to be in a situation come May where they're having to take the ribbons off the trophy and take that Premier League title away from the champions.

"So, I think probably everybody in the Premier League boardroom is hoping for a different outcome.



3 Rival clubs want the result of City's appeal and any subsequent sanctions to be revealed before the end of this season Credit: Getty

"I have spoken to various people closely connected to various clubs this week, and one person put it to me that, if Manchester City win this appeal, then the Premier League is broken beyond repair.

"Is that too extreme?"

City face tough Premier League return

News of City's guilty verdict was delivered in the first week of the international break, so they have had plenty of time to dwell on it.

And they are set to face a hostile reception on their first game back on Sunday when they take on Liverpool.



Anfield is regarded as one of the best stadiums in the world for atmosphere, so Reds supporters are set to make their voices known this weekend.

City and Liverpool have also battled in heated title races, but this match could be the most fierce of all.

Sports.title: ‘Disgraceful’ – West Ham on receiving end of referee clanger to reignite VAR in Championship debate
Sports.content:
‘Disgraceful’ – West Ham on receiving end of referee clanger to reignite VAR in Championship debate

West Ham fans can feel rightly aggrieved after QPR were awarded a controversial penalty during their Championship clash.

Tomas Soucek was adjudged to have fouled Paul Smyth in the area early on in the first half of the 1-1 draw on Friday night as the hosts missed out on the chance to go top.

5 West Ham could not believe that the referee awarded a penalty against them after Soucek's challenge Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Referee Ruebyn Ricardo hesitated every so slightly before pointing to the spot in favour of QPR.

Soucek looked gobsmacked and replays show that not only did he win the ball, but the tackle was made outside of the box.

Nicolas Madsen then scored from 12 yards to put the visitors ahead at the London Stadium.

However, if VAR was used in the Championship, then there is a good chance the decision would have been overturned.

What has been said about QPR's penalty?

Reacting on Thank Football It's Friday, co-host Ade Oladipo said: "We all moan about VAR.

"Soucek just put in one of the best tackles you will ever see, and it's been given as a penalty, it's a disgraceful decision."

Rory Jennings then stated: "Tomas Soucek has put in, honestly, the most perfectly timed tackle.

"It is absolutely inch-perfect, it's a sort of match-defining tackle.

"It's like you have made the ideal tackle at the ideal time, it's precise, it's pinpoint, it' exact and you have executed it to perfection.

"And suddenly, you have conceded a penalty, West Ham are losing 1-0 to QPR at home, and they have been robbed.

5 QPR made the most of the penalty, but there could be a case for the introduction of VAR in the league Credit: Getty

"They should not be 1-0 down, they should not have conceded a penalty."

Oladipo then added: "You know when a referee goes into his office at half-time, and they've got TV monitors in there, and sees that.

"Does he just make a beeline for Nuno (Espirito Santo, West Ham boss) and just apologise straight away? It's so bad."

Jarrod Bowen levelled for West Ham in the 70th minute, but then saw his stoppage time penalty saved by Pierce Charles to ensure it finished all square.

What did Nuno say about the penalty decision?

Speaking post-match to talkSPORT, Nuno declared the referee made the wrong decision regarding QPR's penalty..

He said: "I saw the images, I think everybody at the London Stadium realised that it was not a penalty.

5 Bowen brought up his eight goal of the season to draw West Ham level in the second half Credit: Getty

5 But the England international couldn't win the game for the Hammers after his penalty was expertly saved Credit: Getty

"Tomas took the ball, it's outside of the box, so he has a big influence on the game, especially going into half-time, though both teams didn't do nothing.

"But we are a goal down, but the reaction in te second half was positive.

"It's not the best one, but again, we have to sustain, we have to start the game and sustain the levels of performance."

Should VAR be in the Championship?

VAR has been a constant source of controversy in the Premier League since it was introduced in the 2019/20 campaign due to inconsistency with decisions such as penalties and red cards.

Clubs even went to a vote about scrapping it from the top flight two years ago, but it has remained since then.

Earlier this season, there were calls for the Championship to bring in VAR after Aune Heggebo scored for West Brom at Norwich City.

5 VAR is only present in the top league of English football, but there could be a push for it to appear lower down the pyramid Credit: Getty

Replays show that the ball went in off his arm during the 2-1 win and, despite Norwich's protests, the goal stood.

The Football Association later handed Heggebo a two-match ban for 'successfully deceiving a match official'.

VAR would likely have overturned the goal, but talkSPORT host Jeff Stelling explained why it should not be introduced in the EFL.

"Nobody, I would say 90 per cent of EFL fans do not want VAR anywhere near the game," he claimed.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer is no England ‘bottle job’ – where was Piers Morgan’s criticism of Ben White for World Cup walkout?
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer is no England ‘bottle job’ – where was Piers Morgan’s criticism of Ben White for World Cup walkout?

Rory Jennings has questioned Piers Morgan’s hostility towards Chelsea star Cole Palmer after the TV host called him a ‘bottle job’.

Palmer withdrew from the England squad with a minor muscle issue.

4 Cole Palmer has played 14 times for England since making his debut in 2023 Credit: Getty



The 24-year-old was controversially left out of Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad and has missed several international camps in recent times.

Tuchel had said Palmer had a ‘point to prove’ and needed ‘to step up’ to ‘keep his shirt and justify the nomination’.

Despite five players withdrawing from the England squad, Palmer took the most flak with the initial reason for the decision being stated as ‘load management’.

Arsenal fan Morgan was chief among those calling out the Chelsea star.



Piers Morgan on Cole Palmer

Speaking on his YouTube show, Football Uncensored, he said: “I think he’s a bottle job, Palmer. I think he’s a bottle job.

“Talk about drinking the Kool-Aid. That’s a player, to me, who is massively squandering his obviously brilliant ability.



“The fact that he is so apparently lacking in dedication and commitment to his country…

“I think any player who doesn’t give 100 per cent to his country, which is clearly what Tuchel is saying about Palmer, you’ve got to just think, what’s wrong with them?”



Palmer defended

talkSPORT host and Chelsea fan Jennings defended Palmer for pulling out of the England squad.

He also pointed to Morgan’s staunch defence of Cristiano Ronaldo following his walkout from the Portugal squad during the international break.

4 TV host Morgan did not hold back in his verdict on Chelsea star Palmer Credit: Getty

Jennings also highlighted Morgan’s seeming silence over Ben White’s decision to leave the England World Cup camp in Qatar following a reported fallout with then assistant Steve Holland.



Jennings said: “Piers Morgan seems to have a lot to say about Cole Palmer. I don't understand where the hostility comes from.

“When you look at how he protects Cristiano Ronaldo from any kind of criticism, I don't really understand why he doesn't extend a similar courtesy to Cole Palmer. He seems to go for the jugular with Cole Palmer.

“He started talking about how rude Cole Palmer was in a restaurant. I think Graham Souness brought it up. That is anecdotal nonsense.

“He was rude in a restaurant and therefore that has some sort of impact on the way we should view him as a footballer. Rude in a restaurant in Dubai? It's utter nonsense.



“I don't remember Piers Morgan having a lot to say when Ben White walked out on England during a tournament in Qatar.

4 White left the 2022 World Cup for personal reasons - only returning for selection in March 2026 Credit: Getty

“I don't remember Piers Morgan saying that that was disgraceful. I thought it was. I don't think you should ever really turn your back on your country.

“I thought it was poor when Ben White did it, and I don't think Ben White should have the opportunity to play for England again.



“But I would also say that Cole Palmer, the situation is slightly different. This isn't me protecting him from criticism because I like and rate Palmer. This is simply acknowledging the facts.

Palmer and Tuchel relationship

Jennings also argued that Palmer would be well within his rights to be unhappy with England boss Tuchel for leaving him at home this summer.

The Three Lions lost in the World Cup semi-final to Argentina, missing out on a golden opportunity to win it for the first time since 1966.

He said: “The England manager who cost England a place in a World Cup final, the England manager who has been incredibly snide about Gareth Southgate, about the English DNA, who has got so much wrong since he has been appointed.



“This England manager left Cole Palmer out of a World Cup. He then bemoaned the lack of creativity and spark in England's DNA.

“He picked a team based on physicality. He picked a squad based on physicality. And he had the audacity to almost moan that we didn't have enough football.

4 Tuchel told Palmer he was missing way too many England camps Credit: Getty

“When he leaves [Adam] Wharton at home, when he leaves Palmer at home, when he leaves Trent Alexander-Arnold at home, when he leaves Phil Foden at home.



“These are some of the best footballers in the world. And he left them all at home and then got the hump because [Noni] Madueke and Dan Burn rely on physicality.

“Cole Palmer might have been injured, by the way, but if he has decided that he doesn't want to play for Thomas Tuchel, look, I can understand that.

“I don't think it's too disingenuous from Palmer. I'd be very interested to hear what Piers Morgan has to say about his beloved Ben White.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo sends message to Portugal just 23 minutes into Al Nassr return
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo returned to the score sheet just days after his dramatic falling out with Portugal boss Jorge Jesus.

The legendary forward is back with Al Nassr in the Saudi Pro League and netted after just 23 minutes in Friday night's 3-0 win over Al Diriyah.



2 Ronaldo is back to his best in front of goal at Al Nassr after a dramatic international break with Portugal Credit: AFP

Ronaldo was there to open the scoring with a tap-in after goalkeeper Waleed Abdullah parried Kingsley Coman's shot into his path.

In doing so, the veteran forward has netted his 980th goal for club and country.

However, his international future remains uncertain following his dramatic exit.



After being an unused substitute for Portugal in their 2-1 win away at Norway in the Nations League, the 41-year-old dramatically left their training camp.

Ronaldo then released an explosive statement in which he hit out at Jesus for broken promises amid his lack of game time.



The five-time Ballon d'Or winner also stressed that he will not retire from international football despite the fallout.

And he may well have given Jesus, who guided Al Nassr to top-flight glory last season, food for thought with his latest goal.



However, the Euro 2016 winner could face a ban by the Portuguese Football Federation as a result of his abrupt departure.

Ronaldo vs Jesus on talkSPORT

Whilst Ronaldo's career with Portugal is not officially over, the recent drama may overshadow his legacy as their all-time record scorer and appearance maker on 146 and 234 respectively.

Piers Morgan, who landed a bombshell interview with him in 2022 before he left Manchester United for the second time, says he was proud of the forward for standing up for himself.

2 Al Nassr fans showed their support for Ronaldo with a banner that read 'Greatness is earned' Credit: AFP



He also insisted that Ronaldo deserves respect, given he is regarded as one of the greatest footballers of all-time.

However, talkSPORT's Simon Jordan suggested that the common denominator in the Portuguese's fallouts is his behaviour.

Another instance saw Ronaldo clash with former United boss Erik ten Hag, who he later criticised by saying: "If you don't have respect for me, I'm never going to have respect for you."

Morgan then sent Ronaldo a clip of his debate with Jordan on talkSPORT earlier this week, and got an interesting reply.



"That blonde guy, tell him to stop with the Botox," the former Real Madrid star said of the ex-Crystal Palace owner. "He looks like an apple."

Jordan replied: "I wish I could take Botox. I think it's quite flattering."

Sports.title: Benin boss slams Argentina stars for refusing to exchange shirts in Lionel Messi’s farewell game
Sports.content:
Benin boss slams Argentina stars for refusing to exchange shirts in Lionel Messi’s farewell game

Benin manager Gernot Rohr says Argentina's stars brutally snubbed his players at Lionel Messi’s final international match.

The African side travelled to Buenos Aires midweek to take on the 2026 World Cup finalists in commemoration of the star’s incredible international career.



3 Benin were chosen as the final international opponents for Lionel Messi Credit: AFP

But following the match, footage surfaced of Argentina players snubbing opposing players with Messi, in particular, at the heart of it.

While Rohr conceded that his side were proud to have played their part in the historic match, he was left with a bitter taste following the treatment dished out to his players.

What has Gernot Rohr said about Argentina?

“We are very happy to be part of history, especially for a football legend like Lionel Messi,” Rohr said.



“And to play this match at the Monumental Stadium was an extraordinary adventure for my young players.

“The only downside was that the Argentinians gave our players nothing. Not even a photo of Messi.”



He continued: “We wanted to exchange jerseys, but we didn’t get a single one. They wouldn’t even let us into their tunnel (changing room).

“Security was turning everyone away. Some players were even bringing their jerseys to exchange with other players.



“We tried everything, but to no avail.

“However, I gave Messi’s 2018 shirt to coach [Lionel] Scaloni, who got him to sign it for me and then returned it to me, but that was all.

“He had me sign it and then gave it back to me. I waited half an hour, but it’s not a big deal.”

3 Benin's stars were unable to get anywhere near Messi - both on and off the pitch Credit: Getty

Argentina capped off an emotional evening with a comfortable 3-0 win over the minnows.



Messi signed off in style by converting a 71st-minute penalty – his 126th and final goal for his country in 208 matches.

He had supplied the assists for Nicolas Otamendi and Nico Paz after the break.

What did Messi say after his final appearance for Argentina?

After the match, he addressed the adoring crowd in Buenos Aires and spoke of his pride at having worn the famous blue and white shirt.

He remarked: “It was a tremendous honour to wear this jersey for over 20 years.



"Not coming anymore is going to be deeply painful.

3 Messi bid farewell to the international scene shortly after netting his 126th and final goal for Argentina Credit: Getty

“I never stopped fighting, never stopped giving my all.

"I swear to you that I’d like to come back for life, because playing for the Argentina national team is the most wonderful thing that can happen to you.”

Meanwhile, Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni said of the outgoing star: “It’s been a dream come true. I never thought I’d be the coach of the best footballer in history.

“We are eternally grateful to him for giving us the opportunity to be with him.



“The tears are because so many things are going through my head. Not seeing him anymore will be sad; he leaves us with an incredible legacy.

“The feeling of having him (Messi) on your side is incomparable… I’ve never seen that aura in anyone else in my life.”

Sports.title: Chelsea plan upgrades to training ground that ex-owner once eyed for royal property
Sports.content:
Chelsea plan upgrades to training ground that ex-owner once eyed for royal property

Chelsea have taken early steps towards upgrading their training base by holding discussions with the local council.

The Premier League side have been stationed at the Cobham Training Centre in Stoke d'Abernon, Surrey, since January 2005.



3 Nothing is imminent, but Chelsea have made a start on plans to upgrade their Cobham training base Credit: Getty

Temporary buildings on the £20million site housed players and staff before the facilities were officially opened in 2007.

Chelsea men's and women's teams train on its pitches, with academy sessions and matches also taking place there.

It was considered to be a world-leading centre upon its unveiling, but domestic and European rivals have overtaken its standard of quality.



There is now a vision for redevelopment as Elmbridge Local Council have revealed the club's interest in upgrading their Cobham HQ.

"We can confirm that pre-application discussions have taken place regarding Chelsea Football Club's training ground in Cobham," they said in a statement.



"Pre-application discussions are a normal part of the planning process. They allow applicants and planning officers to discuss emerging proposals before any formal planning application is submitted. These discussions help identify planning issues, provide guidance on relevant policies and requirements, and do not indicate that any future application will be approved or supported.

"No planning application has been submitted at this stage. If an application is received, it will be considered through the normal planning process, including public consultation, and assessed against relevant local and national planning policies."



Where else could Chelsea have trained?

Before moving to Cobham under former owner Roman Abramovich, Chelsea trained a stone's throw from Heathrow Airport in Harlington.

Their west London rivals Queens Park Rangers took over the site once the move to Surrey was completed.

However, Abramovich appeared keen on a location close to the centre of the capital - Regent's Park.

3 Chelsea have trained at Cobham, which has over 30 pitches and a high-quality gym, for over two decades Credit: AFP



3 Abramovich liked the idea of the club training at Regent's Park, but this was an almost impossible plan Credit: Getty

Ken Bates, who sold Chelsea to Abramovich in a £140m deal in 2003, recalled the interest to The Blueprint podcast three years ago.

"Abramovich hired a helicopter for a trip around London," the late Bates explained via The Telegraph. "He saw a park and said, 'That looks like a good park. Let's buy that for the training ground.'

"But he got told, 'I don't think you will get that. That's Regent's Park and it's owned by the Queen.'"



Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital completed a £4.25b takeover of Chelsea from Abramovich in May 2022.

It was announced last month that Clearlake would acquire the shares owned by Boehly and Mark Walter - 26 per cent worth £950m.

The ownership are known as BlueCo, and now tasked with taking the club's training facilities to the next level.

Sports.title: Heat is on for Michael Carrick and Roberto De Zerbi as Man United and Spurs meet in match neither side can afford to lose, writes CHRIS WHEELER
Sports.content:
So where were we? Before the roof caved in at Manchester City. Before the fury of the football world rained down on the Etihad. Before the Premier League landscape as we know it began to shift.

For some of their rivals, a marathon international break that promised nothing more than three weeks of misery became altogether less painful as the fascination over City's guilty verdict diverted attention away from their own troubles.

Nowhere more so than at Manchester United and Tottenham who meet at Old Trafford on Saturday evening as the Premier League swings back into action and the City storm abates for 24 hours before their trip to Anfield.

At United, there has been pleasant surprise over the unexpected respite City's fall from grace has given to their neighbours after a difficult start to the season on and off the pitch.

Make no mistake, though, the heat is back on Michael Carrick and his adversary Roberto De Zerbi. If there is a loser on Saturday, the sanctuary of these last three weeks will count for very little.

De Zerbi is barely six months into a five-year contract, having done enough over the final seven games of last season to save Spurs from relegation.

The heat is back on Michael Carrick and his adversary Roberto De Zerbi ahead of their meeting at Old Trafford on Saturday evening

Although the two-year deal handed to Carrick as he led United to a third-place finish in May showed less faith from his club, he has said that it's 'ridiculous' to speculate over his future already.

Maybe so, but both teams need to improve urgently – and for one of them it might be about to get a whole lot worse before it can get any better.

Not for the first time in recent years, United and Tottenham are setting an embarrassingly low bar for the Big Six clubs.

Spurs arrive at Old Trafford sitting rock bottom of the table, having yet to win in the Premier League this season.

De Zerbi's side had failed to score in their first five games too until the 86th minute of their last outing against Aston Villa when late goals from Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke couldn't avert a 3-2 home defeat.

United are likely to have dropped lower than their current 12th position by kick-off, with five other Premier League games taking place earlier on Saturday.

Carrick's side have won just one of their five league matches this term, at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town back in August. This despite a relatively gentle start to a season that was always going to get tougher once the Champions League fixtures kicked in.

Given that the opener at home to Sabah of Azerbaijan was tantamount to a bye, the serious stuff is about to begin with a trip to Atletico Madrid next week followed by a more winnable game at Como eight days later.

For the second game in a row, United face bottom-of-the-table opposition, having scraped a draw at Fulham with a late equaliser before the international break.

'It's not been ideal, to be totally honest. It's a long break. Probably too long from my perspective,' said Carrick at Carrington on Friday.

Manchester United are likely to have dropped lower than their current 12th position by kick-off

Spurs arrive at Old Trafford sitting rock bottom of the table, having yet to win in the Premier League this season

'But then of course we've made the most of it. Regardless of results, when you've had a period like this, international breaks in general are normally a time where you can have a bit of a review and plan what's next.

'We're calm in some ways. We understand where we want to get to and how we want to get there. But that doesn't mean we're calm in terms of how we play. We need to have a little bit of fire moving forward. We need to keep pushing for more.'

Carrick could argue that he didn't have the same backing from his club in the transfer market this summer as De Zerbi. The £380million spent by Spurs was more than double what United paid for new signings.

Indeed, two of the midfield targets whose valuations were too rich for United's blood, Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, went to Spurs instead.

The folly of failing to strengthen at left-back and centre-forward was exposed within weeks of the new season starting as Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko went down injured.

Shaw is fit again now but two of the players who have replaced him so far, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui, were injured on international duty for Denmark and Morocco and have been ruled out of Saturday's game.

There are growing concerns over Sesko's persistent shin injury after he withdrew from the Slovenia squad. 'Ben's a little bit further away,' said Carrick. 'We're still working through it to see how long the issue will be.'

He added that Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, who both pulled out of England duty, have 'done a little bit of training' along with Amad Diallo who hasn't played this season. Matthijs De Ligt has been out for almost a year.

At least, Carlos Baleba could make his debut against Spurs after playing in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Lausanne last Friday.

The Cameroon midfielder was United's most expensive summer signing at £70million, and the club's financial limitations were laid bare in their latest yearly results. They show that United's debt and the cost of servicing it are now both above the £1billion mark despite record revenues of £677.6million.

There were protests against the club's owners, the Glazer family and Ineos billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe, before the last league game at Old Trafford which ended in defeat to City in the Manchester derby.

Ongoing discontent over a clampdown on ticket touting has deepened during the break after it emerged that United are going to appoint a supporter escalations executive, fuelling concerns that the club's war on its own fans has only just begun.

Carrick desperately wants a win to keep a lid on things. The only consolation is that De Zerbi's need may be even greater.

Sports.title: The glaring problems Roberto De Zerbi must fix ahead of Tottenham's crunch test at Man United, how his patience is starting to wear thin after dismal start - and why new signings are a concern after £340m rebuild
Sports.content:
Pressure is mounting and the team is rock bottom of the Premier League and badly misfiring, and recent evidence tells us Tottenham seldom react well to such scrutiny.

Their last trip to Manchester United turned out to be the penultimate game of Thomas Frank’s tenure.

Again, they were under pressure, sinking towards the drop zone and desperate for a win amid an injury crisis only to have captain Cristian Romero sent off inside half an hour as they slipped to a first defeat to United in nine meetings.

Spurs return to Old Trafford eight months on with reasons to believe this time can be different and that two points from the first five games need not be the precursor for another miserable season fighting for survival.

But Roberto De Zerbi really does need signs that his £340million rebuilding operation is going to come to life.

Game of patience... for how long?

There were signs De Zerbi’s patience was starting to fray after the 3-2 defeat at home to Aston Villa on the last outing. 'We can’t say everything is bad but it’s not enough,' were his final words of a scathing post-match press conference.

He criticised his team collectively for failing to cope when one man down with Micky van de Ven off injured as Villa scored the first and for losing their balance and pushing too hard when Mo Kudus came on.

Mateus Fernandes has yet to show his talents after his £85million move

The Spurs boss demanded more from Mateus Fernandes, an £85million signing from West Ham who was replaced at half-time and spent the international break with Portugal’s Under 21s.

Also from Dominic Solanke, who he said was low on both his physical condition and confidence.

New boys need to hit the mark

The limited impact of new signings will concern De Zerbi. Aside from Jan-Paul van Hecke who stepped in ably as Romero’s replacement, none have hit the ground running.

Van Hecke was back early from Netherlands duty with a cut requiring stitches to the top of a foot. Spurs expect him to be available for Old Trafford if the wound has healed.

Sandro Tonali has taken much of the flak at Spurs because more was expected for the record £100m fee. 'Football is very strange,' he said while on duty with Italy. 'In 10 days everything can change from negative to positive.

'On Tottenham, the moment is negative for results but positive for the football we are playing.'

Italy brought Tonali some degree of comfort. He started the first three of four Nations League games under returning boss Roberto Mancini and came on in the other.

He struggled in the defeat against Belgium when United’s Youri Tielemans controlled midfield. The Italian media put down to the difficulties of 20-year-old Alessandro Romano of Cagliari on debut and Tonali was more influential against Turkey and France.

Sandro Tonali featured extensively for Italy in their Nations League matches

The leadership vacuum

Amid the disappointing start for Spurs, old criticisms have resurfaced, including the absence of personality in the dressing room.

‘They’re void of leaders and characters,’ claimed former Spurs boss Tim Sherwood on Sky Sports as he discussed the fact they had not come back from behind to win in the Premier League for almost two years.

It is a valid point, and the one De Zerbi alluded to when the Villa goal scored with captain Van de Ven off the pitch.

Vice-captain Pedro Porro had gone off injured. Two more of his captains Ben Davies and James Maddison were not on the pitch.

Archie Gray, 20 years old and fifth in the captaincy ranks, had replaced Porro although there was no shortage of experience with seasoned internationals Rodrigo Bentancur, Van Hecke, Tonali and Andy Robertson all on the pitch to organise and instruct.

De Zerbi often tells stresses how much his players care with a hint they maybe care too much because they became highly emotional during last season’s relegation fight.

As if he might prefer it if some were colder and more calculating.

Andy Robertson is one of the most experienced players in Tottenham's squad

Where are all the goals?

Conor Gallagher and Kudus ended the wait for Premier League goals but they have been scarce and there have been echoes this season of Frank’s early problems.

Frank tightened Spurs at the back lost creativity and when he tried to open-up and play with more freedom and flair found his team became alarmingly vulnerable at the back.

De Zerbi’s Spurs have been the same. After goalless draws against Nottingham Forest and Everton, his team were 3-0 down at home to Villa before producing a late kick.

Omar Marmoush, who is yet to score since his loan which will convert into a £60m transfer from Manchester City, found the net twice for Egypt against South Sudan. It might be good for his confidence but is not the standard of the Premier League.

Mathys Tel, not even among the substitutes against Villa, scored five in four appearances with France Under-21s, including a hat trick against Switzerland. Again, not quite the same.

Calling out for a paceman

Savio and Kudus are quick off the mark in tight areas, but Spurs have not quite replaced the direct threat of Heung-min Son’s destructive pace up front.

So many Premier League teams are electric on the break. Not so Spurs. Perhaps it is where Mykhailo Mudryk came into the equation, but the Ukraine winger on loan from Chelsea is still out with the ankle injury he picked up in training, days after his debut.

Mykhailo Mudryk is out injured and has yet to make an impact since his loan move

Attacking stars on way back

Thirteen, including two ‘keepers, were away on international duty. For those who remained, everyone had the first week off before returning to the training centre and ending the second week with an internal game against a team made up of players from the U21s and U18s.

It was an important time for those returning from injuries and those whose pre-season schedules were interrupted to work on fitness.

De Zerbi needs Maddison, Kudus and Solanke up to speed to boost his attacking options. Dejan Kulusevski’s progress is encouraging, although after nearly 18 months out it is best if nobody relies on him to save the season.

Ramos revisited…

If De Zerbi fails to beat United he will be the first Spurs boss who failed to win any of the first six league games since Juande Ramos in 2008.

Under Ramos they took two points from the first five and he was sacked when they lost the next three as well. Harry Redknapp was appointed and they finished the season in eighth.

Roberto De Zerbi could match the unwanted run of Juande Ramos in 2008

There is no sign Spurs are getting twitchy about De Zerbi. After his rescue act at the end of last season and the recruitment drive in the summer there is a will to give him time.

The next five fixtures, however, seem vital to the idea of turning this around. There are three daunting away games at United, Chelsea and Leeds and home games against Coventry and Crystal Palace, which would seem very winnable if Spurs did not have such wretched home form.

...as De Zerbi hails 'inspiration' Kulusevski

Roberto de Zerbi has asked his Tottenham players to draw inspiration from Dejan Kulusevski’s return from a serious knee injury.

Kulusevski, 26, will travel with the Spurs squad to Manchester United, in what will be a significant step in his recovery even if he is not named on the team-sheet.

'He is an inspiration,' said Spurs boss De Zerbi. 'He has reacted very well, with character, with courage, with passion. It’s a good word, passion.

'We have to take inspiration from Deki and I said the same in the meeting to the players. He is an example for everyone. Forget the player, but how he reacted to the injury, the reaction to being unlucky, the character he showed in this time is an example for everyone.'

Dejan Kulusevki, pictured in July, is close to a Spurs return after more than a season out injured

It has been a long road back for Kulusevski who injured a kneecap in May 2025. There were fears he might not make a full recovery, but he fought back and got through his first training game during the international break.

'I suffered many times from long injuries,' said De Zerbi. 'They’re bad because you lose football, but you come inside yourself and know yourself better. You start to communicate better with yourself. You find motivation, fix the target, fix the goal. You become stronger.

'If you react in the right way to the injury, like if you react in the right way to this situation of our club, the table, this season, last season, two seasons ago, you become better as a player, you become stronger as a player and as a man.'

Spurs have suffered during Kulusevski’s absence. They escaped relegation on the final day of last season and are now bottom of the Premier League after two points from the first five games of the new campaign despite spending £340million in the summer market.

'It’s possible, why not?' replied De Zerbi when asked if Spurs could emulate Aston Villa, who finished fourth last season despite winning none of their first five games.

'But to do what Villa did, we have to click. The first win is not a gift from God. You have to deserve to win and we didn’t deserve to win so far.'

De Zerbi revealed James Maddison suffered an injury setback in training last week which will not rule him out of the game at Old Trafford but will prevent him from starting.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso REJECTS Thomas Tuchel's criticism of Cole Palmer's decision to withdraw from England squad as he insists Chelsea were right to take care of star themselves
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso REJECTS Thomas Tuchel's criticism of Cole Palmer's decision to withdraw from England squad as he insists Chelsea were right to take care of star themselves

Xabi Alonso insists Chelsea were right to take care of Cole Palmer themselves rather than send him away on England duty, despite Thomas Tuchel's apparent annoyance at his withdrawal.

Alonso revealed how Palmer's injury concern was related to the groin problem which has previously plagued him, but also declared him fit for Saturday's visit of Bournemouth. Alonso added his other sidelined stars – Moises Caicedo, Joao Pedro, Reece James and Marco Palestra – are all available also. 'They have trained well and they are ready to go,' the Blues boss said.

Tuchel was critical of Palmer withdrawing at the beginning of the international break, saying he 'misses way too many camps' and that this was 'another missed opportunity'.

However, Alonso believes Chelsea were justified in reducing Palmer's risk, especially with others such as Bournemouth's Alex Scott injuring themselves while away.

'We were cautious, and he was cautious as well, he wanted to be,' Alonso said of Palmer. 'He wouldn't have played the way he wants to play. It's sometimes better to take a step back and wait until you feel better and do it the right way.

'There is always a risk. With Morgan (Rogers), there was a risk. Nothing happened. With Jamie (Gittens), there was a risk. We've lost him for a few weeks. With Cole, it was the right decision.'

Thomas Tuchel criticised Cole Palmer after he withdrew from the England squad, claiming the Chelsea star 'misses too many camps'

But Xabi Alonso insists the player and the club made the right call to protect their player

Chelsea allowed Palmer to use the first two weeks of the international break to rest before having him return to training in the build-up to Bournemouth.

Asked whether Palmer was worried with Tuchel's take on his withdrawal, Alonso added: 'I don't know. He's been focused on training. He wants to feel good. He's still young in his career. He has been there, and I'm sure when he feels good and is playing good, he will be back.'

While Alonso insisted Palmer is now 'feeling better', he did reveal his problem was 'a little bit from the pubalgia he had'. That is the chronic groin injury which causes pain to those who have it and largely limited his influence in Chelsea's last subpar season.

During the break, Piers Morgan called Palmer a 'bottle job' for withdrawing from England duty. Alonso said about that: 'I don't know the comment and I don't know the guy.'

The return of Caicedo will give Chelsea as big of a boost as any of their other returning stars. Without his protection, their defence carry the worst record in the Premier League, having conceded 12 goals in five games to leave them sitting 10th.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport earlier this week, Caicedo played a part in the first half of a behind-closed-doors friendly against Portsmouth on Saturday. Chelsea lost that game 2-0, and it is understood Palmer, Joao Pedro and James did not participate in that secret fixture.

However, they are all in contention for facing Bournemouth, who have not yet won in the Premier League under Marco Rose. The German was the head coach of RB Leipzig when they ended the 35-match unbeaten run secured in the Bundesliga by Alonso's Bayer Leverkusen.

'We are all happier when we see Moi on the pitch,' Alonso added on Caicedo. 'Not just myself, but his team-mates, they are happier. Everyone loves Moi because of how generous he is with his effort, how much he helps each of his team-mates, how important he is. Everyone is really happy.'

Sports.title: Georgia Stanway reminds Sarina Wiegman she can always rely on her, Maya Le Tissier takes her chance - and a bright moment for one of the Lionesses' stars in the making
Sports.content:
Georgia Stanway reminds Sarina Wiegman she can always rely on her, Maya Le Tissier takes her chance - and a bright moment for one of the Lionesses' stars in the making

The Lionesses took a two-goal lead in their World Cup semi-final play-off against Greece with a 3-1 victory in Crete.

The Lionesses were denied automatic qualification by group leaders Spain earlier this year and have been forced to take the long route to reach the promised land of Brazil 2027.

First up was Greece across a two-legged semi-final, and goals from Georgia Stanway, Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo gave England the advantage before Greece scored late to narrow the gap and make Tuesday's return leg slightly less comfortable.

Daily Mail Sport's women's football reporter TARA ANSON-WALSH was at Pankritio Stadium to bring you the things we learned...

England work hard to unpick the lock

For a relatively small stadium, attempting to enter Heraklion's Pankritio Stadium is about as simple as jimmying your way into Fort Knox.

Security guards shepherd visitors this way and that, men on scooters blockade the path, and endless metal barricades intervene before access is finally granted and the pitch, set back from the stands by its athletics track, comes into view.

For the back-to-back European champions, against a Greece side 54 places below them in the world rankings, it was a similar story on the pitch.

Wiegman had set England up to dominate. In possession, England moved to a back three, with Maya Le Tissier, filling in at right back for the injured Lucy Bronze, unleashed high up the wing.

Alessia Russo continued her recently revived goalscoring form by scoring England's third

In the rare moments Greece won the ball back, Le Tissier dropped in alongside her captain, Leah Williamson, but the directive was clear: put this play-off to bed.

There was an undeniable sense of frustration, then, with the game drifting towards half-time and, despite nine shots at goal, the score still 0-0.

Lauren Hemp fizzed a shot wide. Lauren James' looping effort over the goalkeeper was chalked off by VAR for offside.

It wasn't until a neat passage of play in the 39th minute, ignited by Laura Blindkilde Brown, that England finally found a way through.

The Manchester City forward threaded the ball through to Alessia Russo, who flicked on superbly to her Arsenal team-mate in the tightest of spaces, and Stanway's shot finally rang true. The Lionesses barely celebrated. Whether it was relief or simply expectation wasn't entirely clear. But at last, the pitch was in sight.

Once the first had gone in, two more followed, with Le Tissier netting her first England goal before Russo continued her recently revived goalscoring form. A late goal from Greece's Calliste Brookshire proved a thorn in an otherwise positive evening.

Stanway comes up trumps

If there is one player Sarina Wiegman can rely on to save her blushes, it's Georgia Stanway.

A labouring World Cup opener against Haiti at Australia 2023? There's Stanway to drive home the winning penalty. Under pressure after losing the opening match of the Euros in Switzerland? There's Stanway to fire in the opener against the Netherlands and steady the ship

Such are the expectations surrounding this England side, for better or worse, that a goalless first half would have been viewed as a disappointment.

If there is one player Sarina Wiegman can rely on to save her blushes, it's Georgia Stanway

With England knocking and knocking against a team yet to qualify for a World Cup, it was Stanway who came up with the goods.

It was her first goal of the season, having so far failed to find the back of the net for her new club Arsenal, but her fifth of the Lionesses' World Cup qualifying campaign, making her the side's top scorer.

In a tight spot against Greece? Line up once again, Stanway.

Le Tissier gets off the mark

Maya Le Tissier has been forced to be patient while waiting for game time with this team.

A centre back at Manchester United and someone Wiegman sees as the natural long-term replacement for the perennial Lucy Bronze at right back, Le Tissier has been biding her time since her first call-up four years ago. She did not play a single minute during last summer's Euros.

Yet the Guernsey-born star has remained a constant, steady presence in the background, simply getting on with her work.

Maya Le Tissier has been forced to be patient while waiting for game time with this team but got her first England goal against Greece on Friday night

'She's working so hard every single day. When she's with us, when she's with her club, you can tell,' Wiegman said.

'She's also developing, and today she had a big job too. She covered the whole right side where she had to defend but also, when we were in possession, she had to get up higher up the pitch.

'She came through and delivered a great shot and that was a great goal and I was happy for her and the whole team, because that was an important goal.'

Warning sign for the Lionesses

Greece's goal was a frustration for both the players and Wiegman. A three-goal lead would have allowed England to return home in comfort, but they now find themselves in a slightly more precarious position.

The hosts had already sent out a warning in the first half, catching Esme Morgan off her heels as Ioanna Papatheodorou crashed a shot against the crossbar. It came completely against the run of play.

In the second half, with England 3-0 up, a lobbed ball over the top beat Morgan once again and the visitors were punished.

A three-goal lead would have allowed England to return home in comfort, but they now find themselves in a slightly more precarious position after conceding late on

A diplomatic Wiegman, never one to criticise individual players, said at full time: 'I'm happy with the 3-1, but I'm not happy with the one (Greece's goal).

'I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to fix from today.

'Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy. So sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that's what you saw.'

Erica Meg Parkinson makes her debut

The 18-year-old NWSL forward became Sarina Wiegman's youngest-ever debutant against Greece, usurping a 19-year-old Michelle Agyemang, who scored 41 seconds into her debut last year.

In the nine minutes or so Parkinson spent on the pitch, she looked a handful, making probing passes forward while also showing the natural signs of naivety that come with a player of her age.

Regardless, it was a bright moment for one of England's stars in the making.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca may be bullish but Liverpool cauldron is just the start: Man City's guilty verdict will follow them all season and raises more questions than answers for their stars, the title race and the league, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca may be bullish but Liverpool cauldron is just the start: Man City's guilty verdict will follow them all season and raises more questions than answers for their stars, the title race and the league, writes IAN LADYMAN

For Enzo Maresca, relief finally came 13 minutes into a quarter of an hour press conference when someone asked a routine question about Erling Haaland’s fitness.

‘Ah, finally,’ the coach of Manchester City smiled.

It was the first and only question of the day that had anything to do with the actual football. And this – with City now living some weird post-115 version of reality – is how it will be for the foreseeable future.

Maresca played his role of ‘football guy’ as well as could have been expected as he sat behind a desk on a raised platform at City’s training ground yesterday morning. The bullet points did not make for headlines.

I am fine, the players are fine. I trust the club.

If Maresca’s team carry any such composure into the Anfield boiling pot on Sunday afternoon then they may handle what comes with a little more deftness than many anticipate or indeed would like.

Enzo Maresca delivered an assured performance when faced with questions about the verdict

But the City manager’s problem is not just about Anfield. It’s about a bigger picture, the one that will see the matter of his club’s guilty verdict in their fight with the Premier League follow him and his team all the way through the season until the result of City’s appeal is known.

Sunday’s clash with Liverpool on Merseyside feels like perhaps no other game in Premier League history.

The day in 2012 that Liverpool’s Luis Suarez faced Manchester United’s Patrice Evra at Old Trafford after being accused of a racial slur in a previous meeting was unforgettable. Suarez is still waiting for his pre-match handshake.

But that was about individuals. This one is about a club and an alleged culture of systemic cheating. It is about collective values, integrity and fairness and as such cuts to the heart of what sport should always fundamentally be about.

And yes, it will be deeply personal too.

The modern Liverpool-City rivalry has been desperately unpleasant at times. Some time-served City fans stopped going to Anfield some time ago, citing a level of hostility not witnessed at any other stadium.

So City will travel west on Sunday morning with their guts churning at the thought that Liverpool now have an opportunity to occupy a moral high ground. This at a place where their staff and players say they have not always felt safe, a place at which complaints have previously been made about incidents on the way to the stadium and indeed behind the away dugout.

‘I really wouldn’t want to be on that City bus,’ says a source previously close to match day arrangements involving these clubs.

Still, though, this does not represent the peak of the mountain for Maresca’s team. In terms of what lies ahead, they are only in the foothills.

Enzo Maresca insisted he would have still joined Man City had they been found guilty of financial breaches prior to him being offered the role

Maresca spoke with insight yesterday about footballers and how their minds work.

‘They are 20, 25 years old,’ he said.

‘They come here, they enjoy their training sessions, they go home happy. They are top of the league, so they are relaxed.

‘Look at Enzo Fernandez. In Argentina it's almost every game is like going to Anfield, so no problem.

‘They are just thinking how they can beat Liverpool. We are going to try.’

Maresca is right, up until a point. It’s true that we often afford the average Premier League footballer a breadth of emotional intelligence that deeply encompasses the deeper issues of the game when in truth the ‘eat, sleep, play, repeat’ model is closer to the truth.

Equally, few of them are stupid. The Premier League is stressful and the season is long. It is emotionally and physically taxing. How well, then, do we really think City players will cope in the long term with the unmistakably surreal nature of their new predicament?

How, for example, would a three-point lead at the top of the Premier League feel at Christmas if there remained enormous doubt about whether City will even be a top-flight club next season?

How does a team even begin to conduct a title race against that kind of backdrop? A siege mentality can be helpful but even that will only take a group of players so far.

Maresca was comfortable under questioning on Friday morning. He was graceful. But this will be no single rodeo. This is the way it will be from now on. Wherever City play and whatever the result.

Next Wednesday, City face the reigning European champions PSG at the Etihad. UEFA have a long fight with City in their memory bank too. Across town at Old Trafford, meanwhile, that famous banner celebrating their neighbours having gone 35 years without a trophy – taken down when City broke through in 2011 – is going back up again. The implication is clear – none of it has counted.

And this is how ground continues to move under City’s feet. Nothing now feels as it did.

At the club the mood remains tense but bullish. City feel the Premier League’s motives to be unfair and pre-meditated and the judgment of the commission it appointed to hear their case to be unsound.

They are confident an appeal judge will view the evidence they provided with more objectivity. This is the principle and the argument that has been outlined internally to Maresca, a coach who is in his third spell working at the club.

His predecessor Pep Guardiola – for whom he worked in the treble season of 2022-23 – would perhaps have been rather front-footed on Friday. Guardiola has sat on that same podium before and railed against the perceived motives of the rival Premier League clubs City have always felt resented their smashing of a glass ceiling traditionally tinted red.

But Guardiola has lived this fight and this City era in a way Maresca has not. The younger man’s two spells amount to less than two whole years between them. From this point of view, this is not Maresca’s scrap but he has been thrown into the middle of it nonetheless.

The rank and file City supporters will continue to back their club. What choice do they really have? Others associated with the club have started to waver.

Maresca threw his backing behind the club's ownership and chief executive Ferran Soriano, right, and vowed to speak openly 'when we win the appeal'

As one high-profile former City executive said privately this week: ‘The sooner the club holds its hands up, the sooner we can move on and start again. We all want a City we can be proud of.’

Pride – and maybe even some hubris – will be on show in and around Liverpool on Sunday. City have long resented what they view as Liverpool’s self-satisfied view of themselves and as such their resilience – on and off the field – will be examined this weekend.

Comments from former players such as Kyle Walker and Vincent Kompany this week have not been without merit. With 25 City trophies between them, they will always feel they prevailed where it mattered. This is a saga as unfair on them as it is on those who paid to watch. But the threat to City’s standing, reputation and long-term feeling of self-worth is real.

Guardiola once described Anfield as a ‘bugger of a ground’. It was, in his decade in England, the one place that vexed, frustrated and tortured him like no other.

Maresca will feel some of that and more this weekend. This already feels like an event of almost unprecedented complexity and depth.

But the problem for City and their manager is that when it’s over, the rest of this inevitably uncomfortable season – indeed the rest of a sporting lifetime that will forever feel different – is only just beginning.

Sports.title: Riyad Mahrez risks infuriating wife Taylor Ward on Dele Alli's live stream with indiscreet comment about 'the birds in Dubai'
Sports.content:
Riyad Mahrez has risked infuriating his wife Taylor Ward with a comment he made to Dele Alli during the former Tottenham star's live stream.

Alli, 30, was speaking to various footballer friends on his new Twitch channel and Mahrez did not appear to appreciate that he was being broadcast live to thousands of fans watching on.

Mahrez picked up the call and struggled to hear Alli when he said: 'I'm in London, streaming, I was just calling people, they can hear you, they can hear you live on stream bro.'

The 35-year-old replied: 'I'm in Dubai bro. There are some f***ing birds in here bro, honestly.'

Upon realising what Mahrez had said, Alli swiftly pushed his chair away from the microphone before moving out of shot briefly and looked sheepish upon his return to the stream.

Mahrez has been married to his British model and influencer wife since 2023 and the couple share two children. He also has two children with his first wife, British model Rita Johal.

Riyad Mahrez made an indiscreet comment to Dele Alli while speaking on his live stream

Ward and Mahrez have lived in Saudi Arabia since his move to Al-Ahli three years ago.

His indiscreet remark on Alli's stream risks embarrassing his other half, who co-founded jewellery line Astalia and has almost three million followers on social media.

Her relationship with Mahrez has been well documented. They starred in Amazon series Married to the Game, which gave viewers a deep dive into the lives of footballers' wives and girlfriends.

Ward opened up on her life during that programme, including the moment when Mahrez revealed he would be leaving City for Saudi Arabia in a clip that went viral.

Ward said she was 'overwhelmed' when Mahrez informed her they would be leaving Manchester and moving to Jeddah at short notice, with the star telling her: 'It's part of the game, innit,' after she had expressed concern that she would be 'sat at home on my own'.

Speaking to Daily Mail Sport last year, Ward admitted Mahrez's response to her 'still haunts me', but said the Algerian player was 'straight-talking' and 'to the point'.

'That whole week was just an emotional rollercoaster really,' she said. 'It was a huge shock and I had absolutely no idea. One day we were planning for Riyad to go back to pre-season with City and then overnight we were moving to Saudi and I was planning this whole move.

'I think it was just very overwhelming at the time and a massive shock because I just didn't see it coming at all. That scene with Riyad - that is just him to a tee.

Mahrez and wife Taylor Ward are pictured celebrating after his victory with Al-Ahli last season

Ward is a social media sensation with nearly 3million followers on Instagram

'He is just straight talking and to the point. He is very much just like, "it is what it is, you've got to get over it now", whereas I'm more emotional. That's why we work because I'm a bit of a flapper in those situations and he's very on the ball and just gets on with it.

'One day he rang me while I was sat on the beach and said "we're moving and I'm going tomorrow, that's it".

'He put me on the phone to one of the girls at the club and I burst into tears - I was like "I can't believe this is happening". It happened so quick, you don't get a minute to say bye to everyone. One minute he was starting pre-season, the next he was saying goodbye.'

Mahrez has scored twice in four games this season for Al-Ahli and the Algerian is regarded as one of the best African footballers of all time.

Alli, meanwhile, remains without a club and appears to be transitioning into raising his media profile, though he says he remains intent on returning to the sport.
