On agriculture, Mr Akobundu said an ADC government would improve security on farmlands, expand access to credit, reopen land borders for legitimate cross-border trade and support local processing to increase food availability.

He also promised reforms to improve electricity supply and affordability, strengthen entrepreneurship financing for young people and women, and restore the operational capacity of the eastern maritime port corridor to reduce freight costs and improve access to international markets.

The proposed programme also includes implementing the Supreme Court judgement on local government autonomy, reviewing the division of legislative powers between the federal and state governments, improving healthcare and ensuring that annual budgets are implemented within their fiscal years.

Mr Akobundu said the campaign would be inclusive and focused on persuading voters through clear policy proposals rather than political rhetoric.

“We will campaign lawfully and relentlessly. We will listen to Nigerians, persuade them with a clear plan and defend their right to choose their future,” he said.

He expressed confidence that Atiku would win the presidential election and become Nigeria’s next president.

World.title: My wife knew I dated actresses, still fed them — Yinka Quadri
World.content:
Veteran actor and filmmaker Yinka Quadri has revealed that his wife, Sadiat Adenike, knew about his extramarital affairs with actresses in the entertainment industry.

Quadri married Adenike in 1989, four years after they first met in 1985. Their marriage has produced children.

The 67-year-old actor made the revelation during an interview on the African A-List podcast, which was posted on Facebook on Friday.

He explained that some of the actresses he was involved with eventually became friends with his wife.

He added that some of the women he dated would approach Adenike themselves and tell her about his alleged relationships with other actresses in the entertainment industry.

He said: “I won’t mention some of the ladies in the industry. They would become friends with my wife and tell her I was dating someone.

“Some of them were women I was actually dating, but they went to her out of jealousy.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“She wouldn’t fight”

He said many of them were taken aback when his wife revealed, after hearing their gossip, that she already knew who they were talking about.

Quadri also noted that some of the actresses he dated often became jealous, even though his wife never showed jealousy or confronted them.

“Meanwhile, my wife would say she was already aware I was dating the person they came to gossip about. She wouldn’t fight them because of that”, said the actor.

“She fed them”

Quadri also revealed that some actresses occasionally stayed overnight at his house when shoots ended late.

He said his wife knew about the relationships and still prepared meals for the actresses and attended to their other needs.

Quadri noted, “Sometimes, when production ended late, they would sleep in my house on Kalu Street.

“She would feed them, and even though she knew I was dating them, she gave them everything they needed.”

Sacrifice

Quadri acknowledged his wife’s sacrifices, crediting her support as a factor in his success.

He also reflected on other aspects of their marriage that have raised difficult questions about love, loyalty and the limits of sacrifice in a relationship.

Beyond his family life, the actor recalled abandoning his education to support his father’s thriving business long before fame came his way.

He said he kept his passion for acting hidden from his father, who regarded actors as beggars.

He eventually sold an unfinished house to fund a film project.

World.title: Appeal court reschedules SERAP’s appeals against SSS N100m defamation judgement
World.content:
The Court of Appeal in Abuja on Friday rescheduled two appeals by the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) challenging N100 million defamation judgement given in favour of the State Security Service (SSS).

The appeals were filed separately by SERAP and its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare.

SERAP and Mr Kolawole lodged the appeals following a 5 May judgement of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court, Abuja, which found SERAP liable for defamation over publications accusing two SSS officials in a publication of invading its Abuja office in September 2024. The two SSS officials are Sarah John and Gabriel Ogundele.

A three-member panel presided over by Judge Danlami Senchi adjourned both appeals on Friday following a disagreement over the over the second appeal by Mr Oluwadare. The court held that the appeal was not ready for hearing.

The court also vacated its earlier decision to reserve judgement in SERAP’s appeal, and set 13 October as new for further proceedings.

Disagreement over second appeal

When Mr Oluwadare’s appeal was called, Mr Oluwadare’s lawyer, Hannah Ayanwale, informed the court that his appeal was not ready for hearing because the appellant’s brief was only filed the previous day. The lawyer also said a document was inadvertently omitted from the additional record of appeal, which was also filed the previous day.

The SSS officials’ lawyer, Akinlolu Kehinde, who is a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, confirmed service of the appellant’s brief. He described the appeal as an abuse of court process, wondering why two apoeals – one by SERAP and the other by Mr Kolawole – arose from only one judgement given by the trial court.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said his clients initially thought Mr Kolawole had abandoned the appeal by not filing the necessary processes within time.

He also apologised for not filing an earlier application challenging the appeal and asked the court for time to file the respondents’ briefs.

Paul Ngbeoma, lawyer to the third respondent in the second appeal, also apologised to the court, noting that his client would not file processes but would participate in the hearing.

The panel faulted the lawyers to the various parties for the tardiness in informing the court that the appeal with pending filings was not ready for hearing.

It then directed the lawyers to the SSS officials to file his clients’ respondents’ brief by Monday, 12 October, and the appellant to file a reply to the respondents’ brief by morning of the following day, Tuesday.

The panel said it earlier set a date for the judgement on SERAP’s appeal because the lawyers did not infirm it that both appeals arose from the same judgement.

Judge Senchi then set 13 October for the two appeals.

Background

SERAP’s publication of 9 September 2024 alleged that SSS officials unlawfully entered its Abuja office after the organisation called on President Bola Tinubu to investigate corruption allegations involving the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited and reverse increases in petrol prices.

The publications described the officials as “a tall, large, dark-skinned woman” and “a slim, dark-skinned man” but did not identify them by name.

SSS later filed the suit alongside two of its operatives, who alleged that SERAP’s publications defamed them.

They sought N5 billion in damages, arguing that the allegations had damaged their reputations.

However, SERAP maintained in its statement of defence that SSS operatives had entered its Abuja office.

Delivering judgement on 5 May, Judge Yusuf Halilu of the FCT High Court found SERAP liable for defamation and awarded N100 million in damages against the organisation.

Dissatisfied, SERAP appealed against the judgement, arguing that the claimants – the two officials of the SSS – did not establish that the publications referred specifically to them because the reports did not mention their names, ranks, designations or offices, or include their photographs.

The organisation also argued that no independent witness testified that they had read the publications and understood them to refer to the claimants.

It challenged the trial judge’s reliance on his own observation of the claimants’ physical appearances to conclude that the descriptions identified them.

It also asked the Court of Appeal to set aside the judgement and the consequential orders.

SERAP is a Nigerian civil society organisation that uses litigation, research and advocacy to promote human rights, transparency and accountability in governance.

World.title: ICC rejects US sanctions, vows to continue work
World.content:
The International Criminal Court (ICC) has rejected sanctions imposed by the United States, describing them as an attempt to disrupt its operations and intimidate those working with the institution.

The US imposed the sanctions on Friday, hours after one of the court’s former judges won the Nobel Peace Prize.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump would never allow the ICC to prosecute Americans.

“Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC. We expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American servicemembers for their defence, to rein in the court,” Rubio said.

Reacting to the sanctions in a video statement, ICC President Tomoko Akane said they were intended to disrupt the court’s operations and intimidate its staff and those who cooperate with it.

“The court, for its part, will not be deterred,” Akane said.

She said the court would continue to discharge its mandate independently and impartially, guided by the law and evidence, and in the interest of victims of serious crimes.

“The court will continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of the law and the evidence, for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes,” she said.

Akane urged the ICC’s 125 member states to take “concrete actions” to ensure that the court had the resources needed to carry out its responsibilities.

“This is not just about defending a single institution, but about safeguarding the international order grounded upon the rule of law,” she said.

She warned that the sanctions raised broader concerns about the protection of international justice and those working to uphold it.

“No one should be punished for serving the cause of justice. History will judge this moment. Future generations, and above all the victims of mass atrocities, will ask how we responded when an institution created to protect them came under attack,” Akane said.

US sanctions typically restrict American companies from doing business with designated individuals or institutions. They can also put pressure on financial institutions, insurers and software companies to end their dealings with those targeted.

Rubio said the sanctions announced on Friday were structured to allow room for negotiations and to “present a solution to address our concerns”.

World.title: INEC begins voters’ register display, PVC distribution in Kebbi
World.content:
By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Kebbi State has commenced the display of the preliminary voters’ register and distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) across the state’s 21 local government areas.

The Head of Voter Education at INEC in Kebbi, Malam Haladu Saadu, said the exercise would run from October 9 to October 15, 2026, at registration area centres.

Saadu explained that after the completion of the display and PVC distribution at the registration area level, collection would commence at polling units to ensure that eligible voters who turned up could obtain their cards.

He added that the display of the voters’ register and distribution of PVCs were taking place simultaneously across the 21 local government areas of the state.

However, visits to some display centres showed a low turnout, with only a few residents seen checking the displayed lists as of the time of filing this report.

The exercise provides registered voters an opportunity to verify their details on the preliminary register and collect available PVCs ahead of future elections.

World.title: JTI reaffirms commitment to Nigeria’s economic growth
World.content:
By Soni Daniel

Japan Tobacco International (JTI) Nigeria has reaffirmed its long-term commitment to the country’s economic growth and development, expressing confidence in Nigeria’s future and pledging to sustain responsible business practices.

The company, which said it had operated in Nigeria for 18 years, maintained that its continued presence reflected its confidence in the country’s economic prospects and commitment to creating sustainable value for its stakeholders.

The General Manager of JTI Nigeria, Abdallah Simba, stated this while reflecting on Nigeria’s development journey and the country’s 66th Independence Anniversary.

Simba said Nigeria remained an important market for the company, adding that its continued operations demonstrated confidence in the country’s long-term potential.

He said JTI’s business philosophy prioritised responsible corporate conduct, regulatory compliance, employee development and constructive engagement with stakeholders.

“Our commitment to Nigeria goes beyond our business operations. As Nigeria celebrates the important milestone of its 66th independence, we recognise the importance of building a responsible and sustainable enterprise that contributes positively to the country’s development while creating long-term value for our employees, partners and stakeholders,” Simba said.

He explained that the company’s operations were guided by corporate governance standards, ethical business practices and respect for the country’s regulatory framework.

Simba also highlighted JTI Nigeria’s commitment to fostering an inclusive workplace through professional development, diversity, equal opportunities and a culture of mutual respect.

According to him, responsible corporate citizenship is essential to building sustainable businesses, particularly in highly regulated industries where compliance, transparency and accountability are critical.

As Nigeria navigates an evolving economic environment, Simba expressed confidence in the country’s resilience and its capacity to create opportunities for sustainable business growth.

He reaffirmed the company’s commitment to maintaining its presence in Nigeria, strengthening stakeholder relationships and contributing to the country’s long-term economic aspirations.

World.title: NDLEA seeks traditional rulers’ support to fight drug abuse
World.content:
By Soni Daniel

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), Jigawa State Command, has sought the support of traditional rulers in tackling drug abuse and illicit drug trafficking in the state.

The State Commander, CN Hassan Katangana Kabaju, made the appeal during a courtesy visit to the Emir of Hadejia, Alhaji Dr Adamu Abubakar Maje, CON, at the Hadejia Emirate Palace on Friday.

Kabaju, who was accompanied by members of his management team, was received by the Galadiman Hadejia, Alhaji Usman Abdul’aziz, on behalf of the emir.

During the visit, the NDLEA commander highlighted the role of traditional institutions in raising awareness about the dangers of drug abuse, guiding young people and mobilising communities to support efforts to combat illicit drugs.

He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to working with traditional rulers and other stakeholders to protect communities and promote a drug-free society.

The agency said the visit was part of efforts to strengthen collaboration with traditional institutions in addressing drug abuse and illicit drug trafficking in Jigawa State.

In his response, the Emir of Hadejia pledged the emirate’s support for efforts to tackle drug abuse and trafficking.

World.title: Tinubu reaffirms skills development drive as NPRGS empowers 700 in Oyo
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to empowering Nigerians through skills acquisition and sustainable livelihoods, as 700 beneficiaries graduated from a 10-day Federal Government vocational training programme in Oyo State.

Dr Abiola Arogundade, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Technical, Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education (TVEE), stated this on Friday in Ibadan at the graduation ceremony.

The training was organised under the National Poverty Reduction with Growth Strategy (NPRGS) to equip beneficiaries with practical, market-relevant skills for economic independence.

Arogundade said the initiative reflected Tinubu’s determination to bridge Nigeria’s skills gap and empower young Nigerians to compete effectively in the evolving economy.

She said the programme was designed to promote self-reliance, improve employability and enable beneficiaries to build sustainable livelihoods.

According to her, the 700 beneficiaries comprised 30 participants trained in artificial intelligence (AI) and graphics, 85 in makeup artistry, 85 in fashion design and 500 in digital economy-related skills.

“This project is very dear to my heart because I come from Aremo, Ibadan.

“But it is also very dear to the heart and vision of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, whose determination to close Nigeria’s skills gap is a major driver of the mandate we have been given.”

Arogundade said Tinubu believed young Nigerians needed opportunities, skills and tools to compete effectively and achieve economic independence.

She urged stakeholders to support initiatives that equipped young people with relevant skills and opened pathways to sustainable livelihoods.

Sen. Sharafadeen Alli, APC governorship candidate in Oyo State and representative of Oyo South Senatorial District, said the initiative would contribute to poverty reduction not just in Oyo but across the country.

Sen. Alli said the Tinubu administration had introduced measures to cushion the effects of petrol subsidy removal, adding that the empowerment programme was part of efforts to tackle poverty and unemployment.

Similarly, Sen. Yunus Akintunde (representing Oyo Central) commended Arogundade for facilitating the programme and urged beneficiaries to preserve and make productive use of the equipment provided.

The Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, represented by Shola Ladoja, also commended Arogundade and the Federal Government for the initiative, while expressing

optimism that the programme would contribute to poverty reduction and improve livelihoods.

The ceremony attracted youths, representatives of non-governmental organisations, politicians, traditional rulers, entrepreneurs and academics.

At the end of the programme, all beneficiaries were awarded certificates and provided with start-up kits to support their transition into self-employment and sustainable livelihoods.

World.title: 2027: APC campaign to begin in Kaduna on October 24
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu will be formally inaugurated on October 14, with the campaign officially kicking off in Kaduna on October 24.

The Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, disclosed this after meeting with Tinubu at the State House, Abuja, saying the President had approved a timetable for campaign visits to states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State, said the campaign organisation would be inaugurated at the State House Banquet Hall on Wednesday, October 14, while the official flag-off would take place in Kaduna 10 days later.

“The President asked for me to come and brief him on where we are, and to discuss the timetable for the state visits,” Yari said.

“By God’s grace, his team, I, and Mr President himself, we have agreed on how it’s going to be done. We have put forward a proposal.”

He said the campaign would move to Port Harcourt, Rivers State, after the Kaduna flag-off, before proceeding to Maiduguri, Borno State.

Yari added that the full itinerary would be made public after the inauguration, noting that the proposed visits had been approved by the President and the campaign team.

“By God’s grace, on the 24th of October, we’re going to do our flag-off campaign in Kaduna, inshallah,” he said. “Then we outlined our state visits to each and every place where we will go, and then the President has approved them.”

On the prospects of opposition presidential candidates Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Yari dismissed their chances of defeating Tinubu, arguing that a presidential candidate needed nationwide support to win.

He claimed that Tinubu had the backing of more than 20 states across the country, while challenging the opposition candidates to demonstrate comparable support beyond their respective regions.

“Can the ADC candidate today in the southern part of the country beat his chest and say he has control of one state in the South? And I don’t think Peter Obi, who used to be my colleague, can beat his chest and say he has control of one state in northern Nigeria,” Yari said.

He argued that strong support in one region would not be sufficient to secure victory in a presidential election without support from other parts of the country.

Yari cited the 2011 presidential election, when the late former President Muhammadu Buhari secured substantial support in northern Nigeria but lost the national contest, to support his argument about the importance of a broad geographical spread.

The former governor also defended Tinubu’s record in office, saying the APC would campaign on what it considered the administration’s achievements rather than promises.

“President Bola Tinubu, since the time he assumed office, has turned around the situation that he met on ground; still, the economy is moving,” he said.

“So I think we have done enough that we can tell our opponents about what we did.

“We are not promising. We are doing it, and we are going to continue.”

Yari was appointed Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in August 2026 to coordinate the party’s mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election bid.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu sure of winning over 20 states – Yari
World.content:
Yari



—Says Peter Obi doesn’t have control of any state in North

— APC Campaign Organization to be inaugurated October 24

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA- THE Director-General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has declared that President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign will be formally inaugurated on October 14 and flagged off in Kaduna on October 24, with a nationwide tour of states already approved by the President.

He also said that President Tinubu has control of over 20 states of the federation while his opponents, Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, and Alhaji Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, cannot boast of having control of any state outside their region.

Yari, a former Governor of Zamfara State, disclosed this after meeting President Tinubu at the State House, saying the campaign leadership and the President had agreed on a timetable for state visits ahead of the 2027 general election.

“The President asked for me to come and brief him on where we are, and to discuss the timetable for the state visits,” Yari said. “By God’s grace, his team, I, and Mr President himself, we have agreed on how it’s going to be done. We have put forward a proposal.”

He said inauguration of the campaign organisation would hold on Wednesday, October 14, at the State House Banquet Hall, while the official flag-off would take place in Kaduna on October 24.

“By God’s grace, on the 24th of October, we’re going to do our flag-off campaign in Kaduna, inshallah,” he said. “Then we outlined our state visits to each and every place where we will go, and then the President has approved them. So we are going to hit the ground running by the 24th of October, inshallah.”

Yari said Kaduna would be followed by Port Harcourt (Rivers State) and Maiduguri (Borno State), adding that the full itinerary would be released after the inauguration.

“The next state is going to be Port Harcourt. From there, we will be in Maiduguri,” he said. “We have the timetable, and we’re going to make it available after the inauguration. But these have all been understood and approved by the team of Mr President and I.”

On whether the ADC presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the NDC presidential candidate, Mr. Peter Obi are threats to the President Tinubu’s re-election, the APC campaign director-general dismissed the chances of opposition figures, arguing that no candidate can win the presidency without a national spread.

“We are talking of the president of the country, and this president, who, by God’s grace, Almighty God used him to support Atiku some time back, and at the same time to support Peter Obi,” Yari said.

“If Allah uses me to support you, there is no how Allah will use you to bring me down. I mean, they cannot bring him down.”

He challenged the opposition’s electoral strength, asking whether the African Democratic Congress candidate could claim control of any state in southern Nigeria, and whether Obi could claim any state in the North.

“Can the ADC candidate today in the southern part of the country beat his chest and say he has control of one state in the South? And I don’t think Peter Obi, who used to be my colleague, can beat his chest and say he has control of one state in northern Nigeria,” Yari said.

“This calculation shows us that even if you have control of 80 per cent of the South, if you don’t have anything in the North, you cannot make it. If you have 80 per cent control of the North, if you don’t have any state in the South, you cannot make it. And that’s what it is.”

Yari cited the 2011 presidential election, in which the late former President Muhammadu Buhari won strong support across northern states but lost nationally, to illustrate his argument that regional strength alone is insufficient.

“Look at Buhari, of blessed memory. He had control of over 70 per cent at that time, over 11 states in the North, and had no control of one in the South. He couldn’t make it all the way,” he said.

“And today, I’m sure Asiwaju (Bola Tinubu) has control of more than 10 states in the South, in a conservative estimate, and I believe he has control of more than 10 states in the North. This is calculation; it is not rocket science.”

The former Zamfara governor insisted that Tinubu had improved the country since taking office and that the APC would campaign on performance rather than promises.

“President Bola Tinubu, since the time he assumed office, has turned around the situation that he met on ground; still, the economy is moving,” Yari said.

“So I think we have done enough that we can tell our opponents about what we did.”

“We are not promising. We are doing it, and we are going to continue.”

Yari was appointed Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in August 2026 to lead the party’s mobilisation for Tinubu’s second-term bid.

World.title: NFL legend Mike Ditka, Bears’ Super Bowl-Winning Coach, dies at 86
World.content:
NFL legend Mike Ditka, who won league titles as both a player and coach with the Chicago Bears and Dallas Cowboys, has died at the age of 86.

His family announced his death on Friday in a statement, describing him as a beloved husband, father, grandfather and friend.

“While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family,” the family said.

“Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.”

Jarrett Payton, son of late Hall of Fame running back Walter Payton, who played under Ditka in Chicago, shared the family’s statement on social media.

Ditka, a tight end, was selected fifth overall in the 1961 NFL Draft and played in the league from 1961 to 1972. He helped the Bears win the 1963 NFL championship and later caught a touchdown pass for the Dallas Cowboys in their 1972 Super Bowl victory.

As a coach, Ditka led the Bears to victory in Super Bowl XX in January 1986, when Chicago defeated the New England Patriots 46-10 to end a 23-year championship drought.

He also served as an assistant coach with the Cowboys during their Super Bowl-winning campaign in 1978, when they defeated the Denver Broncos.

The Bears said Ditka’s contribution to the franchise, spanning decades as a player, coach and ambassador, was immeasurable.

“His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level,” the team said.

Ditka recorded 121 wins and 95 losses as head coach of the Bears and New Orleans Saints. His forceful personality and hard-hitting approach earned him the nickname “Iron Mike” during his playing career.

After coaching, he became a prominent television football analyst and commentator. His gruff manner and outspoken personality also made him a popular figure in Chicago sports culture, including as a subject of parody on Saturday Night Live.

Born and raised in suburban Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, Ditka played basketball, baseball and American football at the University of Pittsburgh.

He was named the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year in 1961 after becoming the first rookie tight end in league history to record more than 1,000 receiving yards in a season.

Ditka was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1986 and the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988, becoming the first tight end to be inducted into the latter.

Bears founder George Halas, who had coached Ditka during his playing career, appointed him head coach in 1982. During his 11 seasons in Chicago, Ditka guided the team to three conference finals and one Super Bowl title.

His celebrated 1985 Bears team finished the regular season with a 15-1 record before defeating New England in the championship game. The squad also became famous for its “Super Bowl Shuffle” music video.

Despite occasional clashes with assistant coaches and players, Ditka established himself as one of the most recognisable figures in American football.

The Bears retired his jersey number, 89, in 2013. Ditka described the honour as “the consummation of a career” and “a tremendous honour.”

He also appeared in films and television programmes, often playing himself, and endorsed numerous products, particularly in the Chicago area.

AFP

World.title: Pipeline Security Claims Raise Bigger Questions
World.content:
By Ayoola Ajanaku

There is a legitimate national conversation to be had about the cost, structure, transparency and effectiveness of Nigeria’s pipeline surveillance architecture. There is also a legitimate argument about whether communities in the Niger Delta should derive greater economic value from the protection of the natural resources extracted from their environment.

When that conversation is reduced to ethnic insinuations, unverified figures and an apparent attempt to justify one contractor by attacking another, the country risks losing sight of the bigger issue: energy security is a national security matter, not a tribal entitlement.

That is where Asari Dokubo appears to have missed the point. In a video circulating this week, the Niger Delta activist questioned why Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has faced criticism over pipeline surveillance while, according to him, the Olu of Warri, Ogiame Atuwatse III, and Dr. Osahon Okunbo were receiving as much as ₦2.7 trillion annually for protecting pipelines.

Dokubo initially referred to the amount as monthly before correcting himself to annual. Importantly, however, no documentary evidence was presented in the video to substantiate the ₦2.7 trillion figure, and reports carrying the allegation have expressly treated it as unverified.

That distinction is not cosmetic. It is fundamental. A claim of ₦2.7 trillion annually for pipeline surveillance is so extraordinary, that it demands concrete documentary evidence. Contracts, procurement records, payment schedules, scope of work, contracting entities and government approvals would have to be placed before the public.

Without such evidence, the figure remains an allegation – Not a fact. That is perhaps the first thing Dokubo missed.

The mathematics of the allegation in public domain – Therein is another problem where Dokubo’s allegation appears to collapse different entities, individuals and contractual relationships into one giant financial arrangement.

Osahon Okunbo is associated with Pipeline Infrastructure Nigeria Limited (PINL), where he has served in senior executive capacity. The Olu of Warri has also been publicly associated with PINL’s leadership structure. The relationship between a monarch, a company and a pipeline surveillance contract cannot simply be translated into a claim that the monarch personally receives the entire value of a corporate contract.

Indeed, this is not a new controversy. In 2022, reporting on the pipeline surveillance arrangement specifically recorded a denial that the Olu of Warri personally owned PINL, while identifying PINL alongside Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited and Maton Engineering Nigeria Limited among companies awarded pipeline surveillance contracts.

More recent reporting identifies Osahon Okunbo as a key executive of PINL, with the company operating on critical pipeline infrastructure.

The distinction matters because corporate contract value is not automatically personal income.

What Dokubo gets right

To be fair, there is a legitimate question beneath Dokubo’s provocative presentation. If several companies are receiving public money to protect critical national infrastructure, Nigerians are entitled to know how much each contractor receives, what kilometres of infrastructure each is responsible for, what performance indicators apply and what results have been achieved.

That is a serious governance question – So too is Dokubo’s broader argument that the Niger Delta should benefit economically from the protection and development of its natural resources.

That argument should lead to a conversation about transparent procurement, community participation, local employment, measurable security outcomes and accountability – Not ethnic arithmetic(s).

Pipeline security cannot become a competition over whether an Ijaw, Itsekiri, Bini or any other Nigerian is entitled to a particular contract.

Nigeria’s oil infrastructure belongs to Nigeria. The responsibility to protect it is therefore national priority – This is where Osahon Okunbo becomes relevant.

Perhaps the greatest irony in Dokubo’s intervention is that he appears to have overlooked what the emerging pipeline-security model represented by PINL is actually trying to do.

Okunbo has publicly argued that sustainable infrastructure security cannot depend on force alone. At the World Economic Forum in Davos, he emphasised inclusion, community engagement and indigenous partnerships as critical to securing energy infrastructure. He has also spoken about the importance of patient capital and community buy-in to Nigeria’s energy future.

In a public account of PINL’s operations, Okunbo described an approach built around traditional institutions, youths, local leadership, surveillance technology and continuous stakeholder engagement.

That is a materially different proposition from simply putting men on boats and around pipelines. Modern energy security involves intelligence, technology, community relations, rapid response, environmental protection, infrastructure maintenance and the creation of incentives for communities to protect – Not destroy the assets around them.

Indeed, host-community groups have publicly credited PINL’s engagement model with improved pipeline security and community relations, although such claims should themselves be assessed against independently verifiable production and security data.

The Tompolo question is legitimate to an extent, but the comparison is wrong. Tantita’s role in pipeline surveillance is itself an important part of Nigeria’s evolving security architecture. Reports have put the company’s annual contract value at about ₦48 billion, following a federal government award reported in 2023.

The appropriate question, therefore, is not whether Tompolo deserves a contract, while somebody else does not. The appropriate question is whether every contractor is delivering value commensurate with public expenditure.

That standard should apply equally to Tantita, PINL and every other contractor. If Dokubo believes the Federal Government is paying too much for pipeline security, let the contracts be published.

If he believes one company is receiving preferential treatment, let procurement records establish it. If he believes Niger Delta communities are being short-changed, let the data demonstrate it.

If he believes there is corruption, the appropriate institutions can investigate, but once the argument moves from evidence to ethnicity, the substance begins to disappear.

According to Lagos News Hub, ‘Energy security is bigger than Dokubo’s quarrel, as Nigeria has spent decades paying the price for oil theft, pipeline vandalism, illegal refining and production disruptions. Every barrel prevented from reaching the market affects government revenue, foreign exchange, investment confidence and the capacity of the country to finance development’.

Pipeline security is therefore not merely about who gets a contract. It is about whether Nigeria can secure the infrastructure through which its economic lifeblood flows.

That is the point Asari Dokubo appears to have missed. His intervention could have opened a valuable national debate about procurement transparency and the economics of Niger Delta security.

Instead, by advancing an extraordinary ₦2.7 trillion allegation without documentary proof and framing the matter partly through ethnic identity, he risks turning a serious national-security conversation into another quarrel over who owns the Niger Delta.

Nigeria needs more accountability, not more suspicion; more evidence, not more allegations; more collaboration, not more ethnic polarisation. The pipelines do not know the ethnicity of the men protecting them.

In a nutshell, the Nigerian economy does not either need such distraction(s) – What matters is whether the infrastructure is secure, whether oil production is protected, whether communities benefit, whether public money is properly spent and whether every contractor, regardless of name or origin, can account for the value delivered.

That is the conversation worth having and that is precisely why energy security should never be twisted on its head.

*Ayoola Ajanaku is a Communications and Advocacy Specialist based in Lagos, Nigeria….

World.title: APC Writes INEC, Demands Enforcement of Supreme Court Judgment On Party Membership Register
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress (APC) has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately enforce the Supreme Court on party membership register and compliance with Sections 77 of the Electoral Act 2026.

Recall that the Supreme Court delivered a judgment on 24 September, 2026 in INEC v Zenith Labour Party with Suit No. SC/CV/495/2026 regarding compliance with the statutory requirements governing the submission and use of political parties’ membership registers for party primaries, congresses and conventions.

In a letter dated 9th October, 2026, which was addressed to the INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, and signed by National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda and National Secretary, Sen. Ajibola Basiru, the party said INEC, as appellant in the suit, is constitutionally bound to give effect to the judgment under Section 287(1) of the 1999 Constitution.

The Supreme Court in Suit No. SC/CV/495/2026 set aside the Court of Appeal order that had nullified Section 77(5) to (7) and Section 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026 and Activity Serial No. 2 of INEC’s Revised Timetable for the 2027 General Election.

The APC said the judgment affirmed the mandatory nature of Section 77.

Section 77(4) provides that each political party shall make its membership register available to the Commission not later than 21 days before its primaries, congresses or conventions.

Also, Section 77(5) provides that only members whose names are in the register shall be eligible to vote and be voted for, while Section 77(6) prohibits use of any other register.

The governing party cited the Supreme Court’s pronouncement at page 24 that the practical effect of Section 77(7) is that a party that fails to submit its digital membership register within the prescribed period may be precluded from fielding candidates.

The ruling party noted that the objective of Section 77 is to ensure that political parties adhere to the principles of internal democracy, particularly through the fair, transparent and verifiable conduct of party primaries, congresses and conventions.

The party maintained that the court anchored its decision on Section 228(a) of the Constitution which empowers the National Assembly to make laws to ensure internal democracy, citing Ardo v Nyako (2014).

The party noted: “In the circumstances, the All Progressives Congress respectfully requests the Commission to: (i) Immediately enforce the judgment of the Supreme Court in INEC v Zenith Labour Party, Suit No. SC/CV/495/2026, delivered on 24 September 2026, in accordance with its terms and legal effect.

“Verify compliance with section 77(4) of the Electoral Act 2026 by determining whether each political party submitted its digital membership register within the statutory period of not later than 21 days before the relevant primary election, congress or convention.

“Apply the statutory consequences of non-compliance in accordance with Section 77(7) of the Act and the Supreme Court’s decision, including the exclusion of any party from fielding candidates where the statutory conditions for that consequence have been established.

“Ensure strict adherence to Sections 77(5) and 77(6) by requiring that only candidates whose names appear in the register duly submitted to the Commission are recognised as eligible to vote and be voted for in the relevant internal party election, and that no alternative register is used in place of the register submitted to INEC.

“As a political party, we insist that compliance with section 77 of the Electoral Act 2026 is not a matter of discretion but a statutory obligation whose interpretation has been authoritatively addressed by the Supreme Court.

“Allowing political parties to disregard the prescribed statutory requirements without the application of the consequences stipulated by law would undermine the objectives of internal party democracy, electoral transparency and the rule of law.

“We, therefore, urge the Commission to act expeditiously and decisively, in strict conformity with the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), and the judgment of the Supreme Court, which must be enforced in any part of the Federation by all authorities and persons, to ensure that the statutory regime governing party membership registers is effectively implemented.”

World.title: Israel Trains Nigerian Health Workers on Maternal Emergency Care
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The Embassy of Israel in Nigeria has trained Nigerian healthcare professionals in life-saving maternal emergency care as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s response to childbirth-related complications and reduce preventable maternal deaths.

The five-day clinical training programme, led by Israeli medical specialist, Professor Offer Erez, was held at the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH), Enugu, from October 5 to 9, 2026.

The programme brought together doctors, obstetricians, gynaecologists, midwives, professors, clinical lecturers and other healthcare professionals for specialised instruction in postpartum haemorrhage (PPH), obstetric emergencies, thrombosis, haemostasis and emergency response protocols.

Postpartum haemorrhage, a condition involving excessive bleeding after childbirth, remains a major cause of maternal deaths worldwide. The embassy cited World Health Organisation (WHO) estimates indicating that Nigeria records about 75,000 maternal deaths annually, underscoring the need to improve emergency obstetric care and access to skilled medical intervention.

Speaking during her official visit to Enugu State, the Chargé d’Affaires of the Embassy of Israel in Nigeria, Ms Racheli Stavissky, reaffirmed Israel’s commitment to supporting Nigeria’s healthcare development through medical expertise, innovation and professional capacity building.

She said every mother deserved access to safe childbirth and quality emergency medical care, adding that behind every maternal mortality statistic was a woman, a family and a community.

Stavissky said Israel was proud to share its medical expertise with Nigerian healthcare professionals, noting that equipping doctors, midwives and medical educators with advanced clinical skills could save lives beyond the duration of the training.

She also expressed the embassy’s readiness to expand cooperation with UNTH in maternal healthcare, medical education and emergency medicine.

The training combined evidence-based clinical instruction, high-fidelity medical simulations, practical sessions and multidisciplinary emergency response exercises.

Participants received specialised instruction in the early detection and management of obstetric haemorrhage, maternal stabilisation, haemostatic resuscitation, emergency blood transfusion protocols and coordinated clinical decision-making.

A major component of the programme was the Training-of-Trainers approach, designed to equip Nigerian healthcare professionals with the knowledge and practical skills to train their colleagues and extend improved emergency obstetric care to other healthcare institutions.

Erez commended the commitment and professionalism of Nigerian healthcare workers, describing the collaborative learning environment at UNTH as encouraging.

He said the training was designed to strengthen healthcare teams’ ability to recognise and manage life-threatening obstetric complications through practical simulations, evidence-based haemorrhage management and coordinated emergency response.

“Our goal is to bridge the gap between clinical knowledge and emergency response while empowering Nigerian doctors, midwives and medical educators to transfer these skills to others,” he said.

Erez added that building local capacity to train other healthcare professionals was essential to sustaining the benefits of the programme and improving maternal health outcomes.

The Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, also welcomed the Israeli delegation, describing the initiative as an important contribution to healthcare development in the state.

Mbah said strengthening the healthcare system required more than investment in infrastructure, stressing the importance of continuous professional development, access to international expertise and modern approaches to patient care.

He expressed appreciation to the Embassy of Israel and the medical team, saying the specialised training would enhance the capacity of healthcare professionals to respond to critical maternal emergencies.

The governor also expressed the state government’s interest in expanding cooperation in medical education, healthcare innovation and institutional capacity development.

The embassy said it remained committed to partnerships aimed at strengthening institutions, improving healthcare delivery and promoting the wellbeing of communities across Nigeria.

World.title: Oyedele Clarifies, Says 𝐍𝐍𝐏𝐂 D𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭, Commercial Decision, N𝐨𝐭 S𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐲
World.content:
*Says no public fund committed to initiative

*CSJ prescribes 50% annual cut of PMS subsidy

Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, has clarified that the newly-introduced discount on petroleum motor spirit (PMS) was purely a decision by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) to forfeit its retail profit margin and not subsidy.

In a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance, Friday, the minister explained that initiative is a commercial decision taken by the state oil company without public funds being committed.

He stated that a retail margin discount happens when a marketer voluntarily reduces its profit margin, or temporarily gives it up entirely, to lower the price paid by consumers.

The minister said, “𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘥𝘪𝘴𝘤𝘰𝘶𝘯𝘵 𝘭𝘰𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘱𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘦𝘴 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘴𝘶𝘮𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘤𝘢𝘯 𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘦𝘯𝘨𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘯 𝘕𝘕𝘗𝘊 𝘙𝘦𝘵𝘢𝘪𝘭’𝘴 𝘣𝘶𝘴𝘪𝘯𝘦𝘴𝘴 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘱𝘳𝘰𝘧𝘪𝘵𝘴 𝘢𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘢𝘮𝘦 𝘵𝘪𝘮𝘦.

“Since 1 October 2026, motorists have been paying less for petrol at NNPC Retail Limited stations, following a discount on the company’s retail margin. We welcome the relief this brings to households, commuters and transporters.

“Some commentators have described the discount as a return of fuel subsidy. That is not correct. Here, plainly, is what the discount is and what it is not.”

Providing further clarification, he stated:

“Every marketer adds a margin to the price it pays for the fuel it sells. A margin discount means the retailer chooses to take a smaller margin, or no margin at all for a period, and passes the saving to the customer. The cost of the discount is borne by the retailer alone.

“A subsidy is different. It is when government pays part of the price the consumer would otherwise pay. That money comes from public revenue — funds that would otherwise go to salaries, schools, hospitals and infrastructure. That is the regime this administration ended in 2023, and it is not coming back.”

By constrast, he noted that subsidy involves government financing part of the product’s cost with public funds.

According to him, the cost of the discount is borne by the retailer alone, adding that the initiative did not represent a reversal of the government’s petroleum pricing reforms.

NNPCL Retail, he further said, continues to purchase petrol from the Dangote Refinery and other suppliers at prevailing market prices on commercial terms before applying its retail margin to determine the pump price.

However, he said under the NNPC template, the discount is being absorbed by the company’s retail margin, leaving the pump price reflective of market conditions.

He differentiated the initiative from a situation in which crude oil belonging to the Federation is sold below market value to reduce domestic petrol prices.

Such an arrangement, he argued, would effectively transfer the cost to public revenue.

The government, he stated, was committed to the removal of fuel subsidy and would continue to pursue alternative measures to ease the impact of high petrol prices on households and businesses without returning to a system that placed the financial burden on public resources.

Oyedele also deflated concerns that reducing the company’s retail margin would necessarily result in lower profits for NNPC Limited and, consequently, reduced dividend payments to the Federation, adding that the reduction in earnings per litre could be offset by increased sales volumes as motorists patronised the company’s stations in response to the lower prices.

Meanwhile, the Centre for Social Justice (CSJ) has argued that the announcement by the federal government’s initiative on price modulation mechanism to ensure that petrol price stabilises at not more than N1,350 falls short of the expectations of Nigerians who desire a reasonable relief that reduces the hardship.

A statenent issued by CSJ’s Lead Director, Eze Onyekpere said Nigerians were buying petrol at about N800 before the start of the America-Israel-Iran war, adding that the expectation is that any relief measure should revert fuel price to the N800 figure with a sequenced detailed plan to further reduce the price between N400-N500 per litre in the medium term.

World.title: Yari: Tinubu Controls Over 10 States in North, South
World.content:
.Says neither Atiku nor Obi can lay claim to one state in south or north respectively

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, on Friday made a comparative analysis of the strength of the three main candidates in the January, 2027 presidential poll saying APC’s Bola Tinubu has an edge over Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, his two opponents from African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC).

Speaking with newsmen after meeting with President Tinubu at the State House, Abuja, the two-time former governor of Zamfara State was emphatic that Tinubu controls more than 10 states each in both the Northern and Southern parts of the country.

His words: “Today, I’m sure Asiwaju has control of more than 10 states in the south, in the conservative estimate, more than 10 states in the south, and I believe he has control of more than 10 states in the north. This is calculation, it is not rocket science.”

He also stressed that Tinubu has turned the nation’s economy around since he assumed office over three years ago adding that this would come in handy in campaigning for people to give him second term.

“President Bola Tinubu, since time he assumed office, has turned around the situation that he met on ground, still the economy is moving. So I think we have done enough that we can tell our opponents about what we did. We are not promising. We are doing it, and we are going to continue.”

Yari, however, rated both Atiku and Obi low on the issue of geographical strength arguing that the duo cannot boast of any major support base in the South and North respectively.

According to him: “Can you say that the ADC candidate today in the southern part of the country, can he beat his chest and say he has control of one state in the south? And I don’t think Peter Obi who use to be my colleague, can beat his chest. Can he say he has a state control in the northern Nigeria?”

The Senator further stressed that from empirical calculations, there was no way a candidate without wide geographical spread can become President of Nigeria and cited the example of late former President Muhammadu Buhari who was very popular in the North but had no base in the South.

Said he: “This calculation shows us that even if you have control of 80% of the south, if you don’t have anything in the north, you cannot make it. If you have 80% of control of the north, if you don’t have any state in the south, you y make it, and that’s what it is. Look at Buhari of blessed memory. He had control of over 70% at that time, over 11 states in the North and had no any control of one in the south. He couldn’t make it all the way.”

The APC campaign DG also hinted that Tinubu had in the past assisted Atiku and Obi in their past political careers saying God will continue to make things work for the good of the President.

“We are talking of the president of the country, and this president, who, by God’s grace, Almighty God used him to support Atiku some time back, and the same time to support Peter Obi.

“So if Allah uses me to support you, there is no how Allah will use you to bring me down. I mean, they cannot bring him down.”

Asked when the party’s presidential campaign will kick off, Yari stated that proper campaign which begins on November 24, in Kaduna will be preceded by a meeting of the Campaign Council in Abuja on November 14.

His wo: “The President asked for me to come and brief him on where we are, and to discuss the timetable for the state visits. And by God’s grace, his team, I, and Mr President himself, we have agreed on how it’s going to be done. We have put forward a proposal.

“The inaugural meeting is going to be done on the 14th of this month. That’s next Wednesday at the State House banquet hall, and by God’s grace, on the 24th of October, we’re going to do our flag off campaign in Kaduna, inshallah, and then we outlined our state visits to each and every place where we will go, and then President has approved them. And so we are going to hit the ground running by the 24th of October, inshallah.

“The next state is going to Rivers, from there we will be in Maiduguri. We have the timetable, and we’re going to make it available after the inauguration. But these have all been understood and approved by the team of Mr President and I.”

World.title: UNILAG Introduces 3-Month Food Delivery Pilot, Partners Swoop
World.content:
Iyke Bede

The University of Lagos (UNILAG) has introduced a three-month pilot programme to regulate food delivery services on campus, with Swoop as one of two platforms approved to operate within the school campus.

The programme is aimed at addressing concerns over the growing number of unregistered delivery riders entering the university and the implications for campus security, student welfare and orderliness.

Under the new arrangement, food delivery access will be restricted to registered and identifiable riders operating through the university’s approved platforms.

Swoop said it would work with the university’s security unit to ensure that riders participating in the programme are registered and identifiable, while also collaborating with the Dean of Student Affairs on issues relating to student welfare.

“We are pleased to have been selected by UNILAG as one of the two platforms supporting this important programme,” said Demola Adesina, Country Manager for Swoop and a UNILAG alumnus.

He continues:“The university has been very clear that student safety and security are the priority, and we share that responsibility. Having studied at UNILAG myself, I’m deeply invested in creating a solution that makes our campus safer and more convenient. Our focus is to ensure that every Swoop rider operating on campus is properly registered, identifiable and accountable, while giving students continued access to convenient and affordable food delivery.”

The pilot is intended to balance the university’s security requirements with students’ continued use of food delivery services.

Adesina said the university’s requirements would make accountability an important part of the pilot.

“Safety and convenience should go hand in hand.This pilot gives us an opportunity to demonstrate that food delivery can be convenient and affordable while still meeting the high standards of accountability expected within a university community. We understand the responsibility that comes with being an approved platform and are committed to working closely with UNILAG throughout the programme,” Adesina concluded.

World.title: CSOs To Tinubu: Save Kano From Imminent Political Crisis
World.content:
The Kano Patriotic CSOs Coalition Forum has urged President Bola Tinubu to urgently intervene in the political and institutional tensions in Kano State to prevent them from escalating into a crisis.

The coalition made the call in a letter to the President titled, “Kano at a Crossroads: An Urgent Call for Immediate Presidential Intervention to Prevent Crisis and Social Upheaval.”

The letter was jointly signed by the group’s conveners, Hassan Ibrahim Gama, Mustapha Muhammed Chiroma and Peter Hassan Tijjani.

Copies were also sent to the National Security Adviser, Inspector-General of Police, Department of State Services, National Intelligence Agency and other security authorities.

The CSOs said the President’s intervention was necessary to encourage restraint among political and community actors and prevent further escalation of tensions.

The coalition also raised concerns over a viral video purportedly showing a Kano State House of Assembly candidate for Gwale Constituency, Aminu Abdullahi Warkal, displaying what appeared to be a pump-action rifle at a political gathering in Janbulo.

The group said the Kano State Police Command had invited the candidate for questioning in connection with the video.

However, the coalition stressed that the circumstances surrounding the incident remained subject to investigation and due process.

It urged political actors, traditional rulers, religious leaders and community influencers to avoid inflammatory rhetoric and actions capable of provoking confrontation.

The coalition said, “Language or conduct capable of generating fear, anger, hostility or confrontation should be avoided, particularly as political activities and campaigns intensify.

“We called on security agencies to closely monitor developments and take preventive measures against violence, intimidation, hate speech and destruction of property.

“We also urged political appointees at both Federal and state levels to avoid unnecessary involvement in the Kano Emirate dispute, particularly matters before the courts.”

They further called for respect for judicial proceedings and decisions relating to the dispute.

The coalition also asked the Federal Government to ensure equal protection for political parties, candidates and their supporters.

It called for the investigation of incidents involving the destruction of political posters, billboards and campaign materials.

The group said persons found responsible for violence should face the law irrespective of their political or traditional affiliations.

It further proposed an inclusive peace dialogue involving the Federal and Kano State governments, traditional institutions, political parties, security agencies, religious leaders, youths, women and civil society organisations.

The coalition urged political parties and their supporters to focus their campaigns on development and governance.

It warned against using political competition, traditional institutions and other sensitive issues in ways that could deepen divisions among residents.

“Kano is too important to Nigeria to be allowed to descend into avoidable confrontation,” the coalition said.

According to the CSOs, stability in Kano has implications beyond the state because of its commercial, cultural and political importance in the North.

The group described the situation as an early-warning stage and urged the President to take preventive measures before tensions escalate.

It said, “We respectfully call on Your Excellency to act now, before tension becomes crisis and crisis becomes conflict.”

The coalition also appealed to all political and community actors to prioritise peace, democratic participation and respect for the rule of law.

World.title: DSS Arraigns Terrorism Suspect, Court Orders Detention in Kuje
World.content:
A Federal High Court in Abuja has remanded a terrorism suspect, Muhammad Ibrahim, at the Kuje Correctional Centre until November 16, 2026, fixed for the beginning of his trial.

Ibrahim was arraigned by the Department of State Services, DSS, on a four-count charge of terrorism-related activities, unlawful possession and transportation of ammunition, failure to disclose information about gun-running activities, and identity fraud.

He is accused of conveying 170 rounds of AK-47 live ammunition concealed in a cooler to one Imrana Halilu in Dankama village, Katsina State, in February 2025.

The DSS also accused Ibrahim of knowingly providing logistical support to terrorist groups by transporting the ammunition in furtherance of terrorist activities.

In another count, the defendant was accused of failing to disclose information about gunrunning activities to law enforcement or security officers, despite allegedly possessing information that could assist in the apprehension and prosecution of those involved.

The fourth charge is that Ibrahim, described in the charge as a Nigerien citizen, fraudulently obtained a Nigerian National Identity Management Commission identity card linked to a National Identification Number (NIN).

The alleged offences are said to contravene provisions of the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022, and the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act, 2015.

Following the defendant’s plea, Justice Salim Ibrahim adjourned the matter to November 16, 2026, for the commencement of trial.

World.title: Free State primary school mourns three children killed in minibus crash
World.content:
Three JCS Independent primary school learners died in a minibus crash this week. Images via Canva/X

JCS Independent, a private Christian school in the Free State, is mourning the deaths of three primary school learners who died in a minibus collision with a truck in Sasolburg on Thursday,8 October.

The driver of the scholar transport, the school’s director, was also killed in the crash.

FREE STATE SCHOOL MOURNS LEARNERS WHO DIED IN MINIBUS CRASH

In a statement on their Facebook page, JCS Independent confirmed the tragic news of the fatal car crash that claimed the lives of three primary school learners, aged between 6 and 9.



The minibus driver, a 60-year-old man, has been referred to as the school director.

Other learners in the vehicle were transported to nearby medical facilities, where they were treated.

The crash happened on the R57 and R59 bridge in Sasolburg on Thursday afternoon. The driver of the truck survived the collision.



Circumstances surrounding the collision are under investigation. A case of culpable homicide has been opened at Sasolburg Police Station.

The school – which closed for the day – appealed to the public not to share any pictures or videos taken at the crash scene. It also pledged to provide counselling support to learners and staff.

PRAYERS UP FOR ANOTHER STUDENT RECOVERING FROM CAR ACCIDENT

Meanwhile, St Patrick’s College in KwaZulu-Natal has urged its community to pray for one of its learners, Ethan Ingram and his father, Richard, who were injured in a serious crash this week.



Richard is an athlete who has represented South Africa abroad.

No other details of the crash have been publicly revealed.

World.title: Calls for Roosevelt High School to REFUND Matric Dance tickets
World.content:
Roosevelt High School has come under fire again relating to allegations from its Matric Dance last week. Image via Facebook

Roosevelt High School continues to face social media backlash amid calls for a refund of Matric Dance ticket sales after principal Cristèl Venter shut down the event early last week.

This was reportedly due to reckless behaviour by Grade 12 learners, including underage drinking, drug use, and a firearm incident.

In a lengthy open letter published on the school’s Facebook page, Venter apologised to students who were not involved in the alleged misconduct. She also vowed to thoroughly investigate the incident and launch disciplinary proceedings against any perpetrators.



Earlier this week, podcaster Penuel Mlotshwa addressed the school learners, urging them to exercise responsibility and accountability.

CALLS FOR ROOSEVELT HIGH SCHOOL TO REFUND MATRIC DANCE TICKETS

On Facebook, preacher and influencer Curt van Heerden called for Roosevelt High School to refund the Matric Dance ticket sales or fund another event out of their own pocket.

This is related to principal Cristèl Venter shutting down the event over alleged misconduct by several Grade 12 learners. Following the event, Venter posted a 10-page open letter condemning students and some parents for their reckless behaviour.

Van Heerden accused the principal of failing to establish the facts and of “misusing her authority” in admonishing the students.

He said: “It’s completely unfair that 95% of the matric students should suffer for what 5% have done.

“You closed down one of the best nights every high school student looks forward to. It’s wrong, it’s unfair, and it should not have happened.



He continued: “The way you spoke to them was unfair. You, as the SGB and principal, need to do one of two things: refund all the students, or come together and plan a proper Matric Dance”.

“This must be investigated. I won’t let it go”.

AVIANTO RESPONSE, AND DEMANDS FOR ‘PROOF’

In another video, Chris van Heerden shared “receipts” that Roosevelt High School’s principal had acted prematurely in shutting down the Matric Dance.

This included screenshots, email correspondence by the events venue, Avianto Hotel, which disputed claims that it had called for the event to end early.

Avianto disputed that alcohol was served to Matric learners or that intoxicated learners had damaged or vomited on their property, as was alleged. The venue also claimed that the firearm incident involved adults, and not Grade 12 learners.

Several parents also expressed their disappointment and frustration, particularly at the principal admonishing the students at the venue and posting an open letter on Facebook.

One mother told TimesLive that she had saved money to give her daughter the best Matric Dance experience, only for it to be cut short.

Another father, Mohamed Kader, went on record to state that the sequence of events described by the principal was incorrect.

Other parents are requesting “proof” of the principal’s claims of underage drinking, drug use and claims that students had become violently ill at the venue.

When approached for comment, principal Cristèl Venter stated that she was not authorised to speak to the media.

World.title: Cardoso playing mind games? Mokoena weighs in on Sundowns injury concerns
World.content:
Former Orlando Pirates winger Lebohang Mokoena believes Mamelodi Sundowns coach Miguel Cardoso could be playing mind games ahead of Saturday’s MTN8 final.

Masandawana will face the Buccaneers at the Moses Mabhida Stadium in Durban, with both sides looking to get their hands on the first major trophy of the season.

Cardoso revealed this week that Teboho Mokoena, Bathusi Aubaas and Aubrey Modiba could miss the highly anticipated clash due to injuries sustained while on international duty with Bafana Bafana.



However, the Sundowns coach indicated that late fitness tests would determine whether the trio would be available for selection.

Cardoso looking to win first domestic cup with Sundowns

Despite the injury concerns, Lebohang Mokoena believes Cardoso could be attempting to keep Pirates guessing about his starting line-up.

“It might be an advantage in the midfield if they don’t have Mokoena and Aubaas, but they also have an Allende and Mkhulise. I think the battle is going to be in that midfield,” he told Soccerbeat.



Mokoena suggested that coaches often use uncertainty surrounding player availability to gain a psychological advantage over their opponents before major matches.

He also pointed to reports that Monnapule Saleng had returned to training, although the Sundowns winger has yet to feature for the club this season.

“There’s always those mind games played by coaches before big games. I also heard Saleng is training, he might be available, but he’s never there.



“Psychologically, the game has those things where the coaches are throwing in those ducks, saying certain players might be available so as not to give away the line-up.”

Mokoena believes the uncertainty surrounding Sundowns’ team selection could be part of Cardoso’s strategy, with Pirates left waiting to discover which players will be available for the final.

He suggested that Teboho Mokoena and Modiba could be fit enough to feature against the Buccaneers, despite the concerns raised earlier in the week.



The final promises to be another intriguing encounter between the two South African giants, with Pirates looking to extend their dominance in the MTN8 while Sundowns aim to reclaim the trophy.

Do you think Cardoso is playing mind games?

World.title: Heading to the beach? Saturday’s tides could surprise you
World.content:
If you’re heading to the coast on Saturday, check the tide times before planning your activities, as spring tides bring changes to water levels along South Africa’s coastline.

However, tides are only part of the picture. Wind, waves and swell can also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

Spring tides are here

Spring tides coincide with the new moon on Saturday, 10 October, bringing higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.



These changes can affect swimming, surfing, fishing and other coastal activities. Conditions will vary from beach to beach depending on the seabed, wind and swell.

Higher tides can cover rocks and reefs that are normally visible at low tide, while lower tides can expose more of the shoreline.

Time to watch along the coast on Saturday

Checking the high and low tide times can help beachgoers, anglers and boat users plan their activities around changing coastal conditions.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Jacob Zuma’s brother breaks silence: ‘It’s not looking good’
World.content:
Former president Jacob Zuma's health has come under renewed scrutiny after his brother raised concerns and President Cyril Ramaphosa confirmed he was receiving medical treatment. Image: X

Former president Jacob Zuma’s brother has raised concerns over his health, warning that “it’s not looking good”. President Cyril Ramaphosa has also confirmed that the 84-year-old is still receiving medical treatment.

Khanya Zuma reportedly said that his brother had been unwell, contradicting earlier assurances from the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party that its leader was healthy.

The former president is reportedly receiving treatment at a private hospital in Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal.



JACOB ZUMA’S BROTHER SPEAKS OUT

In an interview, Khanya said that Zuma had complained about feeling unwell when they last saw each other.

“When I last saw him, he said, ‘Brother, I am not feeling well.’ But you could not tell that he was ill,” he said.

While acknowledging concerns about his brother’s condition, Khanya said a younger family member had been in contact with the hospital and had received a more reassuring assessment from doctors.



The family has not publicly disclosed the nature of Zuma’s illness.

RAMAPHOSA CONFIRMS ZUMA IS RECEIVING TREATMENT

Meanwhile, Ramaphosa confirmed on Friday, 9 October, that Zuma had been unwell and was receiving medical attention.

[WATCH] President @CyrilRamaphosa responds to questions from members of the media at the conclusion of his visit to Phuthaditjhaba, Free State, following the launch of the Free State Catalytic Investment and Industrialisation Project.



The President wishes former President Jacob… pic.twitter.com/NV2Xs2kLnm  October 9, 2026

“President Jacob Zuma has not been well, and he has now been put under treatment by doctors,” Ramaphosa told journalists in remarks broadcast by SABC.

Ramaphosa also confirmed that the military surgeon general had been briefed about the former president’s condition.

The president wished Zuma a speedy recovery and expressed hope that he would recover sufficiently to continue serving South Africans.



Ramaphosa’s comments follow days of conflicting accounts about Zuma’s health, with his party maintaining that he had merely attended a routine examination.

MK PARTY INSISTS ZUMA IS HEALTHY

The developments follow The South African’s report on Wednesday, 7 October, that Zuma had been hospitalised following campaign activities in KwaZulu-Natal.

Initial reports indicated that he became unwell while campaigning in Msinga.



However, MK Party spokesperson Sifiso Mahlangu dismissed concerns about his health.

“The president is not unwell. He is very much well and alive; it was a regular check-up,” Mahlangu said.

The party subsequently issued a statement confirming that Zuma had attended a routine medical examination, which it said he undergoes twice a year.



“We hereby confirm that he is healthy and in good spirits. His campaign programme will continue accordingly,” Mahlangu said.

Despite those assurances, it was reported on Friday that Zuma had remained at a private hospital in Pietermaritzburg on Thursday night.

He was reportedly admitted to intensive care.

Neither the hospital nor the MK Party has officially confirmed the ICU claims.



ZUMA MISSES MK PARTY EVENT

Questions over Zuma’s health intensified after he missed an MK Party event in Orange Farm, Johannesburg, this week.

The party’s second deputy president, Tony Yengeni, attended in his place.

Yengeni told supporters that he had a message from Zuma, urging Johannesburg residents to vote for the party’s mayoral candidate, Bongani Baloyi.



Zuma has played a central role in the MK Party’s preparations for the 4 November local government elections.

The party previously indicated that he would resume campaigning on Friday.

However, there has been no independently verified confirmation of his return to the campaign trail.



Zuma’s diagnosis and expected discharge date remain unknown.

“The injured victims were transported to hospital for medical attention,” she said.

According to Nevhuhulwi, the shootout followed a crime intelligence operation in which law enforcement officers received information about a group using two vehicles allegedly planning to commit a robbery in Roodepoort.
