World.title: Same stink, new excuse as rubbish piles up in Joburg
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg’s rubbish problems are piling up again.

Just weeks after emerging from a prolonged waste collection crisis, Pikitup has once again failed to collect refuse in several parts of the city.

This time, contractual disputes and grounded trucks are being blamed.

While Pikitup insists the problems have been resolved, residents have said they’re tired of paying for a service they aren’t receiving.

Pikitup said the backlog will be cleared by the end of the weekend.

But residents have heard these promises before and until Johannesburg finds a lasting solution to its waste collection woes, this is one crisis that simply refuses to be binned.

eNCA’s Nabeelah Shaikh reports in the video above.

World.title: Manufacturing production takes hit in August
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The latest manufacturing data is much weaker than expected.

Production from factories decreased by 4.3% in August compared to the same month last year.

READ | Steenhuisen lists ways to improve manufacturing industry

Manufacturing production saw the sharpest month on month decline since 2024.

The biggest drops were in the production of petroleum and chemical products, motor vehicles and parts, and paper, publishing and printing materials.

However, the data did not impact on the rand after its release.

World.title: Postbank ready to grow
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Postbank has said its reported loss is not the full story.

The state-owned bank made a loss of R5.2-million in the year that ended in March.

But it said that it would have made a R42-million profit before tax if it were not for a significant interest charge from SARS.

Postbank has submitted a request for a R2.4-billion bailout from Treasury to help it transition to a fully licensed commercial bank.

READ | Postbank cleared as FSCA financial service provider

Currently it takes deposits and is tasked with processing social grants for millions of recipients.

But it wants to expand these services.

Government has long said that Postbank is its tool to offer simple, affordable services to customers in underserved communities.

World.title: 'Asylum seekers won't be allowed to abuse the process' - Cachalia
World.content:
DURBAN - Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia wants asylum status checks expedited, as he worries about people who might abuse the system.

He was speaking in Durban before protests broke out on Friday.

''We should not allow a situation where the asylum seeker process can be abused by people who are in the country illegally. So we need an expedited process. “Nothing that the court has said interferes with our right to enforce our laws against illegal immigration. And that's what we are determined to do," Cachalia said.

The Department of Home Affairs has withdrawn a directive issued on 28 September concerning the intake of asylum seeker applications.

The directive followed a Constitutional Court judgment delivered on 7 July in the Scalabrini Centre of Cape Town matter.

The decision sparked violent protests in Durban and Soweto, with more than 20 cars torched.

World.title: Matric exam countdown begins
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The final countdown is officially on for the 2026 National Senior Certificate exams, with close to a million candidates across the country prepping for next week's launch.

The exams kick off on Tuesday with Computer Applications Technology (CAT) and end on 25 November, packing 123 papers into the schedule.

Basic Education Minister Siviwe Gwarube is expected to deliver a readiness briefing on Sunday.

She is already on the ground checking logistics and visited Fezeka Secondary School in Gugulethu, Cape Town, to hand down a zero-tolerance warning against cheating.

The minister challenged pupils to bring their A-game while ensuring a strong support network is in place to help them over their last schooling hurdle, but she also warned about the consequences of cheating during the matric exams, adding that there are no shortcuts to success.

Gwarube said tighter security measures are in place to safeguard the integrity of the 2026 NSC exams.

eNCA's Ayesha Ismail reports in the video above.

World.title: 'You will be found out' - Gwarube warns pupils against cheating
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Department of Basic Education is tightening its security around the National Senior Certificate exams.

Minister Siviwe Gwarube said officials are reviewing everything from surveillance cameras to who has access to exam papers and whether staff have been properly vetted.

“There are [about] a million candidates that are going to be sitting for this exam. I say to them, don't cheat. You will be found out. And when you are, it is a massive disruption in your career. So rather write this exam with integrity; prepare and prepare well," the minister urged.

Gwarube led a pledge-signing ceremony at Fezeka Secondary School in Gugulethu, Cape Town on Friday.

The event forms part of preparations for the 2026 National Senior Certificate exams.

“The pledge was really about learners pledging that they will be taking these exams with honesty and with integrity and without cheating," she said.

Matric final examinations will commence on Tuesday 13 October 2026 and conclude on Thursday 26 November 2026.

During a media briefing on the state of readiness in Pretoria on Thursday, Umalusi Chief Executive Officer Mafu Rakometsi confirmed that approximately 1.08 million candidates are registered to sit for the year end exams at 9183 centres.

World.title: Kalonzo to Ruto: You have no numbers
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka speaks during launch of economic empowerment equipment distribution at Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos town on October 9, 2026. [John Muia, Standard]

The united opposition will deal President William Ruto a humiliating defeat in next year’s general election, Wiper Party leader Kalonzo Musyoka has predicted.

Speaking Friday in his Ukambani backyard during an empowerment equipment handover ceremony hosted by Governor Wavinya Ndeti at the Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos, Kalonzo declared the opposition will defeat Ruto at the ballot ‘no matter what magic he (Ruto) deploys.

“Ruto has been cornered. We have heard him suggesting that they will import foreigners from neighboring countries to vote for him but even so, he will not secure the numbers. We in the united opposition have committed to produce a single candidate that will face Ruto at the ballot,” Kalonzo said.

Recognizing the need to consolidate his lower Eastern vote bloc, Kalonzo rallied the Akamba community to come out in huge numbers to register as voters in the upcoming voter listing initiative by the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC).

“It is the time to redeem this country. The IEBC will as from next month undertake the final leg of voter registration and I urge all eligible voters to apply for national identity cards and register as voters,” he said, vowing he will defeat Ruto in Luo Nyanza.

Kalonzo called out Ruto over what he termed as the president’s habit of making empty promises to Kenyans. “The other day I heard Ruto promising thousands of dams across the country. He should come for benchmarking in Machakos. Retired President Mwai Kibaki and I secured African Development Bank (ADB) funding for the construction of Yatta Dam and now he has ten months left in office. When will he build?” he posed.

Former Attorney General Justin Muturi, who flanked Kalonzo, declared time was fast running out for the opposition to identify and name its presidential flag bearer for the next year’s general election.

The DP party leader, who has gone public declaring his choice of Kalonzo as the presidential ticket bearer for the opposition expressed his frustrations for the opposition’s dillydallying in naming its flag bearer.

“We (the opposition) are tired of singing one song for years that we will produce and name one person to face Ruto. When you see us here another day, do not entertain such kind of talk. Demand that it is Kalonzo for State House,” said Muturi.

During the ceremony, Governor Wavinya Ndeti unveiled assorted empowerment equipment targeting about 6000 beneficiaries across the county.

Addressing residents during the forum, Wavinya jeered at UDA-allied politicians who have been dishing out cash handouts to residents, terming it untenable.

“It is time to demonstrate to those who are approaching our people with cheap hand-outs that when the people of Machakos are given the tools to work, they produce real wealth. My commitment is that I will continue allocating resources to asset-based empowerment until every household in Machakos enjoys economic dignity,” Wavinya said.

World.title: Revealed: 84 Kenyans killed, 52 missing in Russia-Ukraine war
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi. [File,Standard]

The government has records of 354 Kenyans linked to the Russia-Ukraine war, including 84 classified as killed or missing in action and five being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine.

Prime Cabinet Secretary and Foreign and Diaspora Affairs Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi gave the updated figures in a response to Parliament on the recruitment of Kenyans into the Russian military and the detention of Kenyans in Ukraine on Thursday, October 8.

The records show that 77 Kenyans remain on the front lines, 38 are in camps, 52 have an unknown or unclassified location and 34 are hospitalised.

Another 62 Kenyans have been repatriated, while one is in detention and another has completed a military contract.

The government said Russia has stopped the enlistment of additional Kenyans after Kenya secured the country’s placement on Russia’s ‘Stop List’ during Mudavadi’s visit to Moscow in March.

“The Embassy of Kenya in Moscow has since confirmed that no additional Kenyan nationals have been enlisted in the Special Military Operation following the implementation of the Stop List,” Mudavadi said.

Russian authorities have told Kenya that requests to terminate military contracts will be considered on a case-by-case basis by individual military unit commanders.

Mudavadi said Kenya continues to engage Russian authorities and affected families over the burial, cremation or repatriation of remains after Russia said its Defence Ministry could not meet the cost of repatriating the remains of deceased Kenyans.

Five Kenyans held in Ukraine

Five Kenyan nationals are currently being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine, according to information sent to Kenya by the Ukrainian Embassy in Vienna on September 3.

The government identified them as Evans Kibet, detained since May 2025; Willi Muniu Macharia, detained since November 2025; Haron Kibet Pachenge, detained since March 2026; Joseph, detained since April 2026; and Francis Ndarua Ndungu.

Kenya’s Honorary Consul in Ukraine visited the Zakhid 1 prisoner-of-war camp and reported that the detainees were being held in humane conditions, had access to medical services and were being treated under rules governing prisoners of war.

The government also said Ukraine was holding the remains of four other Kenyans.

They are Simon Gitau, Clinton Nyapara Mogesa, Dennis Bagaka Obwori and Eric Mwangi Nyambura.

Kenya is seeking the release and repatriation of the affected Kenyans through diplomatic channels, including engagement with Ukraine and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

The government wants Kenyans held as prisoners of war to be considered as possible victims of international human trafficking.

Mudavadi said many of the affected Kenyans reported that recruiters lured them with promises of employment before they ended up in military service.

The government says the circumstances surrounding their recruitment could fit the definition of trafficking under Article 3(a) of the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, also known as the Palermo Protocol.

It wants the issue considered during negotiations over their repatriation so the Kenyans can access assistance available to trafficking victims.

President William Ruto has also raised the matter directly with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a telephone conversation, according to the government.

Kenya has further received approval from Kyiv for its ambassador to Ukraine, with the government saying this will improve its ability to respond to cases involving Kenyans in the country.

The State Department for Diaspora Affairs said families should report cases to the government as soon as communication with relatives in Russia is disrupted.

Once a family reports a case, the department collects identification details, travel information and next-of-kin contacts before referring the case to the Kenyan Embassy in Moscow for verification.

The government has also facilitated the return of 62 Kenyans who had been involved in Russia’s military operations.

It has provided affected families with updates from diplomatic missions, information on compensation processes, psychosocial support and guidance on the repatriation or burial of remains.

The government said it is also expanding measures to prevent deceptive recruitment by providing pre-departure information, urging Kenyans to verify recruitment agencies and employment offers and strengthening emergency assistance through Kenyan diplomatic missions.

The scale of the recruitment first emerged publicly in February when Parliament was told that more than 1,000 Kenyans had been recruited to fight for Russia.

The National Intelligence Service report presented to lawmakers said recruiters targeted former security personnel and civilians with promises of lucrative employment, salaries and bonuses.

The figures at the time included 89 Kenyans on the frontline, 39 hospitalised, 28 missing in action, 35 in camps or bases, 30 repatriated, one detained and one who had completed a contract.

The government then stepped up diplomatic efforts. In March, Kenya announced an agreement with Russia to stop further enlistment of Kenyans into its military operations and to facilitate consular support and voluntary disengagement for Kenyans already serving.

The issue remains unresolved for many families. More than 30 families affected by the recruitment were reported this week to be seeking a meeting with President Ruto before Kenya's delegation travels to Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit, demanding answers on missing relatives, repatriation of survivors and the return of remains.

World.title: Wajir patient isolated over suspected viral haemorrhagic fever
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home. [File, Standard]

A 20-year-old man in Habaswein, Wajir County, has been isolated after presenting with symptoms consistent with a suspected viral haemorrhagic fever, following recent travel from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home, where he is being treated after developing fever, headache and cough. He was also found to have severe anaemia, with a haemoglobin level of 4g/dL.

According to a disease surveillance report filed at Habaswein Police Station, the patient told health officials that he had recently travelled to the DRC, where he worked as a “tan boy” on a cargo truck or trailer.

He reportedly developed fever and headache while still in the DRC on September 2, 2026, before traveling by trailer to Uganda, where he stayed for about five days and sought medical attention.

The report states that he was treated with antibiotics in Uganda before travelling by trailer to Malaba. From Malaba, he travelled by motorcycle to a relative's residence, where he stayed for approximately five days.

He later travelled by trailer to Nairobi and proceeded by bus to Isiolo, where he stayed for about 10 days before travelling to Habaswein by Probox vehicle. He arrived in the town around September 20.

Upon arrival, the patient sought treatment at Hilac Medical Clinic, where he was managed for pneumonia and septicaemia for about three days.

However, his condition did not improve and he was subsequently transferred to Albadar Nursing Home, where he remains admitted.

The report adds that the patient is receiving intravenous Augmentin and paracetamol and has been transfused with two units of whole blood.

“Despite the above interventions, the patient remains clinically unwell and sick-looking,” the report states.

Authorities have since placed the patient in isolation as investigations continue to establish the cause of his illness.

“Sample collection has been completed, and the specimen will be shipped to National Public Health Laboratories tonight,” the report states.

World.title: Complainant letters cannot be used to initiate judge's removal, court rules
World.content:
Chief Justice Martha Koome. [File]

A letter addressed to the Chief Justice seeking administrative intervention cannot form the basis for removing a judge, the Employment and Labour Relations Court (ELRC) has ruled.

Delivering a unanimous judgment in a case filed by Environment and Land Court Judge Anthony Ombwayo, a three-judge ELRC bench comprising Justices Jemimah Keli, Onesmus Makau, and Dr. Jacob Gikeri ruled that a letter written to the Chief Justice cannot simply be forwarded to the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) and treated as a petition for removal.

World.title: How KNEC plans to stop cheating in 2026 exams
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere. [File]

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) will use smart padlocks to secure all examination storage containers as more than 3.6 million candidates sit the 2026 national examinations and assessments.

KNEC Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere said the council would monitor the containers from its headquarters to prevent anyone from accessing examination papers before the scheduled times.

“Last year KNEC piloted the use of smart padlocks in 250 containers. This year all containers will be secured using the smart padlocks which will be monitored from the KNEC headquarters,” said Dr Njengere.

Under the system, officials will open containers at designated times. Officials will access Kenya Primary School Education Assessment (KPSEA) and Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA) papers at 6 a.m., while centre managers will collect Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) papers at 7 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.

However, Dr Njengere identified mobile phones as the biggest challenge in preventing examination malpractice.

“Mobile phones remain our biggest challenge in administration of KCSE examination,” observed Dr Njengere.

He warned that the council would not allow candidates or examination officials to have mobile phones at examination centres during examination sessions.

“Any contravention of this rule will constitute a malpractice as per the KNEC Act and the Rules and Regulations,” noted Dr Njengere.

The council will deploy 342,005 contracted professionals to administer and manage the examinations and assessments. They include centre managers, supervisors, invigilators, security officers and drivers.

For KCSE, KNEC will deploy 10,765 centre managers, 12,274 supervisors, 57,432 invigilators and 21,388 security officers. Each examination centre will have at least two police officers.

Centre managers will collect KCSE papers twice a day, and KNEC will place morning and afternoon papers in marked cartons to reduce mix-ups and unauthorised access.

KNEC has personalised question papers with candidates’ details, and examiners will receive anonymised scripts with those details removed.

The 2026 examination and assessment season will involve 3,634,846 candidates, a 6.13 per cent increase from the 3,424,836 registered in 2025.

KCSE rehearsals will take place on Friday, October 16. Examinations for papers with low candidature will run from Monday, October 19 to Friday, October 30, while papers with large candidature will run from Monday, November 2 to Friday, November 20.

KPSEA and KJSEA assessments will run from Monday, October 26 to Friday, October 30.

KNEC Chairperson Prof. Julius Nyabundi said the council was preparing for possible disruption from El Nino rains.

“As we start off the 2026 field administration season, one of the risks we contend with are the attempts to cheat in assessments and examination,” said Prof. Nyabundi.

He urged candidates, parents and examination officials to protect the integrity of the examinations, warning that malpractice could undermine public confidence in the education system.

“Cheating in examinations undermines public confidence in the credibility, fairness and quality of the entire education system,” noted Prof. Nyabundi.

KNEC will operate a 24-hour call centre with toll-free numbers for candidates, officials and members of the public to report incidents and seek assistance during the examination period.

The 2026 cycle will continue the implementation of Competency-Based Education assessments, including School-Based Assessments in primary, junior and senior school.

Grade 10 learners are undertaking their first School-Based Assessment, which will contribute 15 marks towards the Kenya Certificate of Basic Education.

World.title: Mbadi hits out at Sifuna, says opposition lacks economic agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Treasury CS John Mbadi after opening new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by the M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency. [James Omoro, Standard]

The National Treasury CS John Mbadi has hit out at Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, saying that criticising President William Ruto should not be an agenda for a presidential candidate.

Speaking when he opened new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency, Mbadi said lack of economic agenda makes the opposition unsuitable to lead the country.

“I have heard of opposition leaders who want the presidency, but they do not have an agenda for the economic transformation of this country,” he said.

The CS claimed that none of the opposition leaders is suitable for the presidency.

“These opposition leaders cannot make any economic change in this country. They should not be elected,” he said.

He told Nyanza residents to shun the new wave of opposition led by Sifuna.

Mbadi claimed that opposition leaders lack political direction.

He said Sifuna had taken too long to unveil a political party that he will use to run for the presidency.

“Do not join the opposition bandwagon. We are just a few months away from the General Election, but Sifuna still doesn’t know a political party he will use to run for the presidency. They are still leaving in confusion,” Mbadi said.

He said Sifuna has not demonstrated how to improve this country’s economy.

“Former President Uhuru Kenyatta left the economy of this country in tatters. We have tried to improve it but we are not yet where we want it to be,” Mbadi said.

He urged Nyanza residents to support Ruto.

The CS said Ruto’s government had improved mega infrastructural projects across the country as part of economic transformation.

He cited the 74 km Mbita- Sindo- Sori road, Lake Victoria ring road and other infrastructure projects as some of the reasons residents should support Ruto.

“I urge you to support Ruto so that we can continue acquiring more development projects in this region,” Mbadi said.

World.title: Kericho Annex Prison under scrutiny over death of remand prisoner
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Brenda Chemutai, 19, who allegedly committed suicide inside the Kericho Annex Prison where she was awaiting trial for an offence of being in possession of bhang that was seized in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer. [Courtesy]

Questions are mounting over security and accountability at Kericho Annex Prison following the death of a 19-year-old remand prisoner in a suspected case of suicide.

Her family is demanding answers about how she obtained a bedsheet and why they were not notified until nearly 10 hours after the incident.

Brenda Chemutai was reportedly found hanging from a double-decker bed at around 9 am when her fellow cellmates were having breakfast on Friday.

The cell had eight inmates, who had gone for breakfast, according to a police report.

However, her relatives state they were not informed until about 7 pm, after her body had already been taken from the prison and transferred to the Kericho County Hospital Mortuary.

The delay has raised serious concerns for the family, which calls for authorities to clarify what happened between the time Chemutai was discovered and when her next of kin were contacted.

Kericho East Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officer, Kennedy Apindi, said police have launched investigations following reports from prison officials that the incident was a suicide.

He mentioned that preliminary information indicated Chemutai allegedly used a bedsheet.

The family, however, insists that investigators determine when she was found, who discovered her, when the incident was reported to police, who authorised her body’s removal, and why her relatives were not notified immediately.

“We had spoken with Brenda. She was expected to be released around December, and by January we would all have been together at home,” said her sister, Phyllis Cherotich.

Cherotich added that the family had seen no signs indicating Chemutai intended to take her own life.

"Her death has shocked us deeply. She never mentioned any plans of this nature. We want to understand how this was possible given the level of security at the facility," she said.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged use of a bedsheet have also raised questions for the family.

Her uncle, Michael Rono, questioned how such an item came into Chemutai's possession while she was in a remand facility.

"I am deeply surprised. When one enters the prison, one is carefully searched. Where did the bedsheet come from? We ask the government to ensure justice is done," Rono said.

Chemutai had been in remand since 2024, with her relatives saying she was arrested while still a minor and had spent nearly two years awaiting the conclusion of her case.

She was being tried for the offence of possession of bhang in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer.

Her death has consequently brought renewed scrutiny to not only what happened inside the prison but also the circumstances that led to her prolonged detention.

Youth activists from the Voice of Youth Organisation, led by Kelvin Kipchichir, have joined the family in demanding investigations into both the death and the case that resulted in Chemutai's detention.

Kipchichir claimed Chemutai was arrested alongside other suspects in a vehicle allegedly linked to an Officer Commanding Station serving in Kakamega.

According to the activists, police recovered 32 rolls of bhang from the vehicle, while some of the suspects allegedly fled, leaving Chemutai behind.

The claims have not been independently established.

Kipchichir questioned why Chemutai remained in custody for such a prolonged period and called for scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the vehicle and its alleged connection to the police officer.

“We are concerned that an OCS in the National Police Service could allow a vehicle to be used by an individual with a known criminal record,” he said.

He called on the Ministry of Interior to establish who owned or controlled the vehicle and under what circumstances it was allegedly being used.

The activists said the vehicle was still at Kericho Police Station.

For the family, the tragedy has been compounded by personal loss. Chemutai's father died while she was in remand, while she leaves behind a young child.

Relatives said detectives had informed them that the person alleged to own the bhang had since been arrested and was being held in Kisumu.

But the immediate question for Chemutai's family is what happened during her final hours.

They want a clear account of the period between the reported discovery of her body at about 9 am and the notification of the family nearly 10 hours later.

They also want investigators to establish how the bedsheet allegedly used in the incident came into her possession and whether prison officers followed all required procedures after she was found.

The activists are calling for the inquiry to extend beyond the death of Chemutai to her arrest, the length of her detention and the handling of the case against her.

The family has demanded a transparent and independent investigation, saying it wants answers on how a teenager who entered the justice system while still a minor ended up dead in remand custody.

The family says it wants those questions answered before proceeding with burial arrangements.

World.title: Egypt’s Hurghada allocates LE 23 million to first fully-equipped stray dog shelter
World.content:
In a major step toward balancing public safety with animal welfare, the Red Sea Housing Directorate has officially allocated a LE 23 million contract to launch Hurghada’s first fully integrated shelter for free-roaming street dogs.

Moving beyond temporary fixes, the coastal resort town is rolling out a comprehensive, humane strategy designed to manage its stray population with long-term care, structured medical intervention, and proper safety standards.

A modern approach to animal welfare

The ambitious project forms part of a broader technical and logistical framework supporting Red Sea Governorate authorities. Rather than relying on outdated containment methods, the initiative integrates standardized architectural blueprints built around high safety and hygiene guidelines, ensuring that the animals receive proper care in a secure environment.

Key components of the initiative include:

Mass vaccination campaigns: Systematically administering rabies vaccines across the local stray population to protect both communities and animals.

Specialized fleet transport: Equipping the regional directorate with purpose-built transport vehicles adhering to strict technical specifications, guaranteeing safe, stress-free relocation for street dogs.

Structured medical facilities: Establishing dedicated shelter zones for veterinary checkups, sterilization programs, and ongoing recovery.

By combining engineering precision with veterinary science, Hurghada aims to pioneer a sustainable blueprint for animal management along the Red Sea coast—offering a safer, cleaner environment for residents and tourists while giving local stray animals the care and sanctuary they deserve.

World.title: Houthi Airport attacks leave 3 dead and dozens wounded, including two Egyptians
World.content:
The Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) revealed on Wednesday that attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport resulted in several injuries among citizens and foreign residents, ranging from minor to severe, as a result of the Houthi aggression on King Khalid International Airport.

In an official statement, the authority explained that “on Tuesday and Wednesday, Abha and King Khalid International Airports were subjected to two attacks targeting their facilities. Emergency teams and competent authorities immediately responded to both attacks upon occurrence, in accordance with approved procedures and plans.”

The statement continued: “The overt attack on Abha International Airport resulted in two fatalities among female residents of Moroccan and Algerian nationalities, as well as 28 injuries among citizens and two foreign residents of Bangladeshi and Philippine nationalities, with injuries ranging from minor to severe.”

According to the statement: “The attack on King Khalid International Airport resulted in one fatality of a resident of Sudanese nationality, along with eight injuries, including five citizens, two residents of Egyptian nationality, and one resident of Pakistani nationality, with injuries ranging from minor to severe.”

The authority noted that “all injured individuals were immediately transferred to the hospital to receive the necessary medical care, and both attacks resulted in some material damage.”

The authority clarified that it is working in continuous integration and coordination with relevant security agencies to assess damages and take all necessary measures to ensure the safety of passengers and workers, while maintaining the security and safety of the civil aviation system in the Kingdom.

World.title: Israel forces out British diplomats in Jerusalem over West Bank sanctions
World.content:
Israel announced that the majority of British diplomats will depart from the British Consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, in response to UK sanctions imposed on settlements in the occupied West Bank.

According to the BBC, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar stated that Israel implemented the measures it had announced and committed to on September 8 in response to British sanctions. Sa’ar said: “The British Consulate in Jerusalem shuts down its operations today. Accordingly, the plaque of the British Consulate in Jerusalem has been removed.”

However, the British flag could still be seen outside the building, and several staff members were seen entering on Thursday morning.

Limited diplomatic staff inside the building

Sa’ar noted that talks with the British government led to an agreement on specific principles, including that “the Consul General and 20 diplomats (including the Consul General) are ending their duties and will leave Israel.”

At the same time, the Israeli Foreign Minister acknowledged that the building “is owned by the British Government,” clarifying that Israel permitted a “skeleton staff of only seven diplomats with a very limited scope of operations” to work inside.

He added that as a result of this agreement with the United Kingdom, “no steps will be taken against Israel.”

He continued: “We did not want to reach this stage,” explaining that 20 diplomats, including the Consul General, will leave Israel, while a task force of 7 members will be permitted to remain inside the building with a “very limited operational scope.”

UK temporarily withdraws staff for security reasons

In response, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband stated that the United Kingdom has “temporarily withdrawn some staff” for security reasons, emphasizing that the mission “will continue to work with the Palestinian people.”

Miliband added that the UK government does not accept that Israel has the right to close the consulate, reiterating London’s position that “East Jerusalem is occupied territory.”

Miliband noted that following discussions with the Israeli government, the building “will not close” and will be known as the “UK Mission in Jerusalem.”

He further explained that the discussions did not yield an understanding regarding “the necessary guarantees for the security and protection of our staff and premises.”

He added: “Accordingly, the UK has temporarily withdrawn a number of staff and their families to ensure their security and safety.”

British sanctions on settlements

Israel had announced last September that it would close the British Consulate in retaliation for revised UK sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, which are considered illegal under international law.

The British government made last-minute efforts to persuade Israel not to close the consulate ahead of the deadline, after Tel Aviv announced it would close the consulate within 30 days of the sanctions’ announcement.

Israeli media had reported that the United Kingdom threatened to expel Israeli diplomats from London, raising the prospect of further damage to bilateral ties between the two countries.

The British Consulate, originally established in 1838, manages UK relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem, as well as in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.

According to the BBC, the consulate operates separately from the British Embassy in Tel Aviv, which serves as the UK’s primary diplomatic hub in Israel.

World.title: Israel issues high-level travel warning for Egypt and regional nations
World.content:
Israel’s National Security Council (NSC) has issued a renewed travel advisory urging Israeli citizens to avoid all travel to several regional countries, explicitly highlighting Egypt, including the Sinai Peninsula, under a Level 4 (High Threat) warning.

In an official public advisory, the NSC warned of heightened security risks, potential terror threats, and anti-Israel demonstrations targeting Israelis and Jewish communities abroad. The agency noted that regional threat groups and global jihad factions view this period as a key milestone to mobilize actions against Israeli targets.

Alongside Egypt, the Level 4 travel warning applies to destinations including Jordan, Qatar, and Somaliland.

Key recommendations from the NSC statement:

Avoid travel and depart promptly: Israeli nationals are advised to avoid traveling to Level 4 countries and to leave these areas if currently present.

Maintain low public profile: For citizens in regions under elevated threat levels, the council recommends minimizing the use of spoken Hebrew in crowded public spaces, avoiding public gatherings or protests, and refraining from displaying identifying symbols.

Digital and operational security: The advisory instructs citizens not to post advance travel itineraries or personal location details on social media, nor share content reflecting active or past service in Israeli security forces.

The NSC emphasized that citizens abroad experiencing immediate security threats should first contact local law enforcement authorities before notifying Israeli diplomatic hotlines.

World.title: Fitch affirms Egypt’s credit rating at “B” with a stable outlook
World.content:
Fitch Ratings has affirmed Egypt’s long-term foreign-currency sovereign credit rating at “B” with a Stable Outlook.

The agency noted that the rating is supported by expectations of relatively high economic growth for the Egyptian economy, continued strong support from international and regional partners, as well as the economy’s large scale compared to other peer countries in the same rating category.

Fitch stated that since the beginning of this year, the Egyptian economy has demonstrated improved resilience against external pressures. Total international reserves increased by approximately $5.5 billion over the first eight months of the year, reaching around $54.4 billion.

Additionally, the Central Bank of Egypt’s (CBE) net foreign assets surplus rose to nearly $19 billion in August, marking an increase of $5.6 billion during the first eight months of the year.

Fitch added that Egypt’s flexible exchange rate policy faced a real test with the outbreak of the war involving Iran, which led to an outflow of over $6 billion in foreign portfolio investments from government debt securities (around 1.4 percent of GDP).

This caused the Egyptian Pound to depreciate by more than 14 percent against the US Dollar. Despite these pressures, the CBE maintained currency convertibility without imposing foreign exchange restrictions or supporting the exchange rate, thereby enhancing the credibility of the flexible exchange rate regime.

The rating agency highlighted that “hot money” inflows returned quickly to the Egyptian market after weathering the initial war shock, helping the Egyptian Pound gradually recover.

Fitch expects that following the conclusion of Egypt’s IMF program in November 2026, the CBE will continue to maintain positive real interest rates alongside flexible exchange rate management.

Despite ongoing challenges, Fitch projects continued economic resilience, estimating GDP growth at approximately 5.1 percent in 2026, driven by improved performance across the tourism, manufacturing, and consumer sectors. While the agency expects growth to slow slightly to around 4.7 percent in 2027, it noted that this pace remains relatively high compared to many peer economies.

On the other hand, Fitch warned of persistent vulnerability factors, primarily weak public finances, exceptionally high interest-to-revenue ratios, significant external financing needs, inflation, and ongoing geopolitical risks.

World.title: Total closure on the 26th of July Axis and Ring Road in Giza for 5 days
World.content:
Giza Governorate has announced a total closure on the 26th of July Axis and the Ring Road (Western Arc) heading toward 15th of May Bridge for a period of 5 days.

In an official statement released today, the governorate explained that as part of the construction works for the Monorail project (Wadi El Nile – 6th of October Line) and to complete structural works at the Wadi El Nile Monorail Station on the 26th of July Axis, a total closure will be implemented for traffic coming from above the 26th of July Axis and the Western Arc Ring Road heading toward 15th of May Bridge.

The governorate clarified that the closure will initially begin on a trial basis without construction activity for 5 days, starting at 12:05 AM on Thursday, October 8, 2026, until the morning of Monday, October 12, 2026. This trial period aims to assess the impact of the closure on traffic flow prior to commencing actual construction once smooth traffic movement is ensured. Following the trial, the full closure will remain in place for 6 months starting Monday morning, October 12, 2026, until the completion of the project works.

Giza Governorate outlined the suggested alternative routes as follows:

First Alternative Route: Vehicles coming from the Ring Road (Western Arc) above the 26th of July Axis bound for 15th of May Bridge will take the off-ramp leading to Sudan Street, continue along Sudan Street until its intersection with Gamet El Dewal Al Arabeya Street, and then turn left onto Gamet El Dewal Al Arabeya Street heading toward 15th of May Bridge.

Second Alternative Route: Vehicles coming from the Ring Road (Western Arc) above the 26th of July Axis bound for 15th of May Bridge will take the off-ramp leading to Lebanon Square, enter Lebanon Street, turn left onto Shehab Street, and then turn left onto the surface road of the Wadi El Nile Tunnel to reach 26th of July Street toward 15th of May Bridge after bypassing the work zone.

The General Directorate of Giza Traffic, in coordination with the executing company, has placed all necessary traffic guidance and warning signs, floodlights, and flashing beacons around the entire work area to ensure public safety, alongside deploying traffic personnel to facilitate vehicle movement.

World.title: Who is Zack Polanski, the ‘eco-populist’ rattling the UK’s establishment?
World.content:
London — The leader of the UK’s Green Party, Zack Polanski, will on Thursday challenge the political establishment by taking on the ruling Labour Party in a special election for the seat held by former prime minister Keir Starmer.

Polanski, with his deep reserve of progressive policies and an active presence on TikTok cuts a markedly different figure to Starmer, who consistently alienated his Labour Party’s left-wing and developed a reputation as a stilted, ineffective communicator.

That contrast helped Polanski and the Greens gain traction as a popular left-wing alternative to the governing, center-left Labour Party, which has been bleeding voters in recent years over its stance on issues like welfare spending, trans rights and the war in Gaza. Polanski even said on more than one occasion that his party “is here to replace Labour.”

But that momentum has largely stalled since Starmer resigned as prime minister in the summer following enormous pressure from his party. He stepped down as a member of parliament (MP) last month, triggering the by-election.

In Starmer’s place, a more formidable opponent has emerged. Andy Burnham, the current prime minister, is widely seen as a better political operator and more capable of appealing to a broad spectrum of voters, including the progressives Polanski has been targeting.

Britain’s new Prime Minister Andy Burnham took office in July. Christopher Furlong/Getty Images

So the outcome of this by-election – in the central London constituency of Holborn and St. Pancras – represents more than just Polanski potentially becoming an MP.

It pits the Greens and Labour directly against each other for the first time since Burnham took office, acting as the first major electoral test for the new government as well as a barometer of the Greens’ ability to compete with a rejuvenated Labour.

If Polanski wins on Thursday, it will be a stern warning for the new prime minister and could be an early indicator that Britain’s left flank has irrevocably split. But if he loses and Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali holds the party’s seat, it will serve as a sign that Burnham has managed to pull progressives back into the Labour Party and slow its electoral decline.

Differing stances over the war in Gaza and antisemitism are central to that split, and to this by-election. Many Muslim voters have said they will not vote Labour because they think the government has not acted strongly enough over Gaza.

This weekend, the Greens adopted a controversial motion classifying Zionism, which Jewish groups sometimes define as a right to Jewish self-determination, as a form of racism, calling it an “ethnonationalist political project.”

Polanski, who is Jewish and changed his name from David Paulden when he was 18 to honor that heritage, did not vote on the motion nor mention it in his speech to the conference. He describes himself as an “anti-Zionist.” Israel responded by banning Polanski from visiting the country.

On Wednesday, a fresh storm broke out in British media over a reported friendship between the Green Party member who proposed the motion and a man convicted in the United States on al Qaeda terrorism charges.

Any split in the left comes at a critical moment in British politics, with Labour (and the Greens) also focused on containing a rising right-wing wave, most clearly signaled by the rapid ascent of the hard-right populist party, Reform UK.

Who is Polanski?

A self-described “eco-populist,” Polanski, 43, was catapulted onto the national stage last fall when he secured a surprise victory in the Greens’ leadership election, beating two of the party’s four MPs to claim the top job. Before that, he was still a little-known local politician, representing the Greens in the London Assembly.

The broad brushstrokes of Polanski’s image go something like this: to his admirers, he is an antidote to the stiff technocratic tendencies of more mainstream politicians; a gifted communicator willing to adopt the bold left-wing policies Labour has largely shied away from.

To his detractors, he is vague and unable to pin down the details of his own policies.

More recently, his social media use sparked controversy after he criticized the police’s response to an antisemitic attack in north London and, in a separate incident, reposted a photo that some interpreted as threatening Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform UK.

Zack Polanski is running to become an MP for the central London constituency of Holborn and St Pancras. Toby Shepheard/AFP/Getty Images

Still, under his leadership, the party has commanded national attention, building on its best general election performance when it secured four parliamentary seats in 2024. By May, the Greens’ rise seemed astronomic – they briefly polled as high as Labour and the center-right Conservatives, the two parties which have dominated British politics for decades, and enjoyed historic gains in spring local elections.

While Polanski has tried to link the climate crisis to other issues, he has largely prioritized immediate everyday concerns, such as the cost of living and suggestions of public ownership of water and other utilities, alongside other progressive initiatives like championing a wealth tax and rent controls, while also adopting a pro-Palestinian stance.

Polanski has claimed credit for pushing Labour further to the left, most recently saying his party was responsible for influencing Labour’s shifting stance on the Middle East, including the government’s recently announced sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Actor turned politician

A former actor, Polanski’s strength lies in his communication. He hosts his own nightclub nights and holds weekly conversations with academics, activists and journalists on his podcast “Bold Politics” on ideas like an extreme wealth line (a proposed globally agreed limit for an individual’s net worth), re-nationalizing water companies and rejoining the European Union.

But he is prone to slip-ups too – in one disastrous interview shortly after becoming leader he seemed to confuse the national debt and deficit. Months later, he more carefully laid out his economic policy at a left-wing think tank event, though it remains “vague,” said Laura Serra, a political scientist at the London School of Economics.

“People don’t really know what they (the Greens) stand for, what they’re going to do,” she added.

While Polanski’s almost constant media presence has given him a far higher profile than previous Green leaders, analysts argue that the party’s increasing popularity has less to do with him and more to do with the shifting political climate in the UK.

A Green Party sign displayed outside a house. Carl Court/Getty Images

And at the same time, Green parties across Europe have become more influential, propelled by growing support among recent graduates and benefiting from “changing societal cleavages,” said James Dennison, a political scientist at the European University in Florence, who has studied the Greens for more than a decade. “The change is more rapid in the UK, and it’s exaggerated partially because of the electoral system, so it takes them longer to break through, and when they do, they go faster.”

Polanski self-consciously forms part of a wider populist trend too; he describes his approach to messaging as “substance with clickbait” and an alternative designed directly to confront the right-wing populism of Reform, and its Trump-supporting leader Nigel Farage.

“Populism is about the 99%, the vast majority… against the very, very wealthy… Trump and Farage come from the 1% and want to protect the interests of the elite,” Polanski told Bloomberg earlier this year.

This simultaneous rise of the Greens and Reform could fracture Britain’s political landscape, in which the first-past-the-post electoral system typically favors two or three major parties.

So, regardless of who wins on Thursday, the Greens even being competitive in a traditional Labour stronghold like this is indicative of how the smaller, more radical parties are increasingly challenging the mainstream.

World.title: What is pneumonic plague and how dangerous is it?
World.content:
A 28-year-old lab researcher at a Russian institute dedicated to studying plague and dangerous pathogens died of pneumonia of an “unknown” origin.

The Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute operates in Siberia, where several other people are quarantined. Rospotrebnadzor, the Russian agency that oversees infectious disease, has downplayed the link between the researcher’s death and her work, but the case has prompted questions about the type of plague that causes pneumonia.

The US State Department and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said they are monitoring the situation closely. The World Health Organization said Monday it’s in contact with Russian health authorities to verify what happened, what testing is underway and any potential international public health implications.

“Based on unofficial information available, the public health risk to the general population appears to be low,” a WHO spokesperson said, adding that its risk assessment would be updated once more information was available.

What is pneumonic plague?

Pneumonic plague is a rare, deadly lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. Scientists consider pneumonic plague the most dangerous form of the infection.

There are other forms of plague stemming from Y. pestis that attack different parts of the body.

The most common form, bubonic plague, often develops after a flea bite or when the bacterium enters through a cut or break in the skin. The infection triggers swollen, painful lymph nodes and can progress to septicemic plague.

Septicemic plague infects the bloodstream, potentially leading to organ failure, it can also come directly from a flea bite.

Pharyngeal plague attacks the throat after someone eats infected meat.

The bacteria Yersinia pestis causes plague, including the most common, bubonic plague, which typically results from the bite of an infected flea. Pneumonic plague is the most serious form of the illness. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Getty Images

How is pneumonic plague transmitted?

Pneumonic plague is the only form of the bacterial infection that passes directly from person to person. Respiratory particles carry it when a person coughs or sneezes. Droplets from infected animals can also transmit it.

The last documented person-to-person transmission of pneumonic plague in the United States dates back to 1924, during an outbreak in Los Angeles.

What are pneumonic plague symptoms?

With pneumonic plague, particles lodge in the lungs and can trigger severe pneumonia, making breathing difficult. Symptoms can begin within 24 hours of infection.

Other symptoms include fever, chills, headache, body aches, dizziness, weakness, fatigue, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.

Without treatment, it is nearly always deadly.

How is pneumonic plague treated?

Doctors can treat plague with at least 10 to 14 days of antibiotics. Most commonly they use ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, gentamicin, and streptomycin. Patients that get antibiotics within the first 24 hours of infection have the best chance of surviving.

Doctors may also support someone with supportive care and provide supplemental oxygen, fluids and encouragement to rest.

Is there a vaccine for plague?

Although plague vaccines have been in use since the 19th century, it wasn’t clear they offer protection from pneumonic plague.

The WHO doesn’t recommend vaccination, except for high-risk groups such as laboratory personnel who are constantly exposed to the risk of contamination.

Why does plague still happen today?

Although people may be most familiar with plague from reading the Bible or historical literature — or as a metaphor to describe broader pestilence and poverty, according to infectious disease expert Dr. Tyler Evans — it persists today.

Known as the “Black Death” in the 14th century, the infection killed more than 50 million people in Europe. While antibiotics have made it more manageable, it remains present on every continent except Oceania.

Since the 1990s, most human cases have occurred in Africa, according to the WHO.

The last US death from pneumonic plague occurred in Arizona in July 2025, according to the CDC . The young man worked with sick cats and is believed to have contracted the infection from the animals. No one else exposed to the cats reported getting sick.

Evans, who wrote “Pandemics, Poverty and Politics: Decoding the Social and Political Drivers of Pandemics from Plague to Covid-19,” says the risk for plague is “getting worse as the result of ecological changes and particularly with the US pulling back on our public health infrastructure and measures.”

Plague, at least, can be quick to diagnose, he said. And “the antibiotics, first and second line, are very effective for this.”

Soldiers monitored a hospital in India, on September 27, 1994, during an outbreak of pneumonic plague. The soldiers were posted after more than 50 people escaped quarantine. John Moore/AP/File

Globally, how concerned do people need to be about getting sick?

WHO has said the risk to the general population appears to be low.

People with pneumonic plague feel sick very quickly, which can slow potential spread, according to Dr. Rutul Dalal, an infectious disease physician at Penn State Health St. Joseph Medical Center.

“It’s very difficult for someone to even walk, do their daily activities, let alone travel,” Dalal said. People can develop symptoms as early as 24 hours after exposure.

There are no direct flights between Russia and the US, he said, so by the time an infected person would reach the US they would likely already be exhibiting symptoms.

“Of course, you have to be careful, and you should keep this at the back of your mind … The world is a little village now, as I say — connected to each other. But at this point in time, compared to what we have been seeing, like during the Covid pandemic, this is not of that magnitude as of now, and hopefully remains contained as it is.”

For people around patients with plague, WHO recommends avoiding direct contact with those who are sick and urges caution around infected body fluids.

Workers caring for patients with pneumonic plague must wear standard protective equipment and may also take preventive antibiotics.

In case of exposure, health officials will also monitor family members and other close contacts of an infected person and provide them with antibiotics before they become ill. They also recommend routine hand-washing with soap and water.

World.title: Liberia: Jury Returns Mixed Verdict, Kemayah, Sirleaf, Kollie and Bility Guilty
World.content:
Judge Ousman Feika Rejects Defense Submission Before Closing Arguments; His Prediction of a Supreme Court Challenge Raises Courtroom Questions

Monrovia- A jury at Criminal Court “C” in Monrovia has returned a series of guilty, not-guilty and inconclusive verdicts in the high-profile Saudi-donated rice trial, marking a dramatic development in a case involving former senior government officials accused of criminal wrongdoing in the handling of humanitarian rice donated to Liberia by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

The verdicts followed the final arguments by prosecution and defense lawyers on Friday, bringing the trial to a critical juncture in a case that has attracted national attention because of the identities of the defendants and the humanitarian purpose of the donated commodity.



Among the defendants reported guilty on the principal charges were former Foreign Affairs Minister Dee-Maxwell Saah Kemayah, former Internal Affairs Minister Varney A. Sirleaf, National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA) disaster-victim official Augustine Kollie, and former General Services Agency (GSA) Deputy Director Edris Idris Bility.

Other defendants, including former NDMA Executive Director Henry O. Williams and former GSA official Memmie Davie Larmie, were reported not guilty on all five charges in the information supplied from the proceedings.

However, the jury’s decisions were not uniform across all defendants. Some individuals received mixed verdicts, while other charges ended in inconclusive or hung verdicts because jurors did not reach the necessary agreement.

The results, as reported from the courtroom, underscore the jury’s differing assessments of the allegations against the various defendants.

Feika Rejects Defense Lawyer’s Submission Before Final Arguments

Before the commencement of final arguments, Criminal Court “C” Judge Ousman F. Feika reportedly denied an attempt by defense counsel Cllr. Jimmy Saah Bombo to make a submission to the court.

Judge Feika indicated that the submission was not appropriate at that stage of the proceedings and should have been made earlier.

The ruling placed the defense lawyer’s request outside the court’s preferred procedural timeline immediately before the parties presented their final arguments to the jury.

What reportedly astonished observers was Judge Feika’s assertion, made even before the conclusion of final arguments and the jury’s deliberations, that the lawyer would take the matter to the Supreme Court.

That statement, as described by courtroom observers, raised questions about the timing and context of the judge’s remarks, particularly because the jury had yet to deliberate and return its decisions.

Whether the exchange will become the subject of a formal challenge remains to be established. Any assessment of the judge’s conduct or the legal significance of the denied submission would require the precise wording of the request, the court’s ruling, and the applicable procedural rules.

Nevertheless, the episode added another point of contention to an already consequential trial, with the defense and prosecution preparing to conclude their presentations in a case carrying significant public interest.

Jurors Deliberate Behind Masks As High-Profile Defendants Await Outcome

Before the trial proceedings began, jurors were reportedly observed wearing masks intended to conceal their identities.

The arrangement underscored the sensitivity surrounding a prosecution involving former government officials and allegations concerning the handling of humanitarian assistance.

The jury was tasked with evaluating charges that included theft of property, economic sabotage, misapplication of entrusted property, abuse of office and criminal conspiracy.

At the heart of the prosecution’s case was the handling of 29,412 bags of rice donated by Saudi Arabia, reportedly valued at approximately US$500,000 and intended to assist disaster-affected and vulnerable Liberians.

The prosecution alleged that substantial quantities of the donated rice were improperly handled, diverted or misapplied. The defense, however, challenged aspects of the prosecution’s account, including the circumstances surrounding transfers between government institutions and the evidence linking individual defendants to criminal conduct.

The competing accounts placed the jury in the position of determining whether the evidence established each charge against each defendant.

Kemayah Reported Guilty Despite Dissenting Jurors

Former Foreign Affairs Minister Dee-Maxwell Saah Kemayah was reported guilty on all five charges: theft of property, economic sabotage, misapplication of entrusted property, abuse of office and criminal conspiracy.

The reported vote breakdown indicates that four of the 12 jurors voted not guilty on theft of property, four opposed a guilty finding on economic sabotage, three voted not guilty on misapplication of entrusted property, and four voted not guilty on criminal conspiracy. All 12 reportedly voted guilty on abuse of office.

These figures suggest substantial disagreement within the jury despite the reported guilty outcomes.

The precise legal status of each finding, including whether the verdicts satisfied the applicable requirements for a valid jury verdict, should be confirmed against the official court record.

Kemayah had maintained his defense during the trial, with the proceedings examining his role in facilitating the Saudi donation and the subsequent movement and distribution of the rice.

The outcome, if confirmed by the court record, would represent a major development for a former senior diplomat whose involvement in securing the donation placed him at the center of the controversy.

Sirleaf And Kollie Reported Guilty On All Five Charges

Former Internal Affairs Minister Varney A. Sirleaf was reported guilty on all five charges.

Augustine Kollie, identified in the proceedings as an NDMA official responsible for disaster victims, was likewise reported guilty on all five charges.

The findings against the two officials are particularly significant because the NDMA was central to the management of the donated commodity and the humanitarian response for which it was intended.

During the trial, Sirleaf disputed allegations concerning Kemayah’s role in directing the transfer of rice from the NDMA to the GSA. He maintained that the movement of the commodity resulted from an inter-agency decision and cited storage and inventory concerns.

The jury’s reported decision indicates that the prosecution’s allegations against Sirleaf resulted in guilty findings on each of the five listed charges. The court record will be necessary to establish the precise verdict language and any associated vote counts.

Kollie’s reported guilty verdicts similarly place the NDMA’s handling of the donated rice at the center of the case’s outcome.

Henry Williams And Memmie Larmie Reported Not Guilty

Former NDMA Executive Director Henry O. Williams was reported not guilty on all five charges.

The charges were theft of property, economic sabotage, misapplication of entrusted property, abuse of office and criminal conspiracy.

Memmie Davie Larmie was also reported not guilty on all five charges.

The outcomes demonstrate that the jury did not reach identical conclusions about all the officials whose names were associated with the handling of the Saudi donation.

Williams’ reported acquittals are particularly notable given his position at the NDMA, the agency central to the custody and distribution of the rice.

His defense had to be considered against allegations involving the movement of the commodity, institutional responsibilities and the conduct attributed to individual officials.

The reported not-guilty findings should not be conflated with the outcomes for other defendants. Each accused person’s criminal responsibility must be assessed separately according to the verdicts entered in the record.

Bility Reported Guilty; Siafa Receives Mixed Findings

Former GSA Deputy Director Edris Idris Bility was reported guilty on all five charges.

Bility had previously presented gate passes that he said documented the release of 5,000 bags of rice intended for Gbarnga, arguing that the commodity left the GSA warehouse through a documented process rather than being secretly removed.

The jury’s reported findings mark a significant development in the allegations surrounding the movement and documentation of the rice.

Wayne Siafa, identified in the supplied notes as a former chief executive, received a different set of reported outcomes.

He was reported not guilty of theft of property, economic sabotage and criminal conspiracy, but guilty of misapplication of entrusted property. The abuse-of-office charge reportedly ended in a hung verdict.

That mixed result illustrates the importance of distinguishing individual charges rather than describing every defendant as either wholly guilty or wholly acquitted.

A hung verdict does not constitute a finding of guilt or innocence on the unresolved charge. Its legal consequences depend on the court’s subsequent proceedings and applicable law.

Achievgo Doe And Thelma Duncan Sawyer: Inconclusive Votes On Some Charges

Achievgo Doe and former Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister Thelma Duncan Sawyer were reported not guilty on several charges, with inconclusive voting on others.

According to the supplied courtroom notes, the theft charge against Doe was recorded as not guilty, although one juror reportedly favored a guilty finding. On economic sabotage and misapplication of entrusted property, two jurors reportedly voted guilty in each instance, while the recorded outcome was not guilty.

The abuse-of-office charge ended without a conclusive verdict, with five jurors reportedly voting guilty and six voting not guilty. On criminal conspiracy, four reportedly voted guilty and eight not guilty.

The notes supplied for Sawyer contain a similar breakdown: not-guilty outcomes on theft, economic sabotage, misapplication of entrusted property and criminal conspiracy, alongside a hung verdict on abuse of office.

These counts require confirmation because the reported totals do not always account for all 12 jurors. The exact verdicts should therefore be checked against the official record before publication as definitive legal findings.

Other Defendants: Mixed And Unresolved Outcomes

The supplied notes also identify Rosetta Goah as having been found guilty of theft of property, economic sabotage, misapplication of entrusted property and criminal conspiracy, while the abuse-of-office charge reportedly ended in a hung verdict.

Everlyn Gbee was reported not guilty on the listed charges, although one juror reportedly voted guilty on theft of property.

Momolu Johnson was reported guilty on all five charges.

The opening summary also lists former officials and other defendants whose individual verdicts require further verification, including Edward Konneh and Momolu Duckly. The available notes do not provide a consistent, complete charge-by-charge breakdown for every named individual.

Consequently, the final list of convictions, acquittals and unresolved counts should be established from the court’s official verdict sheets rather than inferred from the preliminary information.

The Bigger Question: What Happened To The Saudi-Donated Rice?

Beyond the individual verdicts, the trial has centered on a fundamental question: whether the movement and distribution of humanitarian rice intended for vulnerable Liberians involved criminal conduct, administrative decisions, or a combination of disputed actions and failures of oversight.

The donation comprised 29,412 bags of rice, valued at approximately US$500,000. Prosecutors alleged that thousands of bags were stolen, diverted or improperly handled. Defense witnesses disputed aspects of that account and described transfers between government agencies as institutional decisions.

The jury’s reported decisions appear to distinguish between defendants and, in some cases, between individual charges. That distinction matters because allegations involving a shared government operation do not automatically establish the criminal responsibility of every person connected to it.

The verdicts also leave important questions concerning the unresolved counts and the precise legal consequences of the jury’s findings.

For Liberians concerned about accountability, the case is about more than the fate of former officials. It is also about whether humanitarian assistance intended for disaster victims reached its intended beneficiaries and whether public institutions can account for the resources entrusted to them.

A Consequential Day For Liberia’s Justice System

Friday’s proceedings at Criminal Court “C” brought the Saudi Rice Trial to a decisive point after weeks of testimony, documentary evidence and competing explanations of the rice’s movement through government institutions.

The reported outcomes include guilty findings against several prominent officials, complete acquittals for others, and unresolved charges where the jury reportedly failed to reach agreement.

Judge Feika’s reported rejection of Cllr. Bombo’s submission before final arguments, together with the judge’s reported prediction of a Supreme Court challenge, also warrants careful examination against the courtroom record.

The next critical step is confirmation of the formal verdicts, clarification of the hung counts and any subsequent rulings or sentencing proceedings.

For now, the central message from the courtroom is that the jury’s reported findings were mixed: several defendants face guilty verdicts, others were cleared of the listed charges, and some allegations remain unresolved. The official court record must determine the final legal position of each defendant.
