World.title: Colombia declares official start of El Niño, warns of strong impacts
World.content:
Colombia’s meteorological institute IDEAM officially declared the arrival of El Niño, and warned that the climate phenomenon could trigger water shortages and forest fires.

In a press statement, the IDEAM said that its “confirmation reflects the sustained warm conditions in the Pacific Ocean, which, according to the latest measurement, broke records, reaching a sea surface temperature anomaly of +3.49°C.”

The meteorological institute said it expected that this year’s “Godzilla El Niño” could continue to disrupt local climate patterns until March next year.

Initially, the weather phenomenon is expected to reduce rainfall between October and December, which is normally the rainy season in large parts of the country.

“Given this situation, and in light of the alerts issued since the beginning of the year, the national government launched an interagency response,.. with specific instructions for the responsible agencies to have their contingency plans formulated and activated by November 30 at the latest,” said the President’s Office in a statement.

The National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) coordinates response capabilities across the country and enhances the monitoring of wildfires using satellite technology. For its part, the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development is taking steps to protect strategic ecosystems, water sources, and the most vulnerable areas. President’s Office

The Mining Ministry “is implementing an emergency plan aimed at ensuring the country’s energy security by strengthening thermal power generation, securing fuel supplies, and implementing efficiency and conservation measures,” according to the President’s Office.

EPM, the local utilities firm in Medellin, has been testing the effectiveness of water rations as they fear the lack of rain could affect the hydro-electric power plants that provide the northwest of Colombia much of its energy.

Before leaving office on August 7, former President Gustavo Petro ordered the mass purchase of solar panels to reduce the pressure on the electric grid.

World.title: Colombia’s draft counterterrorist statute “creates foundations of dictatorial and inquisitorial regime:” opposition
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella’s antiterrorist statute would criminalize political opposition, social movements, and social protest, and essentially form a dictatorial regime, said opposition leader Ivan Cepeda on Wednesday.

In a video, Cepeda said that the true purpose of the bill that was leaked earlier seeks “to advance in the formation of essentially a dictatorial regime,.. which, moreover, has such a regime prostrate to drug trafficking.”

“The true objectives of this statute are to wage a crusade against the political opposition, social movements, and social protest, which is a legitimate right of citizens,” said the Senator of the Historic Pact party.

“Most of the articles in this draft are devoted to provisions that seriously undermine civil liberties, human rights, and the right to protest—not to illegal armed groups,’ according to Cepeda.

The broad legal definition of the word terrorism would allow the government to prosecute protest organizers on terrorism charges if any clashes occur between protesters and police.

This law could serve to intensify the persecution already underway in Colombia against journalists, judges, students, teachers, union members, peasants, indigenous people, people of African descent, LGBTIQ+ individuals—in short, any person or group that criticizes the citizen Abelardo de la Espriella, his government, law enforcement, or any state institution. Such a person could be taken to prison—without even prior warning—and subjected to abuse and torture. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Furthermore, the creation of a National Registry of Terrorist Organizations and Actors would allow the government to criminalize citizens based on an administrative rather than a legal basis, and “grants extraordinary powers to the president to regulate a statutory judicial procedure, specifically the expedited preventive detention proceeding,” said the opposition leader.

The aim is to criminalize social protest; the alleged crime of “manipulating the civilian population” punishes anyone who promotes, finances, organizes, or leads crowds—this is the language of the draft statute—and this is nothing less than the institutionalization of political persecution and the criminalization of free speech. Senator Ivan Cepeda

The antiterrorism statute will be facing opposition when the government tries to push the legislation through Congress, Cepeda said.

“The Historic Pact rejects this and will do whatever is necessary to ensure that the opposition’s rights and guarantees are respected,” said the opposition leader.

World.title: De la Espriella announces first $309M in aid for earthquake reconstruction
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella announced that his Miracle Fund received COP1 trillion ($309 million) for the reconstruction of western Colombia, which was hit by a 7.4M earthquake on August 10.

The announcement followed announcements by the press, which reported that the Finance Ministry allocated ($192 million) COP625 billion to the fund almost two months after the disaster.

Thank you for your patience, but please understand that the government’s bureaucratic inertia and the situation we’ve inherited are extremely complex. However, we’re working to resolve the issue, and the Milagro Fund is now up and running, thanks to God and the efforts of all the officials in this administration. President Abelardo de la Espriella

“In November, the government will move forward with contracting another COP2.7 trillion ($835 million),” Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo told Caracol Radio.

The money is the first of an estimated COP30 trillion ($9.3 billion) that would be needed to rebuild the damage to airports, roads, hospitals and other public works.

The fund will be managed by De la Espriella’s general secretary, Carlos Rios, and a handful of businessmen with ties to the administration.

The announcement followed increased unrest about the government’s lack of response to the earthquake, which affected more than 400,000 people in the Valle del Cauca and Choco province, and the coffee region.

The government’s initial response was delayed because De la Espriella suspended the process to transfer power a month before he took office on August 7.

World.title: Colombia seeks to expand definition of terrorism in draft “counterterrorism statute”
World.content:
The government of President Abelardo de la Espriella will present Colombia’s Congress with a comprehensive “counterterrorism statute,” which would give authorities enhanced powers to fight designated terrorist organizations.

A 116-page draft bill, which was leaked to Caracol Radio, would facilitate a military approach to combat illegal armed groups and organized crime groups, for example through air strikes.

The Antiterrorism Statute would additionally create a National Registry of Terrorist Organizations and Actors, which would make it easier to freeze the assets of suspected terrorists and their financiers.

Last but not least, the bill creates a presidential Terrorism Commissioner and a special prison regime for leaders of designated terrorist organizations.

Broader definition of terrorism

The bill seeks to change Colombia’s criminal law and define terrorism as any individual or collective conduct that produces “fear, panic or terror, creating risks, threats or the use of violence.”

A technical body of the National Security Council (NSC) will advise the council on the inclusion of organizations or individuals that ought to be included to its public National Registry of Terrorist Organizations and Actors.

Anyone who believes he was falsely put on the terror list can challenge this decision before the NSC and the Council of State, Colombia’s top administrative court.

The bill additionally seeks that “the Council of State shall hear, in the first instance, constitutional protection lawsuits filed against the President of the Republic or against defense authorities for acts or omissions related to operations by law enforcement agencies to preserve national security.”

This would make the suspension of military operations more difficult for citizens, who now can seek legal support to protect their constitutional rights at lower courts.

The bill also creates new crimes and modifies the penalties for conduct related to “terrorism,” such as the use of drones, illegal mining, oil theft, the extraction and sale of gold, kidnapping, smuggling, human trafficking, drug trafficking, extortion, cybercrimes, election crimes, riots, and attacks on critical infrastructure.

In the case of riots, “the penalty shall be increased by up to double when the riot is directed against law enforcement units conducting operations; or is carried out in conjunction with listed terrorist organizations.”

The bill also allows Colombian authorities to investigate and prosecute terrorism, terrorism financing or providing material support for terrorist organizations abroad.

High Counterterrorism Commissioner

The bill additionally seeks to expand presidential powers to create the Office of the High Counterterrorism Commissioner.

The expanded power would additionally give De la Espriella six months to regulate the powers of this new advisory office and to appoint its first commissioner.

World.title: Mayor from Colombia’s north claims De la Espriella’s armed men intimidated him
World.content:
The mayor of Sincelejo claimed Sunday that armed men intimidated him during a meeting with Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a video message, Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña said that armed men positioned themselves behind him while the president accused the mayor of corruption and threatened to pull municipal funds.

The accusations were partly published on the social media pages of the president, who accused Acuña of being “a person who, like you, faces 13 corruption charges, has a video in which he explains how to embezzle funds from the PAE, and, on top of that, is set to stand trial in the Supreme Court of Justice on charges of illicit enrichment.”

So let’s see what we do with Sincelejo, but I do not work under your scheme of corruption. And if you think you can continue engaging in those practices, know that someone has arrived who is going to prevent it and that I am going to concentrate on it. This money, mister mayor, I will take care of it, and to take care of it I have to keep it away from your control. President Abelardo de la Espriella

In his response, Acuña claimed that De la Espriella’s video “has been edited and digitally manipulated.”

I ask you, please, to show the full video, where you can see how disciplinary and criminal codes are being violated in Colombia, where you can see how a mayor is being intimidated with rifles in the hands of civilians. How can a mayor be constantly flanked—for the entire duration of an event—by a person armed with a rifle, with the sole purpose of intimidating him? Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

Investigative journalist Laura Ardila said on social media platform X that sources from the province confirmed Acuña’s allegations.

Sources from the department who were present say—fearing they might be named—that they left the scene terrified. They claim that Acuña was indeed surrounded by heavily armed men in civilian clothing, that the president’s office was recording the entire time, and that, based on details like these, they believe it was a scene staged in advance to go viral. Journalist Laura Ardila

The mayor subsequently pointed out that the investigations into his alleged corruption existed before the presidential campaign, during which the De la Espriella campaign may have violated electoral laws, according to Acuña.

Among other things, the mayor said that he had been approached by De la Espriella’s parents to support the far-right president’s campaign and that local print shops may have received unreported campaign funds.

Since this needs to be clarified, mister President, it would be a good idea for the oversight agencies to investigate whether any printing shops in Sincelejo incurred campaign expenses that have not yet been reported to the National Electoral Council, whether there was campaign financing, and where that campaign financing came from, Mister President. Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

The mayor also pointed out that two members of the De la Espriella administration are being investigated on corruption charges and that the president had ties to the now-defunct paramilitary organization AUC.

The president has repeatedly used corruption allegations to target political enemies.

World.title: Colombia’s top corporate lobbyist resigns over reported tensions with president
World.content:
The director of one of Colombia’s most powerful business associations, Bruce Mac Master of the ANDI, resigned amid tensions with President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a letter to the ANDI, Mac Master said that “it is time for me to step down from my role as head of the National Association of Entrepreneurs of Colombia.”

According to the former ANDI boss, “unexpected and troubling circumstances” made working for the association “particularly complex” and ‘multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously.”

In recent weeks, unexpected and troubling circumstances have arisen that have made the Association’s operating environment particularly complex, with potential adverse effects on its members and staff. Multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously. In the face of these challenges, I have sought to act with firmness and prudence, always prioritizing institutional channels and placing the interests of the ANDI above any personal considerations, in an effort to resolve this situation. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master’s resignation followed news suggesting that De la Espriella instructed his cabinet of boycotting the ANDI chief.

According to political news magazine La Silla Vacia, the rift between the ANDI and the government was because De la Espriella’s law firm was never allowed to join the ANDI and the association’s donations in response to the august 10 earthquake bypassed the First Lady’s newly founded and very controversial foundation.

“The General Board of Directors, its Executive Committee, and I did everything in our power to facilitate a solution and create conditions that would allow the Association to fully fulfill its role, seeking to keep channels of dialogue open and to continue contributing,” but “all of those attempts were unsuccessful.”

I deeply regret this, because I have always believed in collective intelligence and in the need for the government, the private sector, and institutions to work together—even in the face of differences—with respect, independence, and a sense of national responsibility. We tried, but we were unsuccessful. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master said that he hoped that his resignation would restore “collaboration between the national government and the business community—as represented by the General Board of Directors, the members, and the various divisions of the Association.”

The former ANDI chief had been trying to represent the business interests of its approximately 1,600 members since 2013.

World.title: Colombia seeks to tighten checks on public protests
World.content:
Colombia’s government published a draft decree that seeks to tighten regulations on public protests.

The draft was published weeks before labor unions and social organizations plan regional anti-government protests ahead of a national strike that is set for November.

The draft seeks to update the Decree #3 of 2021, which was issued months before a national strike that was violently repressed by the police and the military.

In an attempt to prevent another bloodbath, the decree seeks to regulate authorities’ response to protests and the coordinated use of force in response to acts of vandalism and violence.

The decree regulates dialogue between the protesters and law enforcement authorities to promote the peaceful nature of protests.

The decree additionally limits the use of police intelligence against those organizing and participating in the protests.

Last but not least, the decree seeks the effective prosecution of those arrested during protests through increased surveillance and a permanent police presence.

The decree comes amid social tensions that surged after the far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and announced counterrevolutionary measures that seek to undo reforms by his leftist predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro.

Swelling student protests have been publicly accused of being fueled by insurgencies and De la Espriella has warned that police may enter universities if they find evidence they are used to prepare acts of vandalism or terrorism.

World.title: Colombia breaks diplomatic ties with Iran
World.content:
Colombia’s Foreign Ministry said Thursday that it had broken diplomatic ties with Iran and designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

The foreign ministry made the announcements in two separate statements that were published in its website.

In the first statement, the government claimed that the decision claimed to defend “national and hemispheric security, and the fight against transnational crime.”

According to the foreign ministry, the Iranian government has “alleged ties to international terrorist groups and other narco-terrorist groups that threaten [Colombia’s] security.”

Colombia also took into account the documented human rights violations committed by the Iranian government on its territory, the verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities’ obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran’s nuclear program. Foreign Ministry

In regards to the IRGC, the foreign ministry claimed that the Iranian armed force “poses a serious threat to international peace and security” through “covert operations beyond Iran’s borders.”

“Colombia will strengthen its control and security measures to prevent individuals associated with the IRGC from entering its territory,” said the foreign ministry in a second statement.

In his 2017 book “Watch Your Backyard,” Foreign Minister Omar Bula claimed that “Iran and Islamic extremist groups such a Hezbollah and Al Qaeda have profusely penetrated Latin America.”

As part of his foreign policy, President Abelardo de la Espriella has renewed ties with the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

In a response, the Iranian government said that the accusations of the De la Espriella government go “against the principles of mutual respect” and damage both countries’ “interests and benefits.”

“It is clear that none of the arguments put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this measure was adopted solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States,” said Iran’s foreign ministry.

World.title: Trump says Russia will supply millions of tonnes of diesel as US eases sanctions on Moscow
World.content:
Trump says Russia will supply millions of tonnes of diesel as US eases sanctions on Moscow

9th Friday, October 2026 - 22:44 UTC Full article

”Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!” he wrote

US President Donald Trump announced on Friday a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin for Russia to supply some 4.8 million tonnes of diesel to US and global markets, aiming to curb rising fuel prices. To make it possible, the Treasury Department temporarily suspended sanctions on Russian diesel until April 2027.

“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the American and global marketplace, another 500,000 tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 tons immediately thereafter,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. He added that, depending on the condition of its refineries, Russia would deliver a further three million tonnes “within a short period of time”.

“Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!” he wrote, saying that lowering prices for farmers, ranchers and truckers was his “greatest priority”. Putin’s investment envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, said energy cooperation between the two countries “will continue and benefit global markets”.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the deal “a weak decision” and “dishonest”, made while a Ukrainian delegation is negotiating a peace agreement in Florida with Trump’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. “I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen,” he said. “This means millions, billions. All of it goes to the war against Ukraine.”

Russia, one of the world’s main diesel suppliers, had suspended exports of the fuel because of damage caused by Ukrainian drones to its refineries. The suspension was due to expire at the end of October.

US diesel prices hit a record on September 22 and stood at US$6.27 a gallon on Friday; futures fell 4.3% after the announcement. The increase has been exacerbated by the war with Iran, which has disrupted crude flows and refining capacity. A week ago, the G7 agreed to release 100 million barrels from strategic reserves. The cost of living is one of the central issues in the November 3 midterm elections.

World.title: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake shakes Panama
World.content:
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake shakes Panama

9th Friday, October 2026 - 22:38 UTC Full article

The epicentre was about 14 kilometres southwest of Pitaloza Arriba, a sparsely populated area near the Pacific coast some 240 kilometres from the capital, at shallow depth

A magnitude 7.7 earthquake shook Panama on Friday at 12:56 local time, centred on the Azuero peninsula in Herrera province, according to the US Geological Survey. Panamanian authorities have not so far confirmed any casualties, though inspections are continuing and they have not ruled out injuries or people trapped. Damage to buildings was reported in several provinces.

The epicentre was about 14 kilometres southwest of Pitaloza Arriba, a sparsely populated area near the Pacific coast some 240 kilometres from the capital, at shallow depth. Panama’s Institute of Geosciences estimated the magnitude at 7.2. Its director, Néstor Luque, attributed the quake to the Azuero-Sona fault system, which had been accumulating stress for some time. More than 30 aftershocks were recorded.

The National Civil Protection System reported damage in Penonomé, in Coclé province, including to the cathedral of San Juan Bautista, the governor’s office and a hotel, as well as in Chitré and Venao. Its director, Omar Smith, warned that aftershocks would continue, though with decreasing intensity.

The Education Ministry cancelled afternoon classes nationwide, public offices were closed, water supply was cut in some areas because of power failures and Tocumen international airport temporarily suspended operations. The Panama Canal Authority said the waterway was operating normally.

The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center issued an alert for the coasts of Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico, which was lifted hours later. Smith had considered a tsunami unlikely because the epicentre was on land. In Chile, the navy declared a precautionary alert for Easter Island and lifted it after the magnitude, initially estimated at 8.0, was revised. The quake was felt in the Colombian cities of Medellín and Cartagena.

President José Raúl Mulino called for calm and asked emergency agencies for a report on the effects. “What has happened must not be used to generate alarm and disorder,” he wrote.

The earthquake comes two months after a magnitude 7.4 quake that killed 335 people in Colombia’s Chocó department on August 10.

World.title: US sanctions the International Criminal Court hours after a former judge wins the Nobel Peace Prize
World.content:
US sanctions the International Criminal Court hours after a former judge wins the Nobel Peace Prize

9th Friday, October 2026 - 20:53 UTC Full article

Pillay, 85, sat on the court’s Appeals Chamber from 2003 to 2008, presided over the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and was UN High Commissioner for Human Rights from 2008 to 2014

Donald Trump’s administration on Friday imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court as an institution, hours after the Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the Nobel Peace Prize to South African jurist Navi Pillay, a former judge of the court, “for her efforts to promote peace and international law”.

“President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans,” said Secretary of State Marco Rubio. “We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate.” The sanctions cut the court off from the US financial system and extend to those who work with it. Until now, Washington had sanctioned 13 of its judges and prosecutors. Rubio said the measures were designed to give the court and its member states time to address US concerns, and warned that if allies do not “rein in” the court, the United States will continue “its campaign to dismantle the ICC, brick by brick”.

The Hague-based court called the decision “an attempt to obstruct the course of justice” and “an attack on the rule of law and the very foundations of the international legal order”, in a statement signed by its president, Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington in August. The European Union called it “deeply regrettable”, said it would work with the court to ensure it keeps functioning and hoped there was room for dialogue before the sanctions take effect in six months. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, against whom the court issued an arrest warrant in 2024 for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, congratulated the United States and called the court “a political body”.

Pillay, 85, sat on the court’s Appeals Chamber from 2003 to 2008, presided over the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and was UN High Commissioner for Human Rights from 2008 to 2014. The Nobel Committee presented the award as a message to those seeking to undermine international legal institutions. Pillay dedicated it to survivors of international crimes.

Trump has repeatedly said he deserves the Nobel Peace Prize. The 2025 laureate, Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, gave him her medal at the White House in January.

More than 120 states are party to the Rome Statute, including every country in South America. The United States is not.

World.title: A mudslide sweeps away cars and a bus in Santiago after the wettest October on record
World.content:
A mudslide sweeps away cars and a bus in Santiago after the wettest October on record

9th Friday, October 2026 - 20:53 UTC Full article

Las Condes mayor Catalina San Martín put the number of homes with some damage at around 2,000, 55 of them with serious habitability problems

A torrent of water, mud and rocks swept away cars and a public transport bus on Thursday in San Carlos de Apoquindo, in the Las Condes district at the foot of the Andes in eastern Santiago, Chile, after a week of record rainfall. The official toll is six injured, with no deaths or missing, and President José Antonio Kast has declared a disaster zone in the district.

Among the injured is a one-year-old child with a broken leg, according to the presidential delegate for the Metropolitan Region, Germán Codina. More than a thousand people were rescued or assisted and some 200 hectares were affected. Las Condes mayor Catalina San Martín put the number of homes with some damage at around 2,000, 55 of them with serious habitability problems. Water and mud also entered two clinics and the University of the Andes campus.

Momento en comenzó el aluvión en Las Condes. https://t.co/he8miokwcv — Vision País Chile (@visionpaischile) October 8, 2026

Authorities gave successive explanations of the cause. Police initially pointed to an overflowing canal; the national disaster prevention and response service, to the activation of ravines, mountain watercourses that are dry most of the year. Codina later attributed the emergency to the blockage of an underground channel that drains a ravine. The emergency service said it did not send an evacuation alert to mobile phones because it was “a sudden event”, and said its response would be assessed once the emergency was over.

The agency declared a red alert in ten districts of the region, where schools were closed on Friday, and Kast cancelled a ceremony to sign the reconstruction law in order to follow the emergency.

The mudslide capped a week of record-breaking weather driven by an atmospheric river intensified by El Niño. The 52 millimetres that fell on Tuesday 6 were the capital’s highest daily October total in more than a century, and the 74 millimetres accumulated in seven days make this the wettest October on record, ahead of 65 in 1987, according to specialists cited by the Chilean press.

Chile had already suffered a storm in July that left 13 dead and 7 missing, mainly in the Valparaíso, La Araucanía and Biobío regions.

World.title: US plans its first military execution since 1961, by firing squad and livestreamed
World.content:
US plans its first military execution since 1961, by firing squad and livestreamed

9th Friday, October 2026 - 07:48 UTC Full article

Hasan, then an Army major, opened fire with a semi-automatic pistol on November 5, 2009, at a medical centre on the base where soldiers were being prepared for deployment to Afghanistan

The Pentagon will livestream the firing-squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, the military psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009, scheduled for December 3. It will be the first execution carried out by the US armed forces since 1961, the first by firing squad since 1945 and the first publicly broadcast in the country’s history.

“The secretary is right. It will be livestreamed. Details will be released later,” a senior Defense Department official confirmed. The secretary, Pete Hegseth, had announced the plan in an interview with the Human Events Daily programme on the conservative network Real America’s Voice. “We’ll make sure people can see it, that it’s public. Because people need to understand that there are serious consequences for this kind of thing,” he said. Asked about the condemned man’s last wishes, he replied: “I don’t care. We’ll see him on December 3.”

The execution will take place at Fort Hood around 1pm, at the same site and close to the time of the shooting. Military law requires presidential approval for a firing-squad execution; the Pentagon said on Monday that President Donald Trump had given it on Hegseth’s recommendation.

Hasan, then an Army major, opened fire with a semi-automatic pistol on November 5, 2009, at a medical centre on the base where soldiers were being prepared for deployment to Afghanistan. He killed 13 people and wounded 32. A military jury sentenced him to death in August 2013. He represented himself, admitted the attack and said he had “switched sides” to defend the Taliban. He was left paraplegic by police gunfire and is held at the Fort Leavenworth military prison in Kansas. The Supreme Court declined to review his case in March 2025.

The last military execution was that of Private John Bennett, hanged in 1961. In 2008, President George W. Bush approved the execution of Ronald Gray, but a federal court stayed it. The last public execution in the United States took place in 1936 in Owensboro, Kentucky.

Since 1976 only six civilians have been executed by firing squad in the country, three in Utah and three in South Carolina, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. The Trump administration expanded the execution methods authorised for the most serious federal crimes, partly because of difficulties obtaining lethal injection drugs.

World.title: US charges Maduro and Cilia Flores with torture and repression in Venezuela
World.content:
US charges Maduro and Cilia Flores with torture and repression in Venezuela

9th Friday, October 2026 - 07:35 UTC Full article

Maduro and Flores, held since January 3 following a US operation in Caracas and detained at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, have pleaded not guilty to all charges

US federal prosecutors on Thursday brought new torture and repression charges against former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, adding to the drug trafficking and narco-terrorism case both face in a New York court. The same day, the judge denied a request by Flores for house arrest on health grounds.

According to the indictment, between 1999 and 2025 Maduro, Flores and senior officials around them “created and maintained a violent system of repression” in Venezuela, in which thousands of people were detained, tortured or killed by state agents. Prosecutors allege that Maduro “presided over this system”, “ordered the unlawful detention and torture of specific individuals” and received reports on particular prisoners, and that Flores helped develop it. The filing attributes a role to the so-called colectivos — armed civilian groups aligned with chavismo — the FARC guerrilla and the Directorate General of Military Counterintelligence.

The new charges are based on testimony from at least three former senior officials of Maduro’s government, identified in the document by codes, who say they supervised or took part in torture, including of at least three US citizens. According to the indictment, victims suffered beatings, simulated drowning and electric shocks. Former military intelligence chief Hugo Carvajal, a co-defendant in the drug case, pleaded guilty in 2025 and has offered to testify.

Maduro and Flores, held since January 3 following a US operation in Caracas and detained at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, have pleaded not guilty to all charges. Their defence is seeking recognition of head-of-state immunity. Prosecutors respond that the United States never recognised Maduro as president and that acting president Delcy Rodríguez’s government has not sought, through diplomatic channels, either their release or their immunity. The issue will be addressed at a hearing on November 17; the trial is scheduled to begin on June 1, 2027.

Flores’s defence cited heart palpitations, epigastric pain and weight loss of around 11 kilograms, and proposed moving her to a private residence with guards and an electronic tag. Prosecutors opposed the request, citing an “extreme risk of flight” and saying she has refused some medical tests. The judge rejected the request but did not rule out revisiting it if her health deteriorates.

The UN Human Rights Council’s fact-finding mission has documented human rights violations in Venezuela committed since 2014.

World.title: Why Argentina's Falklands sanctions do not automatically reach Sea Lion's operator
World.content:
Why Argentina's Falklands sanctions do not automatically reach Sea Lion's operator

8th Thursday, October 2026 - 08:29 UTC Full article

Photo: Raphael WOLLMANN / Getty Images

The sanctions Argentina has imposed on companies involved in the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands target specific entities rather than entire corporate groups, so the subsidiary currently operating the field is not automatically covered, according to a legal analysis by specialist site Diplomacy & Law.

Argentina's Energy Secretariat declared Rockhopper Exploration plc's activities illegal in 2012 and barred it from operating in the country for 20 years in 2013. In 2022 it imposed a similar sanction on Navitas Petroleum LP. But the project's current operator is Navitas Petroleum Development and Production Ltd, a UK subsidiary of the Israeli group. “A sanction imposed on Navitas Petroleum LP does not automatically become an identical sanction against every affiliated company,” writes the author, Edmarverson A. Santos, unless the law expressly provides for it or a new measure is adopted.

Argentina's legal framework nonetheless reaches beyond licence holders. Law 26,659 of 2011 prohibits direct or indirect participation in hydrocarbon exploration or exploitation that the country regards as unauthorised on its continental shelf, with bans of five to 20 years. Subject to its conditions, it covers shareholders, service providers, financiers, logistics operators and technical advisers. Law 26,915 of 2013 added penalties for directors and companies.

The decree signed by President Javier Milei on September 3 designated the foreign ministry as the enforcing authority, set short deadlines for proceedings and required compliance declarations from those applying for the large-investment incentive regime or hydrocarbon permits in the country. That mechanism explains the effect on companies with business in Argentina: Halliburton, SLB and Baker Hughes have said they will not work on Sea Lion, and Halliburton said the authorities raised criminal and civil enforcement with it.

The analysis distinguishes between making rules and enforcing them. Argentina can deny permits and benefits and sanction those under its jurisdiction, but it cannot exercise coercive authority in the archipelago or another state without an independent legal basis or that country's cooperation. For companies with no ties to Argentina, the risk is mainly reputational or commercial.

None of these measures resolves the underlying question. “Falkland licences cannot establish British title to the islands, and Argentine administrative resolutions cannot establish Argentine title,” the author concludes. The United Kingdom maintains that the activity is legitimate and governed by the archipelago's legislation in accordance with international law; Argentina maintains its sovereignty claim and holds that the licences are invalid.

World.title: What could happen when Argentina's Sea Lion ultimatum to the UK expires
World.content:
What could happen when Argentina's Sea Lion ultimatum to the UK expires

8th Thursday, October 2026 - 08:18 UTC Full article

Milei ordered on September 28 the start of arbitration and said that, if London does not act, Argentina will seek provisional measures from the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea

The two-week deadline Argentina gave the United Kingdom to halt the Sea Lion oil project in the North Falklands basin expires around October 12. Its expiry will not in itself suspend the project or establish a British breach of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, according to a legal analysis published by specialist site Diplomacy & Law.

President Javier Milei ordered on September 28 the start of arbitration under Annex VII of the convention and said that, if London does not act, Argentina will seek provisional measures from the Hamburg-based International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea. The analysis's author, Edmarverson A. Santos, stresses that the deadline was set by Argentina and does not derive from the convention, and that the government's instruction and the formal start of proceedings are separate steps: arbitration begins with written notification to the other state, accompanied by the claim and its grounds. There is no record that this has been sent.

The Annex VII route reflects both countries' choices. Under Article 287 of the convention, Argentina chose the Hamburg tribunal as its first preference and the United Kingdom the International Court of Justice; where the parties do not coincide, the dispute goes to arbitration. Beforehand, Article 283 requires an exchange of views on how to settle the dispute, something a tribunal would have to assess.

If Argentina seeks provisional measures, the Hamburg tribunal could order them while the arbitral tribunal is being constituted, provided it considers that the latter would have prima facie jurisdiction and that the matter is urgent. Such measures would be provisional, not a ruling on sovereignty or the merits.

The main obstacle is jurisdiction. Convention tribunals can only rule on its interpretation or application, not on territorial title. In the 2015 arbitration between Mauritius and the United Kingdom over the Chagos Islands, the tribunal declined to rule on a claim whose real subject was sovereignty; in the 2020 case between Ukraine and Russia, it excluded claims requiring a decision on Crimea, though proceedings continued on the rest. In addition, both countries have made declarations under Article 298: Argentina excluded maritime delimitation disputes, among others, in 1995, and the United Kingdom made exclusions in 2003 and, according to the analysis, again in 2020.

“Argentina would need to formulate claims capable of adjudication under UNCLOS without requiring the tribunal to decide, expressly or implicitly, sovereignty over the Falkland Islands,” the author concludes.

The United Kingdom rejected the arbitration on September 30 and maintains that the activity is governed by the archipelago's legislation in accordance with international law. Sea Lion, developed by Navitas and Rockhopper, has had a final investment decision since December 2025.

World.title: Simon, strengthening rapidly, could hit Jalisco or Colima as a major hurricane this weekend
World.content:
Hurricane Simon strengthened into a Category 2 storm Friday as authorities prepared for possible landfall in Jalisco or Colima — potentially bringing catastrophic winds, dangerous storm surge and flooding to Mexico on the heels of Hurricane Polo last week.

Forecasters expected the Pacific storm to become a major hurricane Friday evening and reach Category 4 strength Saturday, with sustained winds of 230 km/h (145 mph), according to a Friday morning advisory from the U.S. National Hurricane Center (NHC).

At 3 p.m. Mexico City time, the storm had maximum sustained winds of 165 km/h (105 mph) and was about 315 kilometers south of Manzanillo, Colima, moving northwest at 4 km/h (2 mph).

The eye of the storm is forecast to turn north and pass very near or over Mexico’s west-central coast late Saturday or Sunday. Tropical storm conditions are expected to carry through Saturday morning, followed by hurricane conditions Saturday evening or Sunday.

Simon could become the second hurricane to make landfall in Mexico this Pacific season, following Polo, which struck Baja California Sur on Sept. 28 and Sonora on Sept. 29.

Simon’s precise track remains uncertain. The NHC said the storm could weaken rapidly or dissipate if its center moves inland. If its core stays offshore, it could continue north as a hurricane.

A hurricane warning issued by Mexico’s National Water Commission (Conagua) remains in effect from Punta San Telmo, Michoacán, to Punta Mita, Nayarit — points roughly 475 kilometers (295 miles) apart by road. A hurricane watch extends north to San Blas, Nayarit, while a tropical storm watch extends south to Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán.

Dangerous storm surge could strike the coast and nearby inland areas, accompanied by large, destructive waves. Rainfall could trigger life-threatening flooding and mudslides, particularly on steep terrain.

Simon could bring 20 to 38 centimeters (8 to 15 inches) of rain across parts of southwestern Mexico through Sunday, with isolated totals of 64 centimeters (25 inches) in Michoacán, Colima, Jalisco and Nayarit, according to the hurricane center.

Laura Velázquez, Mexico’s national civil protection coordinator, said authorities Friday would establish command centers in Puerto Vallarta, Cihuatlán and Manzanillo.

Authorities began evacuations in El Rebalse, a community in Jalisco that is vulnerable to flooding from the Marabasco River. Seventy residents left on their own and 10 were moved to a shelter, Reuters reported.

Schools in 22 Jalisco municipalities suspended classes Friday and Monday.

Meanwhile, Hurricane Isaias, a Category 3 storm, was churning through the Gulf of Mexico, with landfall in the U.S. expected Friday evening, according to the hurricane center. No landfall in Mexico is forecast.

With reports from El Sol de México, Reuters and La Silla Rota

World.title: MND Local Puerto Vallarta: Mariachis, murals, drainage and demolition
World.content:
This week, Puerto Vallarta announced it will host a national children’s mariachi competition to promote this iconic Mexican musical style. Additionally, the Vallarta Institute of Culture issued a call for artists interested in decorating the walls of a local cemetery, and drainage work is expected to cause traffic disruptions on one of the city’s main thoroughfares.

Meanwhile, the Punta Paraíso tourism megaproject, planned for a stretch of beach in San Pancho, is set to be demolished due to environmental concerns.

Here are some of Puerto Vallarta’s top news stories.

Children’s and youth mariachi competition to be held in Puerto Vallarta

Puerto Vallarta will host the fourth Children’s and Youth Mariachi Competition Oct. 14-16, marking the first time the event takes place outside Guadalajara.

Featuring 18 groups from various regions of Jalisco, the competition seeks to foster the training of new generations of musicians while preserving the mariachi tradition.

Ten groups will participate in the intermediate category and eight in the advanced category. Activities will begin Oct. 14 with a masterclass at the La Lija Cultural Center. In the evening, the groups will perform in the opening gala at the Arcos del Malecón.

The jury will evaluate musical execution, performance quality, ensemble, intonation and adherence to mariachi tradition to select the finalist groups.

The finals will be held Oct. 16, starting at 6 p.m., at the Teatro Vallarta. Before the awards ceremony, all 18 participating groups will perform together.

Calling all muralists to decorate a cemetery for Day of the Dead

The Vallarta Institute of Culture is inviting artists to participate in an initiative to create 10 murals on the walls of the Municipal Pantheon in the 5 de Diciembre neighborhood.

The initiative, dubbed “Recuérdame” (Remember Me), aims to transform these spaces into public art galleries that reflect local identity and contribute to revitalizing the urban environment.

Proposals must draw inspiration from figures, traditions, flora, fauna and Puerto Vallarta’s local culture reinterpreted through the symbolism of Day of the Dead.

Applicants must submit their proposals Oct. 6-19; artist selection will take place Oct. 20. A committee will select 10 artists who must work on the murals Oct. 23-29.

Candidates must also submit a digital portfolio containing a maximum of five previous works demonstrating their experience in muralism. The portfolio must be submitted in PDF format.

Selected applicants will receive a cash prize of 7,000 pesos (US $368) upon completion of the mural.

For additional information about the application process, click here.

Demolition ordered for structures at Punta Paraíso complex in San Pancho

A federal court upheld an order for the partial demolition of the Punta Paraíso real estate development along the beach in San Pancho, Nayarit, following years of legal disputes over environmental irregularities.

The company must restore 1,466 square meters (about 15,780 square feet) of land reclaimed from the sea to its original state by demolishing unauthorized structures, and pay a fine of 96,220 pesos (US $5,300). The ruling also mandates the forfeiture to the government of the buildings known as Tower 1 and Tower 2.

The case also led to allegations against Roberto Rodríguez Medrano, the acting head of the Federal Attorney General’s Office for Environmental Protection (Profepa) in Nayarit. Former legislator Ismael Duñalds Ventura claims that the official endorsed the project’s environmental studies in 2018, when he led the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources in Nayarit.

The concession permitted only recreational and ornamental activities, not commercial exploitation. A Profepa inspection launched in December 2021 confirmed the construction work that resulted in the sanctions.

Profepa head Mariana Boy Tamborrell described the ruling as a victory for the community and for the protection of the coastal ecosystem.

Drainage work at Las Palmas Park begins

The Potable Water, Drainage and Sewerage System (SEAPAL) in Puerto Vallarta has begun sanitary infrastructure rehabilitation work in the Parque Las Palmas neighborhood and along Avenida México — a project expected to last approximately six weeks and result in partial traffic closures.

The construction corresponds to the second phase of work on the area’s drainage system. It entails replacing 66 meters (about 216 feet) of pipeline, increasing conveyance capacity and creating a new alternative for wastewater discharge.

Furthermore, this project reinforces the measures SEAPAL Vallarta is taking to address and prevent issues related to sanitation infrastructure — following recent problems in the Versalles neighborhood — by increasing conveyance capacity and improving wastewater management options in this part of the city.

The construction work will cause intermittent restrictions at the intersection of México and Las Palmas avenues; therefore, motorists traveling through the area should anticipate potential disruptions. SEAPAL asked residents and drivers to take precautions, heed warning signs and follow the instructions of municipal traffic officers.

Gabriela Solís is a Mexican lawyer turned full-time writer. She was born and raised in Guadalajara and covers business, culture, lifestyle and travel for Mexico News Daily. You can follow her lifestyle blog Dunas y Palmeras.

World.title: Senate moves to crack down on spam calls with fines of up to 2.3 million pesos
World.content:
The Mexican Senate has unanimously approved a reform to the Federal Consumer Protection Law (LFPC) to penalize abusive telemarketing calls and other unauthorized commercial communications.

Although the primary issue prompting the reform is persistent commercial calls, the amendments also apply to other communication channels used to contact consumers for advertising purposes. This includes the use of digital tools and messaging apps like WhatsApp for commercial communications.

According to the bill, companies that make persistent contact through calls or other unauthorized channels to offer credit cards, insurance, loans, services or other products without the consumer’s authorization could face fines ranging from 56,570 pesos (US $3,123) to 2.3 million pesos (US $126,982).

Senator Mayuli Latifa Martínez Simón of the National Action Party (PAN), the bill’s sponsor, stated that the goal is to protect consumer privacy and let consumers opt out of advertising.

Martínez’s original initiative envisioned the creation of a registration mechanism for individuals to express that they do not wish to receive advertising, similar to the U.S. Do Not Call Registry. However, other senators argued that the problem doesn’t lie in the lack of registry — rather, they considered it stems from insufficient sanctions.

Indeed, Mexico already has two opt-out registries where consumers can sign up to avoid unwanted advertising: REPEP, for commercial calls, and REUS, for financial services.

However, the Senate considered that existing sanctions have not been sufficient to deter unwanted commercial communications.

The bill draws on data from Truecaller, a mobile app designed to identify calls and text messages from unknown numbers. Truecaller data indicates that Mexico ranks sixth in the world for most spam calls, with an estimated average of 20 to 25 spam contacts per user per month.

The bill warns that this barrage of calls not only disrupts people’s activities but can also increase their exposure to fraud attempts.

Senator María del Rocío Corona Nakamura, of the Green Party (PVEM), noted that everyone has the right not to be persistently called by companies. Now, she emphasized, “They will no longer be able to do so without our consent — whether by text message, email or any other means.”

The bill will now move to the Chamber of Deputies for consideration and final vote. If approved, it will enter into force the day after its publication in the Official Gazette of the Federation (DOF).

World.title: Mazatlán prison riots leave at least 12 dead, including a 2-year-old
World.content:
Riots on successive days at a state prison in Mazatlán have resulted in the deaths of 11 inmates and a toddler who was part of a family visit, while another 16 inmates were injured.

According to reports from the Sinaloa Security Ministry (SSP), Thursday’s riot, which occurred during scheduled family visiting hours, began as a violent clash between inmates who managed to acquire and use firearms inside the facility.

When gunfire broke out in two contiguous units, prison officials locked down the facility and issued a red alert, but struggled to contain the fighting.

Elements of the Army, Navy, National Guard and state security forces were deployed to regain control, but not before 10 people were killed and 16 were injured.

State Security Minister Sinuhé Téllez confirmed that a 2-year-old boy was among the dead, while the injured were transferred to a medical facility for treatment.

The boy’s mother told investigators that she went to visit her husband, but left to pick up another child, leaving the boy in his father’s care. The boy’s father is reportedly among the 16 inmates hospitalized.

Inmates’ families gathered outside the prison, known as “El Castillo,” to demand information about their loved ones, while officials secured the scene inside.

State prosecutors and federal security agents have launched a formal investigation into how firearms were smuggled into the prison — two 9mm handguns were recovered after the incident — and are piecing together the exact sequence of events that triggered the confrontation.

The SSP will collaborate fully with the State Attorney General’s Office, Téllez said, in order to clarify the facts and determine if any prison employee was involved in allowing the weapons inside the facility.

The newspaper Diario de Yucatán said the shootout was allegedly aimed at assassinating Eduardo Jonathan Martínez Larios, alias “El Owen,” identified as a member of the Los Chapitos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel. He was reportedly among the dead.

Early Friday, another confrontation broke out within a single cellblock. The authorities quickly controlled the situation, but not before two inmates were killed.

In a social media post, the SSP said the rest of the prison population was safe, adding that the interinstitutional task force maintains a presence inside and outside the prison to preserve order and security.

Prison staff are in the process of establishing communication with inmates’ relatives to inform them about the situation and “will continue with follow-up to provide them with the necessary information.”

With reports from Reforma, Milenio, Diario de Yucatán and 24 Horas

World.title: El Jalapeño: US politicians viciously harangue journalist who questions their lack of civility
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original article here.

WASHINGTON, District of Columbia — A joint campaign event held on Capitol Hill descended into hostile shouting Monday after a reporter dared to ask whether candidates running in the upcoming midterm elections might consider adopting a slightly milder tone on the trail.

The campaign event, held ahead of the upcoming midterm elections, became heated when a journalist pointed out that describing political rivals in TV ads as “communist saboteurs plotting to steal your groundwater” might be hindering civil discourse.

“How dare you question my absolute, unyielding commitment to respect and decorum, you total hack?” shouted one incumbent senator, pounding a podium while gesturing aggressively toward the press pool. “I have dedicated my entire midterm campaign to promoting mutual understanding, and anyone who claims otherwise is a radical traitor who deserves to be stripped of their credentials, horse-whipped and deported.”

According to witnesses, the campaign atmosphere further deteriorated when a visiting Mexican diplomat politely noted that political leaders in her country routinely manage to address policy disputes and host elections without accusing their opponents of being existential threats to human progress. The suggestion that public servants could run for office without resorting to daily character assassination was immediately denounced by candidates from both parties as an unprovoked attack on American democratic tradition.

“Civility is the bedrock of our republic, and I will personally ruin the career of anyone who implies our campaign strategy lacks it,” added a congressional candidate, adjusting his tie while glaring directly into the camera. “We are running to lead by example, and if the press refuses to report on how overwhelmingly polite and constructive our attack ads are, then the media is the enemy of harmony.”

By the conclusion of the half-hour briefing, three separate political campaigns had issued formal press releases condemning the concept of polite dialogue as an aggressive partisan maneuver, even as several campaign aides handed out informational brochures detailing their candidates’ lifelong passion for peaceful consensus.

At press time, midterm organizers were reportedly drafting a bipartisan resolution that would officially classify any future questions regarding campaign tone, candidate manners or basic decency as deliberate acts of war.

World.title: Multiple newborn deaths at public hospitals in Jalisco and Durango trigger clinical and legal investigations
World.content:
Investigations into the deaths of newborns treated at public hospitals in the states of Jalisco and Durango have expanded as more families demand answers about their children’s deaths.

At least eight and perhaps as many as 18 newborn deaths have occurred since March in the neonatal intensive care unit at the Centro Médico Nacional de Occidente in Guadalajara, Jalisco.

#Estados | Padres de tres bebés fallecidos entre julio y agosto de 2026 en la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos Neonatales del Centro Médico Nacional de Occidente denunciaron ante la FGR al IMSS Jalisco por presunta negligencia médica y falta de higiene. MP. 🔗 https://t.co/Nm3fYpXSTy — La Silla Rota (@lasillarota) October 2, 2026

And last month, five newborns died in the neonatal intensive care unit of General Hospital Zone No. 1 in Durango city, Durango.

Both hospitals are government-funded public institutions under the auspices of the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS).

Earlier this week, IMSS Director General Zoé Robledo ordered an independent clinical audit to review the records of newborns who died in Jalisco, which he said “is not intended to point the finger at medical personnel,” as its “priority is to know the truth, support the families and prevent similar events from happening again.”

At least eight of the deaths in Guadalajara have been linked to hospital-acquired infections involving the bacteria Klebsiella pneumoniae and the fungus Candida albicans.

In Durango, health authorities confirmed that four of the five infants who died between Sept. 15 and Sept. 19 tested positive for the same bacteria.

The clinical audit is being conducted independently of the complaints filed with the Attorney General’s Office (FGR) by relatives of some of the newborns.

Forensic investigations, including necropsies, are ongoing to establish legal responsibilities.

Robledo insisted he will fully cooperate with the FGR and any other competent authority in the investigations, but suggested it remained to be determined that the infections detected had a direct relationship with the deaths.

The IMSS audit is being conducted by a committee comprising neonatologists, infectious disease specialists, and epidemiologists, who will analyze each case individually to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

Robledo said the audit’s findings will be communicated first to the families, adding that if any errors or liabilities are found, the IMSS will act accordingly, “regardless of the level at which they occur.”

Protests by the grieving families last month prompted intense public scrutiny, leading the IMSS to dismiss its state delegate in Durango and the neonatal unit was temporarily closed to contain any potential outbreak.

In Jalisco where the tragedies stretched from March 14 through Sept. 28, the director of the Guadalajara hospital and the head of the neonatal unit were temporarily removed from their posts.

With reports from El País, International Business Times and La Jornada.

World.title: After Torreón school attack, Sheinbaum presents decree on social media content for minors: Friday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🌀 Hurricane Simon forecast to make landfall near Jalisco and Colima this weekend: Citing the National Meteorological Service, Civil Protection chief Laura Velázquez said Simon, a Category 1 hurricane on Friday morning, could hit Mexico’s Pacific coast as a Category 3 or 4. She said the area of impact could be one of five Jalisco municipalities (Cihuatlán, La Huerta, Tomatlán, Cabo Corrientes or Puerto Vallarta) or Manzanillo, Colima. She urged residents to stay informed through official channels.

Citing the National Meteorological Service, Civil Protection chief Laura Velázquez said Simon, a Category 1 hurricane on Friday morning, could hit Mexico’s Pacific coast as a Category 3 or 4. She said the area of impact could be one of five Jalisco municipalities (Cihuatlán, La Huerta, Tomatlán, Cabo Corrientes or Puerto Vallarta) or Manzanillo, Colima. She urged residents to stay informed through official channels. 📱 Government presents decree on “safe digital environments” for minors: Presidential legal adviser Luisa María Alcalde said the decree bars social media sites and other online platforms from displaying or recommending content to minors that generates or promotes hate speech, violent extremism, sexual exploitation or violence, suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, cyber-bullying and illegal conduct. The government announced the decree last Friday, a day after a fatal machete attack at a school in Torreón, Coahuila. Sheinbaum said the decree will be published in the official gazette next Tuesday or Wednesday after further legal review to ensure it doesn’t exceed the executive branch’s authority.

Presidential legal adviser Luisa María Alcalde said the decree bars social media sites and other online platforms from displaying or recommending content to minors that generates or promotes hate speech, violent extremism, sexual exploitation or violence, suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, cyber-bullying and illegal conduct. The government announced the decree last Friday, a day after a fatal machete attack at a school in Torreón, Coahuila. Sheinbaum said the decree will be published in the official gazette next Tuesday or Wednesday after further legal review to ensure it doesn’t exceed the executive branch’s authority. 🚨 Multiple inmates and a 2-year-old boy killed in Mazatlán prison fight: Sheinbaum said she was informed about Thursday’s shooting at El Castillo prison at Friday’s Security Cabinet meeting. Sixteen prisoners were injured, and two firearms were seized.

Why today’s mañanera matters

Federal officials spoke about a range of significant issues at President Sheinbaum’s Friday morning press conference, including a hurricane headed for Mexico’s Pacific coast and a new decree aimed at keeping kids safe online and decreasing the probability of young people perpetrating acts of violence.

The government announced that it would prepare such a decree last Friday, a day after a fatal machete attack at a school in Torreón, Coahuila. The attack — in which a vice principal was killed and four other people were injured — was allegedly perpetrated by 18-year-old twin brothers who formerly studied at the Number 13 Secondary School in the Ejido La Unión area of Torreón. They were allegedly inspired to carry out the attack after learning about perpetrators of violent attacks outside Mexico through social media forums and being exposed to extremist ideology online.

Another significant development that was discussed at today’s mañanera was the death of nine inmates and a two-year-old boy at a prison in the coastal city of Mazatlán, Sinaloa, on Thursday. They were all shot during a fight at the El Castillo prison, located about 14 kilometers east of the center of Mazatlán.

Hurricane Simon set to make landfall in Mexico this weekend

Citing information from the National Meteorological Service, National Civil Protection chief Laura Velázquez said that Hurricane Simon — a Category 1 hurricane on Friday morning — is forecast to make landfall this weekend on Mexico’s Pacific coast “in the vicinity of Jalisco and Colima.”

She said that Simon could make landfall as a Category 3 or Category 4 hurricane.

Velázquez said that “the area of impact” could be in one of five municipalities in Jalisco — Cihuatlán, La Huerta, Tomatlán, Cabo Corrientes or Puerto Vallarta — or in Manzanillo, Colima.

#Huracán categoría 2 🌀 #Simon ⚠️ Simon presenta vientos máximos sostenidos de 155 km/h, rachas de 195 km/h y desplazamiento hacia el noroeste a 6 km/h. 📍 A las 09:00 h, se localiza a 335 km al sur de Manzanillo, #Colima, y a 500 km al sur-sureste de Cabo Corrientes, #Jalisco. — Coordinación Nacional de Protección Civil (@CNPC_MX) October 9, 2026

“It’s still too early to determine the [exact] category [of the hurricane] and the exact point of entry. But in the course of the day today, we may be able to obtain precise information,” she said.

Velázquez urged residents of Jalisco and Colima to keep themselves “very well informed” about the hurricane by remaining attentive to official information disseminated by state and federal authorities.

Government presents ‘safe digital environments’ decree

Luisa María Alcalde, President Sheinbaum’s top legal adviser, presented a “decree to guarantee safe digital environments for girls, boys and adolescents.”

She said that the decree will apply to “digital platforms” that enable communication between users and the sharing of content — i.e. social media sites and other online forums.

Alcalde said that the decree bars digital platforms from displaying or recommending content to minors that “generates or promotes” hate speech, violent extremism, sexual exploitation or violence, suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, cyber-bullying and illegal conduct in general.

Sheinbaum said that the decree is “based on” the Mexican Constitution, which “establishes the protection of girls, boys and adolescents.”

She said that the government’s legal department and the Digital Transformation Agency will continue to work on the decree in the coming days to ensure that it doesn’t exceed the authority of the executive branch of government.

“They might also speak to the [digital] platforms,” Sheinbaum said, adding that the decree will be published in the government’s official gazette next Tuesday or Wednesday.

Mazatlán prison fight leaves 10 people dead

A reporter asked the president whether she was informed at her Friday morning security briefing about the “riña” (fight or brawl) at a prison in Mazatlán on Thursday.

Nine inmates and a two-year-old boy who was visiting the El Castillo prison were shot and killed during the outbreak of violence. Sixteen prisoners were reported injured. Sinaloa Security Minister Sinuhé Téllez López said that two firearms were seized at the prison after a fight between rival groups of inmates. A man known as “El Owen” was reportedly among the nine inmates killed. He is said to be a member of the Los Chapitos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, which is engaged in a long-running war with the Los Mayos faction of the same criminal group.

Sheinbaum said she received information about the case at the Friday morning Security Cabinet meeting. She said that Security Cabinet officials are working with interim Sinaloa Governor Graciela Domínguez to “strengthen the penitentiary system in Sinaloa.”

“I expect that the governor will be able to provide information,” Sheinbaum said.

Asked whether authorities would contact the deceased inmates’ relatives, the president said prison authorities always do so. She said that the cause of the prison dispute would be investigated and that the Security Cabinet would provide more information on the case.

World.title: Postcards from Mexico: Noche de Despecho, or where heartbreak becomes a party
World.content:
It’s 10:15 a.m. on a Friday in a cantina in Valladolid. I’ve spent the last 10 minutes trying to figure out what I’ve walked into, but my only real lead is a table of a dozen 50-somethings singing and dancing to Timbiriche’s “Con Todos Menos Conmigo” over 2-for-1 cantaritos.

As one caterwauls, the others use their straws like wands, stirring around tequila, grapefruit juice and years of suffering in an earthenware jar while nibbling at salted rims and cooling themselves with hand fans. They’ve held the karaoke playlist hostage for as long as I’ve been in the bar — passing the mic around their table like a talking stick at a powwow — and judging by their energy levels, there’s a lot more where that came from.

Leave it to Mexicans to turn a broken heart into a party.

Between songs, the bar’s hostess welcomes newcomers to their weekly Noche de Despecho, literally “Night of Spite,” figuratively, a nocturnal AA meeting for people struggling with a breakup, if AA meetings were musicals. She invites others to request songs — let it all hang out for three minutes — but at this rate, they’ll have to come back next week before their song gets played, and I’m still learning the words to “Mi Historia Entre Tus Dedos,” so regrettably, I can’t.

The Sala de Despecho phenomenon

Somewhere in Guadalajara, Pepe Rodríguez is smiling. He’s the architect, the reason these “Salas de Despecho” are popping up all over the country, from Mexico City to Mazatlán. Word is, he used to come home drunk and sing heartbreak songs in the early hours with his friends. Now their misery is ours.

Part of me wonders what it says about a culture and its views on romance that bars like these have become all the rage. The other part marvels at how adept that culture is at purging pain.

I don’t need to say a word to these women, and I can guess how their relationships ended. The setlist gives it away.

One in a red blouse and knee-length white skirt belts out “Un Millón de Primaveras” by Vicente Fernández. She’s taking way longer than her ex to move on and makes no apologies for this. Another in a black dress swaggers through “Se Me Olvidó Otra Vez” by the incomparable Juan Gabriel. I suspect she’s what her compatriots would call a migajera: she knows it’s over but has left the door open in case the old flame decides to walk back in.

Still another sings “La Puerta Negra” by Los Tigres del Norte. She never had a chance, and now laments the role of puertas negras, or invisible societal barriers imposed by families that prevent lovers from being together.

And then there’s Miss Machiavelli, biding her time coolly as she interprets Oscar D’León’s “Llorarás,” promising her ex, wherever they are, that they’ll be the ones crying when all is said and done.

‘Misery loves company’

This isn’t a ceremony of sadness; it’s equal parts group therapy and public shaming.

Mounted on the wall behind the table where the women sit is the head of a donkey, which, I have to imagine, isn’t entirely without symbolism. In lieu of the spurners not in attendance, those singing have another perfectly suitable jackass to whom they can direct their discontent.

Science says that’s the magic behind these spots.

Each full-throated note, a trigger releasing feel-good endorphins and oxytocin; each sustained falsetto, a cue to the body to lower cortisol levels; each heartbreaking lyric, a step toward processing pain; and each neighbor who joins in, a small confirmation that whoever’s singing isn’t suffering alone.

It’s Friday night in the Sala de Despecho, and misery loves company.

Ethan Jacobs is a freelance writer and writing coach based in Playa del Carmen. He has written extensively in narrative and short fiction formats, and his work has received recognition both domestically and internationally in microfiction, short fiction and narrative essay formats.

World.title: What to Do in Salvador in October 2026
World.content:
SALVADOR · Culture

Salvador’s second half of October runs from Regina Casé’s solo show on Friday 16 October to the Festival Sangue Novo on 17 and 18 October, and closes with Djavan’s musical on 31 October and 1 November.

Key Facts — Who Visitors and residents of Salvador, the capital of the northeastern Brazilian state of Bahia, looking for dated events from 10 October.

— Biggest weekend Festival Sangue Novo, Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October at Trapiche Barnabé; a two-day pre-sale pass started at R$60 (about US$12) half-price.

— Theatre Regina Casé’s solo VIVA! VIDA! plays Teatro Castro Alves from Friday 16 to Sunday 18 October, with tickets from R$25 (about US$5) half-price.

— Month-end Djavan – O Musical: Vidas pra Contar, Saturday 31 October and Sunday 1 November at 18:00, from R$35 (about US$7).

— Public holiday Monday 12 October is a national holiday in Brazil, so banks and many offices close.

— Money US$1 buys about R$4.99 (RT, 9 October 2026), so R$100 is about US$20.

SALVADOR — This guide lists the dated events we could confirm from 10 October, with venues and prices in reais and US dollars. It is written for people who live in Salvador or stay for weeks, and for Americans planning a trip to Bahia.

Prices change as ticket batches sell out, so treat every figure as the price we saw on Friday 9 October 2026. Where an organiser has not published a price, we say so.

10 to 12 October: a children’s forum and the circus

Saturday 10 October, 09:00–13:00 1º Encontro da Cultura da Infância Espaço Cultural Boca de Brasa, Cajazeiras · Price not published on the Sympla page Organised by Inovarte, this meeting is aimed at teachers, school coordinators, early-childhood staff and families. It is built around listening, art and the exchange of experience rather than lectures.

Thursday 8 October onwards Circo Portugal Avenida Paralela · from R$30 (about US$6) The travelling circus opened in Salvador on Thursday 8 October and promises a large magic show and a Globe of Death motorbike act. Check the box office for the closing date and ticket prices before you plan around it.

Monday 12 October is a public holiday for Our Lady of Aparecida, which Brazil also marks as Children’s Day. We found no confirmed ticketed event in Salvador that day, so expect family outings, crowded beaches and closed offices.

16 to 18 October: Regina Casé and the Sangue Novo weekend

Friday 16 and Saturday 17 October, 20:00; Sunday 18 October, 19:00 Regina Casé: VIVA! VIDA! Teatro Castro Alves, Campo Grande · R$50 to R$150 full, R$25 to R$75 half (about US$10 to US$30 full) A 90-minute solo show directed by Daniela Thomas and Estevão Ciavatta Pantoja. It traces the planet’s history from its geological formation to today’s hyperconnected life, with LED scenography and a soundtrack by pianist Amaro Freitas. The cheapest Sector 3 seats cost R$50 full or R$25 half.

Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October Festival Sangue Novo Trapiche Barnabé, Comércio · Tickets on Sympla; pre-sale pass R$60 half to R$120 full (about US$12 to US$24) The eighth edition of this independent music festival has two stages, TIM and Maré. The line-up includes Céu, Rachel Reis, Zaynara, Juliana Linhares, Zé Ibarra and Getúlio Abelha. We did not find gate times, so check the Sympla page before you go.

Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October, 11:00 and 16:00 Cantabrincando com Grandes Pequeninos Caixa Cultural Salvador · R$30 full, R$15 half (about US$6 and US$3) A children’s show with Jair Oliveira and Tania Khalill. Ticket sales were due to start on Tuesday 13 October.

31 October and 1 November: the month closes with Djavan

Saturday 31 October and Sunday 1 November, 18:00 Djavan – O Musical: Vidas pra Contar Concha Acústica do Teatro Castro Alves, Campo Grande · From R$35 (about US$7) The musical follows the singer’s career, with actor Raphael Elias playing Djavan. It received eight nominations at the 13th Bibi Ferreira Award. Outdoor evening shows can be delayed by rain, so check the venue’s channels on the day.

What it means for you

For a visitor from the United States, the prices are low. A top-sector seat for Regina Casé costs about US$30, and a festival pass about US$24.

Book early for the weekend of 16 to 18 October. Regina Casé and Sangue Novo overlap on Saturday 17 and Sunday 18, so you will need to choose or combine an early show with a late one.

Residents on a tighter budget should look at the half-price categories. These are normally for students, seniors and other groups, so carry ID.

Planning your Salvador in October

Salvador is tropical in October, so carry water and sun protection. A light layer helps in air-conditioned theatres.

Sympla is a common ticketing platform for independent events in Brazil. Larger theatre productions may also sell through the venue box office.

Foreign cards may add fees, so compare the rate on the day you buy. Our conversions use US$1 = R$4.99.

After dark, use a ride app or a licensed taxi rather than walking long distances. This matters most around the historic centre and the Comércio waterfront, where public transport thins out late.

Everyday costs matter alongside ticket prices. Our report on Brazil’s September inflation shows where Brazilian prices stand.

For more country context, see our Brazil hub and our expat and nomad coverage.

What is not known

We could not confirm the closing date and prices of Circo Portugal, the gate times for Sangue Novo or the price of the Boca de Brasa meeting. Several events that earlier listings gave for early October have passed, and we have removed them.
