Sunday 11 October, 09:00–17:30 Sucre Viajero at Comuna Lumbisí Plaza de la Identidad, Comuna Lumbisí · Free An entrepreneurs’ fair runs from 09:00 to 17:00. The children’s play El viaje perdido de Pishku is staged at 11:00. Concerts run from 12:00 to 17:30 and include the Coro Mixto Ciudad de Quito, the Banda Sinfónica Metropolitana, the Orquesta de Instrumentos Andinos and La Sonora Dinamita.

Lumbisí is a rural parish on the edge of the city, so most visitors will need a taxi or ride-hailing app to reach it. The programme is free and needs no ticket.

Iron Maiden on Wednesday 14 October

Wednesday 14 October, gates 16:00 Iron Maiden with The Raven Age Estadio Olímpico Atahualpa, Quito · US$72.74 to US$244.66 with fees The Raven Age open at 19:00 and Iron Maiden start at 20:50. It is the band’s first show in Ecuador since 2009 and part of the Run For Your Lives world tour.

Tickets are sold only digitally through Buen Plan. Prices by zone, with fees and taxes included, are US$72.74 for Platea, US$85.96 for Cancha (standing), US$130.93 for Preferencia, US$165.31 for Tribuna, US$204.99 for Campo (standing) and US$244.66 for Palco. As of 6 October, tickets remained in every category.

Entry works through QR codes in the Buen Plan app, which are released five days before the show. Physical ticket exchanges are not available. The app lets you transfer a ticket to another person. Umbrellas, alcohol, drugs, weapons, spiked accessories and sharp objects are banned.

Getting there: the Ecovía bus line extends its service until midnight, and the Metro runs its standard hours of 05:30 to 23:00. Streets around the stadium, including José Correa, Sebastián Quinteros and Manuel María Quinteros, will be closed. Expect crowds, and leave early. We covered the tour announcement in Iron Maiden Plays Quito, Ecuador, on 14 October. The same tour also stops in Lima and Buenos Aires.

Free Plaza Show on Sunday 18 October

Sunday 18 October, 11:00–16:30 Sucre Viajero at Plaza Foch Plaza Foch, La Mariscal, north Quito · Free El viaje perdido de Pishku is staged from 11:00 to 12:00. Live music follows from 12:00 to 16:30 with Grupo Yavirac, Viviana González, the Banda Sinfónica Metropolitana and Orquesta la Familia.

Plaza Foch is the heart of La Mariscal, the district where many visitors and foreign residents stay. This is the easiest of the three Sucre Viajero stops to reach on foot from a hotel.

The Rasmus on Saturday 24 October

Saturday 24 October The Rasmus, Weirdo Tour 2026 Teatro Bolívar, Historic Centre · US$65 to US$100 plus taxes The Finnish band, formed in Helsinki in 1994, plays Quito for the third time after visits in 2018 and 2023. Tickets are sold through Ticketshow online and at its outlets in Quito, Guayaquil and Cuenca. General admission costs US$65, a box costs US$75, Preferencia costs US$85 and the top box costs US$100, all plus taxes.

A Free Exhibition on Weekends

Saturdays 09:00–19:00, Sundays 09:00–15:00 La Ronda: Vida y Cotidianidad Casa de las Artes La Ronda, Historic Centre · Free An exhibition on everyday life in La Ronda, the narrow old-town street known for its balconies and craft shops. Local listings describe it as ongoing and do not give an end date, so check the venue before planning around it.

Combine it with a walk around Plaza Grande. For more on living in the city, see our guide for expats and nomads in Latin America.

What It Means for You

For a reader in the United States, the practical points are simple. Ecuador uses the US dollar, so you pay in the currency you already hold, though card fees and local ticket taxes still apply. The cheapest Iron Maiden seat, in Platea, costs US$72.74 with fees.

Quito sits at about 2,850 metres, so allow a day to adjust before a long evening out. Bring a light waterproof layer for evening events. Book Iron Maiden and The Rasmus through the official platforms only, and treat the free Sucre Viajero shows as the easy way to see local music without a ticket.

What Is Not Known

The start time of The Rasmus show was not in the published announcements we found. Sucre Viajero dates after 18 October were not listed, and the end date of the La Ronda exhibition is not published. Whether Iron Maiden tickets will sell out before 14 October is also unknown. Confirm times with the venue or ticket platform before you travel.

What is the biggest event in Quito in October 2026?

Iron Maiden at Estadio Olímpico Atahualpa on Wednesday 14 October. Gates open at 16:00, The Raven Age play at 19:00 and Iron Maiden at 20:50.

How much do Iron Maiden tickets in Quito cost?

Prices run from US$72.74 for Platea to US$244.66 for Palco, including fees and taxes. Tickets are sold only digitally through Buen Plan.

Are there free events in Quito this month?

Yes. Sucre Viajero offers free concerts and children’s theatre on Sunday 11 October in Lumbisí and on Sunday 18 October at Plaza Foch. The La Ronda exhibition is also free.

Is the Feria Internacional del Libro still on?

No. The fair ran from 30 September to 4 October 2026 at the Centro de Exposiciones Quito.

How do I get to the Iron Maiden concert?

The Ecovía line runs until midnight and the Metro runs from 05:30 to 23:00. Streets around the stadium are closed on the night, so leave early.

World.title: Peru Merges Army and Police Against Crime
World.content:
Security: Peru

Key Facts —Who. Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, the Armed Forces and the National Police —What. A unified command that integrates the military and police against crime, plus a Special Commission Against Criminality —Where. Announced in Lima, followed by a prison visit in Trujillo, northern Peru —When. Announced on Wednesday 7 October 2026; prison visit on Friday 9 October 2026 —Why it matters. Peru is a US partner and a major copper, gold and farm exporter, and extortion hits transport and business —As of. 9 October 2026, 21:35 GMT

President Keiko Fujimori has created a unified command that joins Peru’s Armed Forces and National Police against crime. She announced it on Wednesday 7 October 2026 and said she would no longer wait to confront crime.

What We Know

On Wednesday 7 October 2026, Fujimori announced the unified command at the Army General Headquarters in Lima. It integrates the Armed Forces and the National Police under one structure.

The command includes a control and operations centre and an elite group for search and capture operations. Andina reports she said that the state will no longer wait to confront crime.

Infobae’s headline quotes her saying that the time for a total offensive has come. She also demanded professionalism, legality, discipline and respect for human rights from the security forces.

Fujimori also created a Special Commission Against Criminality to coordinate ministries and public and private bodies. These include the Financial Intelligence Unit, the National Intelligence Directorate and the telecoms regulator Osiptel, along with telecom companies.

A public building in central Lima. File photo.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Peru security Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Else Was Announced

Fujimori promised faster expulsion of foreign criminals and a return of state control over prisons. She also pledged to isolate inmates who direct crimes from jail.

She invited foreign governments to share experience, technology, information and resources. She said Peruvians are desperate and leave home each day in fear of extortion or death.

On Friday 9 October 2026, Fujimori visited the El Milagro prison in Trujillo, in northern Peru. EFE reports she said criminals will try to scare the government but that it will respond firmly.

Reports say scanners at the entrance now work after being out of use for three years, and visitor numbers fell by half under tighter controls. She said she wants three or four more prison wings built quickly, while overcrowding and more than 300 inmates with tuberculosis were noted.

Fujimori also plans to travel to El Salvador from Wednesday 28 October to Saturday 31 October 2026 to meet President Nayib Bukele. Andina reports that the Senate approved the trip.

What Is Not Known

The reports we reviewed do not state how many troops or officers the command will include. They also do not say who will lead it.

The legal basis for the command and its budget were not stated either. Until those details appear, how the command will work in practice remains unclear.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

Peru is a US partner and a major exporter of copper, gold and agricultural goods. Mining investors and importers will watch whether the new command reduces extortion that affects transport and business.

Travellers to Peru should follow guidance from the US Embassy and their own government. Our earlier coverage of the El Salvador plans is in Peru Clears Fujimori Trip to El Salvador and Peru’s Fujimori Seeks 29 October Visit to Bukele Prison.

The announcement is a statement of intent, and its effect on crime will only be measurable over time. We will report concrete changes when official figures are published.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Peru’s unified command?

It is a structure that integrates the Armed Forces and the National Police to fight crime. It includes a control and operations centre and an elite group for search and capture operations.

Who announced it and when?

President Keiko Fujimori announced it on Wednesday 7 October 2026 at the Army General Headquarters in Lima. Andina reports she said the state will no longer wait to confront crime.

What is still unclear about the command?

Troop numbers, the legal basis, who leads it and the budget were not stated in the reports we saw. These details matter for judging how the command will work.

Is Fujimori travelling to El Salvador?

She plans a visit from Wednesday 28 October to Saturday 31 October 2026 to meet President Nayib Bukele. Our earlier reports cover the plans for the trip.

World.title: Brazil Supreme Court Justice Exposes Death Threats
World.content:
Politics: Brazil

Key Facts —Who. Flávio Dino, minister of Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court, and fellow ministers Alexandre de Moraes and Cristiano Zanin. —What. Dino made public excerpts of a court security report showing thousands of messages with threats of assassination and aggression. —Where. Brazil, on social media, with X (formerly Twitter) carrying the highest volume of hostile posts. —When. Friday 9 October 2026, 16 days before the presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October 2026. —Why it matters. Threats against judges add to political risk in Latin America’s largest economy during a tense election. —Prediction markets. Polymarket prices Yes at 19% that Moraes leaves the court before the end of 2026, and Kalshi prices 22% (4:57 pm US Eastern, 9 October 2026). —As of. 9 October 2026, 21:00 GMT

A minister of Brazil’s Supreme Court has made public a court security report that shows thousands of messages threatening judges with death. Flávio Dino posted excerpts on Friday 9 October 2026, 16 days before the presidential runoff.

What We Know

On Friday 9 October 2026, Flávio Dino, a minister of Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court, published excerpts of a security report on his verified Instagram profile. The report was produced by the court itself.

Dino wrote that he had received excerpts of a security report “showing thousands of messages in the same sense: threats of assassination and various aggressions”. The messages name Dino, Alexandre de Moraes and Cristiano Zanin, who are all ministers of the court.

The Supreme Federal Court, known in Brazil as the STF, is the country’s highest court on constitutional questions. Its ministers sit in the capital, Brasília.

Dino said the hatred in the messages comes from “the repetition of lies, aimed at causing violence”. He added that the threats will not change his work, and that if a judge comes to fear deciding a case, “there is no longer a Judiciary”.

The National Congress buildings in Brasília. File photo.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Flávio Dino (Brazil) Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the Report Shows

The report identified threats of shooting, explosion, hanging and dismemberment against court ministers on social media. X, formerly Twitter, carried the highest volume of hostile posts.

One quoted message said Dino would be “the first to be shot” for restricting access to weapons. We are not reproducing the other violent detail in the excerpts.

Another message urged people to invade the court and do to Moraes, Dino and Zanin what was done to Tiradentes, with the head in a public square. Tiradentes is the independence martyr who was hanged in 1792 and whose body was dismembered.

What Is Not Known

The report covers messages from 1 to 6 October 2026, according to Brazilian media, but the exact number of messages was not given. Dino described “thousands” of messages, and no precise figure has been published.

No official response from police or prosecutors had been reported at the time of publication. We cannot say whether any case has been opened over the messages.

Dino published excerpts, so the full text of the report is not available to us. We therefore cannot say how many different authors or accounts sit behind the messages.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

Brazil’s presidential runoff takes place on Sunday 25 October 2026, so political tension is already high. Our earlier reports have covered the strain around the Supreme Court, including Brazil’s Establishment Backs Fachin Over the Supreme Court Crisis.

The Supreme Court oversees cases involving the circle of former president Jair Bolsonaro, which gives the threats political weight beyond the individual ministers. For background on the court’s wider workload, see Fachin Takes on Two More Bolsonaro Processes From Moraes.

US investors watch judicial independence as one input into political risk in Latin America’s largest economy, Brazil. We draw no market conclusion from a single report.

The excerpts we have seen target court ministers, not visitors, and we have no travel advisory to report. Travellers should still follow official guidance from their own governments during the election period.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, the market “Alexandre de Moraes out as Brazil Supreme Court Justice?” priced Yes at 19% on Friday 9 October 2026 at 4:57 pm US Eastern (20:57 GMT), with US$145,269 traded. It resolves Yes if he ceases to be a justice at any time through 31 December 2026.

On Kalshi, which is regulated in the US by the CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission), the market “Will Alexandre de Moraes leave Brazil’s Supreme Court?” priced “before 1 January 2027” at 22%, with 14,072 contracts traded. These are bets, not polls, and they do not comment on the threats.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Flávio Dino?

Flávio Dino is a minister of Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court. He published the report excerpts on his verified Instagram profile on Friday 9 October 2026.

What does the security report say?

It identifies threats of shooting, explosion, hanging and dismemberment against court ministers on social media. Dino says it shows thousands of messages, with X carrying the highest volume of hostile posts.

Has anyone been charged over the threats?

No official response from police or prosecutors had been reported at the time of publication. We will report any official step once it is confirmed.

Does this change the presidential runoff?

The runoff remains scheduled for Sunday 25 October 2026. We have no information that the report alters the election calendar.

World.title: Brazil Adds US$1.5 Billion to Fuel Subsidies
World.content:
Economy: Brazil

Key Facts —Who. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and the Ministry of Mines and Energy —What. A new extraordinary credit of R$7.52 billion (about US$1.51 billion) for fuel subsidies, of which 82% goes to road diesel —Where. Brazil, with effects on fuel prices across the country —When. Issued on Thursday 8 October 2026 and published on Friday 9 October 2026 —Why it matters. The money continues subsidies created to soften the impact of high international oil prices, days before Brazil’s presidential runoff —As of. 9 October 2026, 21:05 GMT

Brazil’s government has opened a new extraordinary credit of R$7.52 billion (about US$1.51 billion) to keep paying fuel subsidies. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva issued the measure on Thursday 8 October 2026, and it was published on Friday 9 October 2026.

What We Know

The measure is Provisional Measure number 1.395, published in the Diário Oficial da União, Brazil’s official gazette, on Friday 9 October 2026. A provisional measure (medida provisória) is an executive order with force of law that Congress must convert into law within 120 days, or it lapses.

It opens an extraordinary credit of R$7.52 billion (about US$1.51 billion) for fuel subsidies. An extraordinary credit is extra budget authority for urgent and unforeseen spending.

All US$ figures in this article use the RT USD/BRL rate of 4.99 reais per US dollar on 9 October 2026. The credit is for the Ministry of Mines and Energy.

The new money continues payments of subsidies created earlier this year by two other provisional measures. These are MP 1.363/2026 for diesel and MP 1.358/2026 for other oil derivatives.

The financial district of São Paulo. File photo. Foto: Zé Carlos Barretta.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Provisional Measure (Brazil) Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Where the Money Goes

Most of the credit goes to diesel. R$6.17 billion (about US$1.24 billion), or 82% of the total, is for subsidies on road diesel production and imports.

The remaining R$1.35 billion (about US$0.27 billion), or 18%, is for other oil products. The funds go to the Ministry of Mines and Energy.

The subsidies it funds were created to contain the effect of high international oil prices, linked to the escalation in the Middle East, on Brazilian fuel prices. CNN Brasil reports the aim as reducing the effects of price rises on the Brazilian market.

A separate package announced in September, with a new diesel subsidy and gasoline and ethanol tax cuts, was put by Agência Brasil at about R$7 billion a month (about US$1.4 billion). That figure covers a different set of measures and is not the cost of this credit.

What Is Not Known

The reports we saw do not state how much the government has spent on fuel subsidies so far this year. Without that total, it is not possible to say how this credit compares with the full bill.

They also do not say how Congress will treat the provisional measure. Lawmakers must vote on it later, and the outcome is open.

Nor do they explain how the spending is treated under Brazil’s fiscal rule. We will report it if the Treasury or the budget authorities publish details.

What It Means for US Readers and Investors

Brazil is a major oil producer, and Petrobras has shares listed in the United States. The subsidy shows how far the government is willing to go to manage fuel prices at home.

Diesel prices matter beyond the pump, because they feed into freight and food costs across a large country. That is why a diesel-heavy credit is relevant for anyone tracking Brazilian inflation or supply chains.

The decree comes as Brazil heads to a presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October 2026. Readers can see how the issue has developed in Lula Extends Brazil’s Diesel Subsidy Eight Days Before the Election.

For the cost side of the story, see Brazil Fuel Subsidy Bill Reaches US$6.2 Billion, Treasury Says Revenue Covers It. Together the two reports show how the subsidy issue has developed before the vote.

Background: Brazil Tax Reform 2026 Replaces Five Taxes With Two VATs.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Brazil approve on 9 October 2026?

Brazil published Provisional Measure 1.395, which opens an extraordinary credit of R$7.52 billion (about US$1.51 billion) for fuel subsidies. It was issued on Thursday 8 October 2026 by President Lula.

What is an extraordinary credit?

It is extra budget authority for urgent and unforeseen spending. Normally a credit is opened by decree, but this one was opened through a provisional measure.

How is the money split?

R$6.17 billion (about US$1.24 billion), or 82%, is for road diesel production and import subsidies. R$1.35 billion (about US$0.27 billion), or 18%, is for other oil products.

Does Congress still have a say?

Yes, because a provisional measure has force of law at once but Congress must convert it into law within 120 days. The reports we saw do not say how lawmakers will handle it.

World.title: Brazil Inflation Rises to 4.58%, Above 4.5% Ceiling
World.content:
Economy: Brazil

Key Facts —Who. Brazilian consumers, the central bank and investors in Brazilian assets. —What. The IPCA index rose 0.82% in September, taking 12-month inflation to 4.58%, above the 4.5% ceiling of the target. —Where. Brazil. —When. Figures published on Friday 9 October 2026; the next Copom meeting is in early November 2026. —Prediction markets. Polymarket prices a 25 basis point cut in November at 86.5%, and Kalshi prices 2026 inflation above 5.00% at 24% (as of 4:55 pm US Eastern, 9 October 2026). —Why it matters. Higher inflation limits room for rate cuts, which matters for the real and Brazilian ADRs. —As of. 9 October 2026, 21:00 GMT

Brazil’s official inflation rate rose to 4.58% in the 12 months to September, above the 4.5% ceiling of the government target. Prices rose 0.82% in the month, the fastest pace since March, as electricity bills jumped after a discount ended.

What We Know

Brazil’s official inflation index, the IPCA, rose 0.82% in September 2026, the statistics agency IBGE reported on Friday 9 October. That followed a fall of 0.32% in August.

The September reading was the highest monthly figure since March 2026, when prices rose 0.88%. Analysts polled by Reuters had expected a rise of about 0.73%.

Over 12 months, inflation reached 4.58%, up from 4.22% in August. That is above the 4.5% ceiling of the government target.

The target is 3%, with a tolerance of 1.5 percentage points either side, so the accepted range runs from 1.5% to 4.5%. The 12-month rate of 4.58% therefore sits 0.08 percentage points above the top of that band.

The Planalto Palace in Brasília. File photo.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Brazil Inflation News Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Pushed Prices Up

Housing prices rose 2.31% and added 0.35 percentage points to the monthly index. Electricity rose 7.98% and by itself added 0.32 points.

Electricity jumped because the Itaipu bonus, a discount on power bills applied in August, came to an end. Electricity alone added 0.32 points of housing’s 0.35.

Food and drinks rose 0.83% and transport rose 0.89%. Among individual items, tomatoes rose 37.76% and potatoes rose 24.07%.

Services prices rose 0.61% in the month. Administered prices, a group that includes regulated items such as power bills, rose 1.59%.

Fuel and travel also pushed up prices, with gasoline up 1.21%, diesel up 1.69%, ethanol up 3.16% and airfares up 9.66%. All nine groups of the index rose in September.

What Is Not Known

It is not yet clear whether the electricity jump is a one-off or the start of a broader trend. Market economists project inflation to end 2026 at 5.01%, according to the Focus survey of 5 October, a weekly poll of forecasters.

The benchmark Selic interest rate stands at 13.75% a year. The next meeting of the rate committee, known as Copom, is on Wednesday 4 November 2026.

Leonardo Costa of ASA sees room for gradual cuts of 25 basis points, or 0.25 percentage point. Goldman Sachs economist Alberto Ramos recommends a conservative calibration of monetary easing.

The Focus survey median still has the Selic at 13.50% at the end of 2026. How the central bank reads the new inflation figures will be clear only after the November decision.

What It Means for US Readers and Investors

Brazil holds its presidential runoff on 25 October, and the real, Brazilian ADRs and US-listed funds that track Brazilian shares all watch interest rates closely. Higher inflation makes deep rate cuts harder to justify, which keeps borrowing costs high.

The next data points arrive quickly. Services sector figures for August are due on Wednesday 14 October, and retail sales follow on Thursday 15 October, with a forecast of about +0.4% to +0.6%.

The IBC-Br economic activity index for August is due on Friday 16 October, with a forecast of +0.5% after a fall of 0.2% in the prior reading. Readers who want the earlier picture can read Brazil’s July IPCA Inflation Falls Back Inside the Target Band.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Friday 9 October 2026 at 4:55 pm US Eastern (20:55 GMT), Polymarket traders priced a 25 basis point cut at the November central bank meeting at 86.5%, with no change at 8.8% and a cut of 50 basis points or more at 5.5%. That market, titled “Bank of Brazil decision in November?”, had US$49,010 traded.

On Polymarket’s “Brazil Annual Inflation 2026” market, a range of 5.00% to 5.49% was priced at 50.5%, 4.50% to 4.99% at 36.8% and 5.50% to 5.99% at 11.3%, with US$159,406 traded. On Kalshi, which is regulated in the US by the CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission), the market “How high will Brazil inflation get this year?” priced above 4.75% at 75% and above 5.00% at 24%, with 19,138 contracts traded.

These prices are real-money bets, not polls, and each price is an implied probability. They are snapshots from the stated time and can move quickly.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

What was Brazil’s inflation in September 2026?

The IPCA rose 0.82% in September, and the 12-month rate reached 4.58%. That is above the 4.5% ceiling of the government target.

Why did Brazilian prices rise in September?

Electricity rose 7.98% after the Itaipu bonus, a discount on power bills in August, ended. Housing as a whole added 0.35 percentage points to the monthly index.

Will Brazil’s central bank cut interest rates in November?

The Focus survey median has the Selic at 13.50% at the end of 2026, which implies further cuts. Goldman Sachs economist Alberto Ramos recommends a conservative calibration of easing.

What is Brazil’s inflation target?

The target is 3%, with a tolerance of 1.5 percentage points either side. The accepted range is therefore 1.5% to 4.5%.

World.title: Mexico’s Central Bank Warns Remittances Lost 20%
World.content:
Economy: Mexico

Key Facts —Who. Mexican workers abroad, the families who receive their money, and Banxico, Mexico’s central bank —What. A Banxico board member warns remittances have lost more than 20% of their purchasing power over the last year and a half, and August inflows fell 3.6% to US$5.452 billion —Where. Mexico, with the United States as the main source of the money —When. Banxico’s board minutes came out on Thursday 8 October 2026, and its August remittance report on Thursday 1 October 2026 —Why it matters. Money sent home supports household spending in Mexico, and the sender side sits in US workplaces, banks and fintechs —As of. 9 October 2026, 21:00 GMT

A member of Banxico’s governing board has warned that money sent home by Mexican workers abroad lost more than 20% of its purchasing power over the last year and a half. The warning, recorded in minutes published on 8 October, came a week after data showed remittances fell 3.6% in August.

What We Know

Banxico, Mexico’s central bank, published the minutes of its governing-board meeting on Thursday 8 October 2026. They record a member saying that the purchasing power of remittances has fallen by more than 20% over the last year and a half.

The member tied that loss to stagnating consumption in Mexico, according to EFE. Remittances are money sent home by Mexican workers abroad, mostly in the United States, and they help pay for household spending.

EFE, reporting on the minutes, points to exchange-rate moves and inflation as the cause of the erosion. This article does not quote peso exchange-rate figures.

A vendor at a market in Tlacolula, Oaxaca. File photo.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on remittances to Mexico Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the Numbers Show

Banxico’s remittance report, published on Thursday 1 October 2026, put August 2026 inflows at US$5.452 billion. That was 3.6% lower than in August 2025 and the first annual fall since January.

August had 13.2 million transactions, with an average transfer of US$412. That fall followed months of annual increases.

The number of transfers fell 6.4% from a year earlier, while the average amount rose 3.0%. Put simply, fewer transfers were sent, but each one was a little bigger.

From January to August 2026, remittances totalled US$41.802 billion, up 2.2% from the same period of 2025. EFE notes that growth came despite what it calls an aggressive US immigration policy, and the United States is the main source of the money.

Private consumption in Mexico grew only 0.8% in January to June 2026, according to the minutes as reported by EFE. The board member linked that weak spending to the loss of buying power.

What Is Not Known

The minutes as quoted do not explain how the 20% figure was calculated or which prices and exchange rates it uses. We have not seen a breakdown by state or by household income.

It is also unclear whether August’s fall is the start of a trend or a one-month dip. Later monthly reports will show whether growth has really ended.

What It Means for US Readers and Investors

Mexican workers in the United States are the source of these transfers, and the money supports household spending in Mexico. A loss of buying power means each dollar sent home buys less for their families.

US banks and fintechs handle many of these transfers, and we have reported on Bitso, which says it moves about 15% of US remittances to Mexico. Investors in firms tied to this corridor should watch Banxico’s monthly data for further falls in the number of transfers.

The figures also bear on US immigration debates, since they show money still flowing under tougher policy. They do not show how many workers are affected.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much did remittances to Mexico fall in August 2026?

Remittances were US$5.452 billion, down 3.6% from August 2025. It was the first annual fall since January.

What did Banxico say about the value of remittances?

Its minutes, published on Thursday 8 October 2026, record a board member saying remittances lost more than 20% of their purchasing power over the last year and a half. The member linked this to weak consumption.

Are remittances to Mexico still growing this year?

Over the first eight months, yes. From January to August 2026 they reached US$41.802 billion, up 2.2% year on year.

What are remittances?

They are money sent home by Mexican workers abroad, mostly in the United States. The money supports household spending in Mexico.

World.title: Colombia Readies Protest Decree Before Rallies
World.content:
Politics: Colombia

Key Facts —Who. Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara and President Abelardo De La Espriella, with the unions CUT and Fecode on the other side of the debate. —What. A new decree on social protest that modifies Decree 003 of 2021, the protocol for how authorities act at protests. —Where. Colombia, with marches expected in Bogotá and other cities. —When. Signature expected around 9 October 2026; national marches called for Wednesday 14 October 2026. —Why it matters. The rules decide when police may act against violent acts and how road blockades are handled, which affects travellers and business. —As of. 9 October 2026, 21:10 GMT

Colombia's Interior Minister says a new decree on social protest is about to go to President Abelardo De La Espriella for signature. In the reports we saw, the decree was not yet signed, and national marches are planned for Wednesday 14 October 2026.

What We Know

Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara said on 8 October that the new decree on social protest would go to President Abelardo De La Espriella for signature the next day, Friday 9 October, according to Semana. The decree was not yet signed in the reports we saw.

Infobae Colombia gives the signing day as “viernes 11 de octubre”, but 11 October 2026 is a Sunday, an apparent error. Semana points to Friday 9 October.

The decree modifies Decree 003 of 2021, the protocol for how authorities act at protests and protect those who take part. The Interior Ministry published a draft that stayed open for public comment until 4 October 2026.

The ministry also says it held meetings with social organisations, the plaintiffs in the court ruling and the security forces. Infobae summarises Lara’s aim as no fewer rights for those who protest and no more space for those who destroy.

The Capitolio Nacional on Plaza de Bolívar in Bogotá. File photo.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on colombia travel Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the Decree Would Change

According to Infobae, the decree defines violent acts so that they can be separated from peaceful protest. Violent conduct includes aggression against people, throwing objects able to cause serious injury, holding people against their will, and using children in protests.

Dialogue stays the main response of the authorities. However, the decree lists eight grounds on which dialogue is considered exhausted.

Those grounds include blockades of medical missions, harm to public services and the risk of food or medicine shortages. They also cover carrying or using weapons and attacks on medical staff or journalists.

The text sets up “solidarity corridors” meant to prevent permanent road blockades. It also creates five levels of response by the authorities.

The draft text said police may act against individually identified violent acts without waiting for dialogue to end. We have not seen the final wording, so that point could change in the signed version.

Reactions are split. Asocapitales, the association of Colombian capital cities, backed the draft, according to Minuto60, while Senator Jennifer Pedraza says the decree treats protest as a problem, according to El Colombiano.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the president has signed the decree or on which day it takes effect. The final text may also differ from the draft that was open for comment.

Colombian legal press describes five levels of response, from mediators and dialogue up to dispersal. It is not known how police will apply them in practice or who decides when dialogue counts as exhausted.

The size of the 14 October marches is also unclear. The unions CUT, the Central Unitaria de Trabajadores, and the teachers’ federation Fecode have called national mobilisations for that day, and Semana reports that Petro will attend the march.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

Travellers in Bogotá and other cities should expect marches on Wednesday 14 October 2026. They should follow local guidance and the advice of their embassy, and allow extra time for road journeys.

Companies and investors will watch whether the new rules reduce protest-driven road blockades. Rules on blockades matter for freight, supply chains and the daily running of cities.

We reported the draft on 1 October, and the story has moved quickly since. For how the draft treated police action during dialogue, see Colombia Protest Decree Lets Police Act During Dialogue on The Rio Times.

If the decree is signed, the 14 October marches would be the first large protest under the new framework. How authorities and marchers behave that day will show whether the decree calms or sharpens the dispute.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has Colombia's protest decree been signed?

In the reports we saw on 9 October 2026, it had not yet been signed. Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara said it would go to the president for signature.

What does the decree change?

It modifies Decree 003 of 2021, the protocol for how authorities act at protests. It defines violent acts, lists eight grounds on which dialogue is exhausted, and sets five levels of response.

When are the marches in Colombia?

The unions CUT and Fecode called national mobilisations for Wednesday 14 October 2026. Semana reports that former president Gustavo Petro will attend the march.

What should travellers to Colombia do?

Travellers to Bogotá and other cities should expect marches on 14 October. They should follow local guidance and the advice of their embassy.

World.title: Accused killer of Edward ‘Scrubby’ Saldano, Paul Sambula receives full disclosure
World.content:
Accused killer of Edward ‘Scrubby’ Saldano, Paul Sambula receives full disclosure

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Thirty-one-year-old Paul Elver Sambula, accused of the March 2026 murder of well-known Belize City street figure Edward Saldano Jr., also known as “Scrubby,” has been provided with full disclosure of the prosecution’s evidence ahead of his preliminary inquiry.

Sambula, a former call center employee, appeared unrepresented before a Magistrate in Court #3 on Friday afternoon, where he received 162 pages of documents, 16 photographs and 11 DVDs containing evidence that prosecutors intend to rely upon in the murder case.

The Magistrate explained the disclosure process to Sambula and advised him to review the material before returning to court on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, for his preliminary inquiry. At that hearing, Sambula will have an opportunity to challenge the evidence before the matter proceeds toward committal to the High Court.

Sambula was initially arraigned on March 10, 2026, for the murder of 26-year-old Saldano, who was gunned down in broad daylight on March 5 near the intersection of Amara Avenue and Dean Street in Belize City. He was remanded to the Belize Central Prison, where he has remained in custody.

The killing, which was captured on surveillance footage, occurred around 12:30 p.m. as Saldano was riding his bicycle toward Dean Street. Footage showed him confronting and struggling with an armed attacker before being shot. After Saldano collapsed, the gunman allegedly stood over him and fired additional shots. Saldano was rushed to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital, where he died.

Police subsequently indicated that the shooting may have stemmed from internal tensions involving individuals from the George Street area. Investigators reported that threats had allegedly been exchanged before the fatal confrontation.

Sambula, who turned 31 while incarcerated in April, remains on remand and has yet to secure legal representation.

World.title: Four BMW tires and rims valued at $1,500 stolen from Belize City garage
World.content:
Four BMW tires and rims valued at $1,500 stolen from Belize City garage

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating the disappearance of four BMW tires and rims valued at $1,500 from a mechanic’s garage on Amandala Drive.

The owner reported that he discovered the tires missing from St. Martins One Stop garage on Tuesday, October 6.

He told police that the four 16-inch tires, mounted on silver rims, had been stored beside a container inside the garage compound.

He said he last saw the tires approximately one week earlier and discovered them missing when he visited the premises around 7:30 p.m.

He reportedly searched the property and questioned employees and neighboring residents, but nobody could account for the missing items.

Police are investigating the theft.

World.title: Belize expresses solidarity with Panama
World.content:
Belize expresses solidarity with Panama

By Zoila Palma: Today, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement saying that Belize stands in solidarity with the Government and people of the Republic of Panama following the recent earthquakes and the damage sustained by affected communities.

“We extend our solidarity to all those affected during this difficult time. Belize reaffirms its friendship with Panama and joins in the hope for the safety and resilience of its people and the restoration of homes and livelihoods,” the Ministry said.

Panama was shaken by a powerful 7.7 quake around 12:56 pm today.

World.title: Watchman charged after US$3,000 stolen from doctor’s Ladyville residence
World.content:
Watchman charged after US$3,000 stolen from doctor’s Ladyville residence

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A watchman from Patchakan Village, Corozal District, has been arrested and charged with burglary after allegedly stealing US$3,000 from the home of a doctor along the Philip Goldson Highway.

Eloy Cawich was formally charged on Wednesday, October 7, following an investigation into a burglary at the residence of a 71-year-old doctor near Mile 10¼ of the highway.

The doctor reported that his home was burglarized sometime between 1:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. on Sunday, October 4.

He discovered that US$3,000 in various denominations had disappeared from an attaché case kept inside his bedroom.

According to the police report, the doctor identified Cawich, his employee, as the only other person who knew where the money was stored. Nothing else appeared to have been disturbed or stolen.

Investigators determined that entry had been gained by breaking glass louvers on a bathroom window. Crime scene technicians also recovered a fingerprint.

Police subsequently detained Cawich, who allegedly admitted to stealing the money during questioning.

The report further states that investigators conducted a video-recorded interview under caution in the presence of a justice of the peace, during which Cawich allegedly acknowledged entering the residence without permission and taking the money.

He was subsequently charged with burglary.

World.title: Construction worker investigate for attempted murder after allegedly chopping coworker with machete who made a joke about him
World.content:
Construction worker investigate for attempted murder after allegedly chopping coworker with machete who made a joke about him

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating an alleged attempted murder at a worksite along the Coastal Road, where a 19-year-old construction worker was attacked with a machete after making a joking remark about a colleague.

A resident of the Bullet Tree Road area, was injured during an incident at Coconut Point Company near La Democracia on Sunday, October 4.

According to his statement, the man said he was socializing with coworkers and their employer at their living quarters around 7:30 p.m. when he made a joking remark about a colleague known as “Dumbotas”.

The main claimed that the coworkerresponded by threatening to kill him with a machete, but he initially dismissed the threat because everyone had been laughing.

Moments later, while he was smoking a cigarette, he was reportedly struck in the back by a rock.

When he turned around, he allegedly saw his coworker standing a short distance away, swinging a machete toward his face.

The man raised his arm to protect himself and sustained a chop wound to his forearm. He claimed the attacker attempted another blow, but he managed to escape and lock himself inside his room.

The complainant was transported to the Western Regional Hospital, where he remained admitted in stable condition when police compiled their report.

Police detained the attacker, a Guatemalan national residing in Armenia Village, in connection with the attempted murder investigation. He is awaiting charges.

World.title: Department of the Environment assesses Economic impact of Sargassum on Coastal Communities
World.content:
Department of the Environment assesses Economic impact of Sargassum on Coastal Communities

By Zoila Palma: The Department of the Environment (DOE), under the Ministry of Sustainable Development and Climate Change, has hosted a closing workshop on the “Economic Assessment of Sargassum Impacts in Belize.”

The assessment was conducted by Rapid Environmental Assessment (2003) Ltd. (REAL), under the auspices of the DOE and the Central American Commission on Environment and Development (CCAD).

The study aims to establish baseline data on the economic and social effects of Sargassum influxes on Belize’s coastal communities, marine resources, and economic activities. Stakeholders in Placencia, Seine Bight, Hopkins, San Pedro, Ambergris Caye, and Caye Caulker were engaged to assess the impacts on tourism, fisheries, and local livelihoods.

The assessment examined changes in hotel occupancy, bookings, and tourist spending, as well as variations in fish catches, income losses, and increased operating costs for fishers. It also considered disruptions to coastal livelihoods, the costs of adaptation measures, government preparedness, policy gaps, and public spending on Sargassum management.

Representatives from the Ministry of Sustainable Development and Climate Change, the DOE, CCAD, the Taiwan Cooperation, and the Belize Sargassum Task Force participated in the workshop to review the findings and discuss strategies to strengthen Belize’s response.

The DOE emphasized that collaboration among government agencies, coastal communities, and private-sector stakeholders is essential to protecting coastal and marine resources while supporting affected livelihoods.

World.title: International News: Despite re-opening of Strait of Hormuz, fuel prices in U.S. and elsewhere keep rising!
World.content:
International News: Despite re-opening of Strait of Hormuz, fuel prices in U.S. and elsewhere keep rising!

By Zoila Palma: Fuel prices remain elevated around the world despite the recovery of oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, as ongoing conflicts, rising shipping costs and disruptions to refinery operations continue to strain global energy supplies.

Gasoline prices in the United States are averaging US$4.36 per gallon, the highest level recorded for this time of year, while diesel prices remain close to the record high set in September, CNN reports.

Although oil is once again moving through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, shipping through the region remains dangerous and expensive. The cost of hiring a very large crude carrier to transport oil from the Persian Gulf to China has surged from approximately US$65,000 per day last year to US$1.6 million per day.

Rising insurance premiums and payments to sailors willing to travel through conflict zones have added further costs, which are ultimately passed on to consumers and businesses.

Energy experts say the crisis has expanded beyond the initial oil supply disruptions linked to the war involving the United States and Iran.

Attacks by Houthi rebels have disrupted shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, while Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries have affected fuel production.

The high cost of transporting physical oil has also created a significant gap between real-world crude prices and futures market prices.

Experts warn that fuel prices could remain under pressure until geopolitical conflicts ease, shipping becomes safer and global fuel supplies recover.

World.title: Pickup driver dies after crashing into parked cement truck in Orange Walk
World.content:
Pickup driver dies after crashing into parked cement truck in Orange Walk

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a fatal road traffic accident in Orange Walk in which a pickup truck driver lost his life after crashing into the rear of a parked truck carrying cement.

According to information provided during Friday’s police press briefing, the accident occurred on Thursday, October 8, when the pickup collided with the back of the stationary truck.

Investigators said the driver of the cement truck, Rosalio Pineda, had parked his vehicle and was sitting inside when he heard a loud bang. Upon exiting, he discovered that a pickup had slammed into the rear of his truck.

The pickup driver, Jose Miranda, sustained serious injuries and was transported to the hospital, where he later succumbed.

Police indicated that the collision occurred near a gas station in Orange Walk and confirmed that an investigation remains ongoing.

Authorities also said toxicology testing would be conducted following the post-mortem examination as investigators work to determine the circumstances surrounding the deadly collision.

World.title: Market Bag: Sorrel scarce, lettuce reaches $2,000
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — Jamaicans may have to dig deeper into their pockets for one of Christmas’ most beloved staples, as vendors at the Coronation Market warn that sorrel could be both scarce and expensive this year.

The festive favourite, traditionally used to make the popular Christmas drink, would normally be making its way into the market by now. However, sorrel was nowhere in sight when Market Bag visited this week, raising concerns about its availability ahead of the holiday season.

With drought conditions continuing to affect agricultural production, vendors say shoppers could face higher prices this year.

“You might search the whole market and you don’t find it. If you do find it, it’s still gonna have a price,” one vendor warned. “Anytime things get scarce, the less it is, the more the price goes up so I won’t put a fixed price because I’m not sure as yet. But the point still remains: if you pay $1,500 last year, now we have the drought, it would be maybe about $2,000.”

Meanwhile, prices for other produce remain high at Coronation Market this week, with lettuce climbing to as much as $2,000 per pound and plantains selling for $3,000 per dozen. Ripe bananas were going for $1,000 per dozen, while tomatoes were priced at $500 per pound.

Sweet peppers were selling for $400 per pound and Scotch bonnet peppers for $600 per pound. Onions and Irish potatoes dipped to $250 per pound, while sweet potatoes increased slightly to $450 per pound.

Catch the latest episode of Market Bag on all Jamaica Observer digital platforms.

World.title: US announces sanctions on ICC, hours after Nobel award to former judge
World.content:
The Hague; Exterior of International Criminal Court or ICC in the Netherlands

WASHINGTON, United States (AFP) — The United States (US) on Friday announced sanctions on the International Criminal Court, vowing to cripple the tribunal’s operations just hours after the Nobel Peace Prize went to a former ICC judge who warned of mounting political attacks on the court.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington would ban transactions with what he called a “rogue court,” escalating a long-running campaign by President Donald Trump’s administration against the Hague-based tribunal.

“Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC,” Rubio said in a statement.

But the immediate impact of the sanctions was softened by a series of exemptions that offer a de facto six-month grace period.

The State Department said that was meant to give the court’s member states time to show “meaningful progress” toward addressing US concerns.

The grace period could be adjusted depending on the “success or failure” of those efforts, the department added.

The court rejected the US sanctions as an attack on international law and warned in a statement that “history will judge this moment.”

Countries including Canada, France, Germany, Japan and the United Kingdom said in a joint statement that they “strongly disagree” with the announcement.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the US decision “a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar.”

The European Union called the sanctions “deeply regrettable” and said it was “ready to take any necessary measures to enable the court to carry out its work.”

The European Commission, the EU’s executive arm, said it hoped the six-month delay meant “there is room for dialogue.”

Rights group Amnesty International urged countries to “resist” the move, saying the sanctions were “designed to isolate and ultimately destroy” the court.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces an ICC arrest warrant over alleged crimes in Gaza, praised the US action.

“The ICC is not a court. It is a political body that poses a mortal threat to law-abiding democracies worldwide and to the very idea of national sovereignty,” his office posted on X.

The move came on the same day the Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the peace prize to South Africa’s Navi Pillay, an 85-year-old jurist who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal, served on the ICC and later led a UN commission that accused Israel of genocide in Gaza.

Rubio’s statement did not mention Pillay or the Nobel award.

He said the sanctions were needed to protect security personnel and elected officials from prosecution by a court the United States has never joined.

“President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans,” Rubio said, adding that the measures would cut off the court’s resources and cripple “its ability to operate.”

The top US diplomat said Washington had for more than a year spelled out “basic gestures of good faith” it expected from the court, and had held off on the designation in hopes that the ICC or its member states would change course.

He said no “meaningful steps” had been taken to address US concerns.

Rubio also called on US allies that belong to the court and “rely on American service members for their defense” to rein it in, warning that otherwise Washington would keep working to dismantle the ICC “brick by brick.”

The Trump administration had already sanctioned 17 people linked to the court, including its prosecutor and several judges, over the ICC’s investigations involving the United States and Israel, which is also not a member.

Trump last month called on all ICC member states to quit the body, denouncing it as “out of control” and a “rogue institution.”

World.title: Hope, Rutherford fire West Indies to record T20 chase of 250
World.content:
West Indies Romario Shepherd (left) and captain Shai Hope celebrate after winning the second T20 international cricket match between India and West Indies at the JSCA International Stadium Complex in Ranchi on October 9, 2026. (Photo: AFP)

RANCHI, India (AFP) — Skipper Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford struck blazing knocks as the West Indies recorded the second-highest T20 chase of all time on Friday to beat India by six wickets.

After India posted 249-5 batting first, the West Indies rode on a 120-run fourth-wicket partnership between Hope, who hit an unbeaten 102, and Rutherford (84) to achieve the target with nine balls to spare in Ranchi.

Hope completed the win with the ninth six of his innings and one that brought up his century off 45 balls, as the West Indies bounced back to level the five-match series at 1-1.

“When you chase here in India, you always give yourself a chance,” said Hope.

“You always think you’re in the game, regardless of what score is on the board. But (from) 5-2 was always going to be challenging.”

South Africa hold the record for the highest successful run chase in men’s T20 cricket, scoring 259-4 against the West Indies in Centurion in 2023.

West Indies’ previous best chase was when they overhauled 231 by South Africa in Johannesburg in 2015.

Hope and the left-handed Rutherford led an aggressive counter-attack after joining forces with the West Indies 58-3.

Rutherford reached his fifty off 24 balls and kept up the charge before falling to left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav.

He hit seven fours and seven sixes in his 37-ball blitz.

Hope, who struck his second T20 ton, stood firm and put on an unbeaten stand of 74 with Romario Shepherd, who hit 34.

Rutherford later called Hope a “phenomenal player” and one who “inspires” him.

Indian speedster Mayank Yadav struck in the opening over with two successive wickets, including removing Shimron Hetmyer for a first-ball duck.

Yadav also bowled Rovman Powell for 24 with a delivery that clocked 150 km/h (93 mph), but Hope and Rutherford turned the match in the West Indies’ favour.

Earlier, Sanju Samson made 82 off 41 balls before skipper Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma powered India to an imposing total after being asked to bat first.

Iyer said dew played a major part in the West Indies chase.

“The margin of error on this wicket was very minor. Any minor error was going into the stands,” he said.

Samson and Ishan Kishan (43) put on 97 runs for the second wicket after swashbuckling opener Abhishek Sharma departed for 20.

Spinner Roston Chase struck the first blow and then delivered two more — bowling Kishan and Shivam Dube — to check India’s surge.

Pace bowler Shamar Springer dismissed Samson but Iyer and Varma bludgeoned 83 runs off 33 balls for the fifth wicket.

Iyer fell to the penultimate ball of the innings after a rapid 40 off 18 balls while Varma finished unbeaten with 44 in equally quick time.

The third match is on Sunday in Indore.

World.title: JPS says power restored after outage impacts several parishes
World.content:
A Jamaica Public Service (JPS) technician on the job. (File photo)

Jamaica Public Service Company (JPS) is advising that all customers have been restored with electricity following service disruption across several parishes on Friday morning.

The electricity provider said the outage was due to transient trips on the transmission network which also impacted generating units. Adverse weather conditions were being experienced at the time of the trips, JPS said in a release.

All customers were restored by 11:34am following the system disturbance at 10:14am. The cause of the event is being further investigated, JPS said.

Among the parishes impacted, based on reports reaching Observer Online, were Kingston, St Andrew, Manchester, Clarendon and St James.

World.title: WATCH: Tile City launches $290m showroom on Constant Spring Road
World.content:
Tile City and Home Centre launched its state-of-the-art Signature Showroom on Constant Spring Road in St Andrew on Thursday, bringing an immersive experience that the company says opens the door to a fresh approach to building, renovating and designing spaces.

The company invested approximately $290 million in the 10,000 square foot showroom, including $40 million in a 240 kilowatt solar energy system.

Among the guests at the launch were Minister of Industry, Investment and Commerce Senator Aubyn Hill, as well as Minister of State in the Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce, Delano Seiveright.

Seiveright praised Tile City’s growth and the impact the initiative will have on the Jamaican economy.

“I am very proud of Tile City and Home Centre, they have been around for 27 years, they started off with two containers and here there are now with this massive showroom,” Seiveright said. “We are excited about it, they have created jobs, they have created opportunities and their reach spreads throughout the entire Jamaican economy.”

According to the company, the grand opening celebrates more than a new space, noting that it represents a renewed commitment to inspiring creativity, making quality design more accessible and helping Jamaicans bring their visions for their homes and projects to life.

World.title: ‘Just know it wasn’t me’: Cardi B addresses cancelled BZR WKND performance
World.content:
Cardi B performs during halftime during Game Three of the 2026 NBA Finals between the San Antonio Spurs and the New York Knicks on June 8, 2026 at Madison Square Garden in New York, New York. (Photo: AFP)

American rapper Cardi B has broken her silence following the cancellation of her highly anticipated performance at BZR WKND in Jamaica, apologising to disappointed fans while insisting that the circumstances surrounding her withdrawal were beyond her control.

In a video message shared on Friday morning, the Bodak Yellow hitmaker said she had initially intended to let the official cancellation statement speak for itself but felt compelled to address the situation amid speculation about the reason for her withdrawal.

“Good morning, I wasn’t really gonna address this because I felt like the statement was enough, but clearly it wasn’t. First things first, I want to really, really apologise to Jamaica and to my Jamaican fans. The reason why I cancelled so late is because when I say I tried my best and I waited and I waited and I waited for things to get in place and together, but it didn’t,” she said.

The Grammy-winning artiste explained that she had been looking forward to visiting the island, particularly as the trip coincided with her birthday celebrations. She revealed that she had made arrangements to extend her stay in Jamaica for a vacation with friends and family following the performance.

“I’m actually sad that I’m not able to go to Jamaica because this weekend is my birthday weekend. So I made plans for next weekend cause after my performance, I was planning to vacation with my friends and my family members for a couple of more days after my performance, which clearly that’s not happening,” she continued.

Cardi B also dismissed speculation that poor ticket sales had prompted the cancellation, claiming that more than 18,000 tickets had been sold for the event.

“For the haters, not the Jamaicans, but for the haters talking about due to low ticket sales, it was never that because I heard there was over 18,000 tickets sold and not only that, but it’s like be for real I’m Cardi B. I’ve done sold out in Saudi Arabia, in Thailand, everywhere around the world and not only was Jamaica was going to pop out for Cardi B, you have people from different Caribbean islands that were going, from The Bahamas to the Dominican Republic to St Lucia…Everybody was going to come see me.”

While the rapper stopped short of revealing the specific issues that led to her withdrawal, she suggested that contractual restrictions prevented her from disclosing further details.

“However, I can’t talk. I can’t talk…contracts, but just know it wasn’t me. Just know. And I’m sorry. I tried my best. I waited this long because I was trying to give chances over and over and over and over and over and over and over again and things didn’t meet to the point that it’s like, it would have just, it’s just, oh, I don’t want to say much,” she said.

Despite the setback, Cardi B expressed hope that she would eventually get the opportunity to perform for her Jamaican fans.

“Just know that I’m sorry. And I really, really, really wish that I could come and perform in Jamaica one day because I really love you guys. I have an amazing fan base out there and I’m sorry. And I love you and sh*t is beyond my hands. I promise y’all,” she ended the video saying.

News of the American rapper’s withdrawal broke on Thursday afternoon, just over a week before her scheduled October 18 performance at the National Stadium in Kingston.

Cardi B had been announced as the headline act for BZR WKND, which is scheduled to run from October 16 to 18.

World.title: MELISSA FRAUD SHIELD
World.content:
One of a number of houses in Unions Acres, St James, still waiting for repair to the damage caused by last year’s Hurricane Melissa.

LASCO Financial Services has revealed that it began holding back 30 per cent of donations made through the Government’s Hurricane Melissa relief platform after its system flagged as suspicious, a number of transactions linked to the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management (ODPEM).

LASCO said it remitted 70 per cent of the money received to ODPEM daily while the reserve was being held, with more than 95 per cent of all donated amounts having been paid over to the agency by the end of March, before the 30 per cent withholding was discontinued in June after the risk associated with the account returned to normal.

The disclosure provides a new explanation for the arrangement, which came under scrutiny after the Auditor General’s Department found that 30 per cent of online donations had been retained for up to 45 days by a financial services institution, without a formal written agreement governing the retention.

The audit found that $15.7 million and US$298,429 in donations withheld between October 28 and December 31, 2025 were due to be transferred to ODPEM by February 15, 2026.

However, the financial services institution told auditors on March 9 that none of the withheld funds had yet been transferred.

Four days later, ODPEM provided a transfer receipt showing that $16.1 million and US$305,292 had been sent on March 9, but the auditor general said she could not independently confirm that the money had reached ODPEM’s accounts because the agency had not provided the relevant bank statements.

LASCO Financial, in a July 31 letter to Public Accounts Committee (PAC) Chairman Julian Robinson, said the decision to retain the money followed a review of the risk associated with the account after its payment system detected suspicious activity.

According to the company, the 30 per cent was not treated as money belonging to it, but as a refundable security reserve intended to protect against possible losses arising from disputed or fraudulent card transactions.

The company said a July 8, 2024 agreement with ODPEM expressly provided for a refundable security reserve, but no reserve was instituted at the time, based on the risk assessment then in place.

LASCO Financial said the 45-day period was based on guidance from its banking partners, who advised that this was the period within which a customer could challenge a transaction.

“If a charge-back occurred due to ODPEM transactions, without reserve, LASCO would have to absorb full loss,” the company said, adding that the arrangement was “standard practice by financial institutions in these types of transactions”.

A charge-back occurs when a card transaction is challenged and the money is reversed through the banking system.

LASCO said the reserve was therefore intended to ensure that money would be available if a transaction processed through the donation platform was later disputed and reversed.

The company said the donation button remained active on the Government’s Support Jamaica website and continued to receive contributions, while the withholding arrangement was eventually discontinued in June after the risk associated with the account had returned to normal levels.

The latest explanation comes after the issue was raised during a meeting of the PAC on July 28 at which questions were asked about why a financial institution had been allowed to retain a portion of disaster donations and whether there was a formal agreement authorising the arrangement.

At that meeting, ODPEM Director General Commander Alvin Gayle told the PAC that the funds, which had prompted the auditor general’s concern, had since been received by the agency.

Gayle also acknowledged that there had been no formal arrangement specifically governing the retention of Hurricane Melissa funds, even though there was an existing agreement covering the processing of donations.

In a subsequent August 31 response from the Office of the Prime Minister (OPM) to questions from the committee, the Government said the legal teams of ODPEM and LASCO were still discussing the terms of the agreement.

The OPM also told the PAC that ODPEM selected LASCO after assessing the available payment-processing options.

It said LASCO is currently the only financial services provider with which Amber Innovations Inc — the company behind the relevant licensed payment products — has granted a non-exclusive licence for a payment-based solution to merchants.

World.title: ‘I don’t shy away from court’
World.content:
Attorney Hugh Wildman speaking at a news conference on Thursday. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

Attorney Hugh Wildman on Thursday insisted that he would never deliberately stay way from the fraud trial of his client Fritz Pinnock in the St Andrew Parish Court, but said his involvement in the murder case of six cops in the Home Circuit Court, downtown Kingston, has been creating unavoidable scheduling clashes due to the latter matter being dragged out by the prosecution.

Wildman was defending himself at a news conference he called a day after Justice Sanchia Burrell told Pinnock that he may have to cross-examine a witness himself if no legal representation is present for him when the delay- plagued Ruel Reid and company fraud trial resumes next Monday.

“Today’s press conference is called to respond to the media reports and various comments concerning the Pinnock and Reid matter, where the judge made certain comments in my absence and gave the impression that I deliberately stayed away from the court.

I wish to make it abundantly clear that everybody in Jamaica knows my position; I don’t shy away from court,” Wildman said.

“In fact, I am known to appear in all courts and take a certain stand to defend my clients vigorously,” he said.

“The situation is this: It is a known fact that we are engaged in the trial of the six police in downtown since the 7th of January of this year.

When the case commenced, the trial judge [Sonia Bertram- Linton] made it abundantly clear that she got instructions from the chief justice that that case must be a priority case; that’s what she told us,” Wildman said.

He said that in all his years of practising law he has never seen a situation in which a murder trial is dragged out by the prosecution the way that the policemen’s matter has been.

“The case has been going on unnecessarily long because of the conduct of the prosecutor in recalling and recalling witnesses, evidence to adduce new evidence, and it goes on and on, uncontrolled.

It amounts to an abuse of process.

The case continues and continues, and nobody knows when this case will come to an end,” he said.

“Everybody in the justice system knows about this.

In fact, we have had cases in court where Supreme Court judges have said they know Mr Wildman is engaged in other matters, and they put off the case.

Up to this week…

The point is this, I explained to Ms Burrell the challenge we are having with the downtown case, which is a priority.

It’s a murder case with six policemen.

I’m representing four of the accused persons,” he said, emphasising that, “It is impossible for me to be at two places at the same time.” On Wednesday in the Parish Court, fellow defence attorney Carolyn Chuck told Justice Burrell that Wildman had advised that he would ask another attorney to hold in his stead; but no one turned up.

Chuck went on to share that Wildman had indicated that he could also have challenges with being present next week as he was given time off from the Supreme Court to deal with the arrangements for his mother’s funeral.

Justice Burrell acknowledged the sensitivity of the matter and extended condolence to Wildman’s family.

However, she queried why this had not been communicated before.

“I don’t take lightly that Mr Wildman is making funeral arrangements for his mother, and my condolence goes out to him and his family, but early information- sharing makes a huge difference,” she said.

“I have to be very sensitive because all of us who are here either have a mother or had a mother at some point…

but I am not understanding the lack of communication; the lack of communication is very unhelpful,” the judge said.

Emphasising that the case impacts four other accused, Burrell said Wildman and Pinnock are not entitled to an infinite supply of the court’s resources.

Her comments came on the one-year anniversary of the official start of the trial, which has been plagued with scheduling challenges.

“It cannot be that Mr Wildman avoids appropriate and adequate communication and expects to get what he asks for,” she said.

“How can the rights of four other people be expected to continuously and infinitely, at this point in time, … be expected to yield to Mr Wildman’s failure — I am using the word failure — to organise himself?” Justice Burrell said.

Pinnock, the former Caribbean Maritime University head; former education minister Ruel Reid; his wife Sharen Reid and daughter Sharelle; as well as Councillor Kim Brown Lawrence (Jamaica Labour Party, Brown’s Town Division) are defendants in the high-profile $25-million fraud trial in the parish court.

In the matter being heard in the Home Circuit Court, the six policemen are on trial for murder in relation to the January 12, 2013 shooting deaths of Matthew Lee, Ucliffe Dyer, and Mark Allen on Acadia Drive in St Andrew, during an alleged shoot-out.

On Thursday, Wildman said he was trying to find a solution to his problem, telling the news conference that he has written a letter to Chief Justice Bryan Sykes urging his intervention.

“I was shocked when I heard that the judge was behaving like that, as if I deliberately stayed away from court.

Everybody knows that that is not my style.

I want to be there to defend my client, Mr Pinnock, and defend him vigorously, because we maintain that there is no case against him.

But the point is that I am locked in that trial downtown.

What do I do?” he said.

“Should I have walked away from the criminal case downtown with the six policemen? I don’t know why this is taking so long.

Every day, up to yesterday, I made serious submissions in law based on the constitution, that the trial is an abuse of process with what is going on downtown,” he said.

World.title: UK bans Protestant march from Catholic area in Northern Ireland
World.content:
“I call for all protests, rallies and demonstrations to be stood down. There is no excuse for a continued ratcheting up of tensions,” Bryant appealed in a statement explaining why he was reversing the original decision by the Parades Commission, Northern Ireland’s independent body for managing the region’s chronic conflicts over Orange Order demonstrations.

Street fighting over those traditional marches helped to trigger the onset of Northern Ireland’s three-decade conflict, known as “The Troubles,” which left nearly 3,700 dead before a 1998 peace accord.

Hundreds of Catholic locals backed by Sinn Féin, the Irish republican party that leads Northern Ireland’s fraying cross-community government, gathered along the Garvaghy Road in Portadown to cheer the reversal.

First Minister Michelle O’Neill, who has been accused of breaking the law while helping locals block the Orangemen’s intended path since Sept. 27, went on Ireland’s flagship TV talk show, the Late Late Show, to express relief on behalf of the residents of Garvaghy Road.

“For the last 13 days they’ve been living with this constant fear and a cloud hanging over them that this unwanted sectarian march was going to be forced down that road,” she said.

But the main pro-British party in the coalition, the Democratic Unionists, denounced Bryant’s move as a capitulation to mob rule. Some DUP lawmakers called for Northern Ireland’s police chief, who had recommended the policy reversal, to be fired.

Democratic Unionist leader Gavin Robinson said the U.K. government had sent a dangerous message that Northern Ireland “should be run on force of numbers and who shouts the loudest.”

Northern Ireland’s nearly three-decade system for managing conflict over parades “now lies in tatters,” he said, “and the rule of law has been fundamentally undermined.”

World.title: Arrested German spy chief lashed out at his old agency over allegations he spied for Russia
World.content:
Jäger did not respond to the letter at the time, according to Hanning, who spoke to WELT before his arrest.

Hanning’s subsequent arrest, including on suspicion of attempted treason, has caused considerable concern abroad. Grzegorz Malecki, the former head of Poland’s foreign intelligence service, told WELT that the case was “extremely concerning” and could deepen allies’ distrust of the BND. He warned this had the potential to undermine intelligence-sharing with Germany.

The BND has also raised eyebrows within Germany’s intelligence community over allegations that it allowed Hanning’s former chief of staff, who is also in custody, to work for Hanning outside his official duties.

While civil servants are generally permitted to take on outside employment, any approval allowing a member of the BND to work for Hanning would have had to be decided at the senior management level, said Günter Heiss, a former intelligence coordinator under former Chancellor Angela Merkel. “Without knowing the details, I would never have approved anything like this had I been in a position of responsibility at the BND.”

Bernd Schmidbauer, a former minister of state and intelligence coordinator under Chancellor Helmut Kohl, told WELT that Hanning had made major contributions to Germany’s national security. The affair was therefore “not only a tragedy for the German intelligence services, but also for the former senior official himself,” Schmidbauer said.

Hanning was among Schmidbauer’s closest aides during the 1990s and went on to lead the BND from 1998 to 2005.

Dirk Banse is an investigative reporter at WELT. Philipp Fritz is WELT’s Eastern Europe correspondent. Uwe Müller is a freelance reporter based in Berlin.
