World.title: Estonia plans to add photos of pedophile offenders to criminal records database
World.content:
The Ministry of Justice has sent for approval a draft law that would display document‑style photos in the criminal records database of people who have a restriction on working with children.

Displaying a photo in the criminal records database helps employers, a child's legal representative, and the Social Insurance Board ensure that the query result concerns the correct person. The change is important, for example, when a parent hires a private tutor for a child and finds the tutor's personal identification code from public sources. A photo also helps identify a person if a job applicant states or writes their personal identification code but does not present an identity document.

The restriction on working with children applies to a person who has committed a contact sexual offense against a child, such as rape.

The aim of the amendment is to protect children better than before from sexual and other dangerous offenders. Currently, employers must check at least once a year in the criminal records database whether a person working with children has a restriction on working with children.

"The easier and more convenient it is to fulfill such an obligation, the more likely employers are to actually do it," the draft states.

Checks will become automatic and more frequent

In the future, an employer will not have to enter the name and personal identification code of a person working with children into the criminal records database once a year. Instead, the system will automatically check people working with children once a month. For this, the automatic check will be linked to the employment register, and the employer must indicate which employees come into direct contact with children.

The employer will receive the result of the check as a simple yes‑or‑no answer. If an employee has a restriction on working with children, the Social Insurance Board will also be notified and will check whether the employer has complied with the restriction.

A person working with a child is someone who, due to their job or activity, comes into direct contact with a child. This means communicating with the child, guiding, teaching, caring for, counseling, or dealing with the child while providing a service.

Such people include, for example, teachers, coaches, kindergarten staff, and others whose duties require direct contact with children. A person may also be considered to be working with children if they work in an institution not intended solely for children but still come into direct contact with children due to their job.

At the same time, not everyone who encounters children is considered to be working with children. For example, a shop assistant, customer service worker, or a regular city bus driver is generally not considered a person working with children, because their job does not require direct and continuous interaction with children.

It is different, for example, for a school bus or excursion bus driver who transports a specific group of children and comes into more direct contact with them due to their job. The final assessment is made by the employer, who must consider the person's duties and their nature.

The draft notes that in practice there have been situations where people with a restriction on working with children have ended up working as school janitors or bus drivers.

Automatic checks can only cover people working in positions where they come into direct contact with children. Therefore, a person must be removed from the list of people to be checked as soon as they stop performing such work.

The records database will not become public

The ministry refers in the draft to studies showing that public sex‑offender registries have not had a positive impact on reducing repeat offenses. Some studies do indicate that a public registry may reduce the risk of first‑time offenses. According to the ministry, adding photos may help people recognize a dangerous individual and warn their close ones.

However, adding photos does not make the registry public. Queries can still be made only by persons specified in the law: employers, institutions issuing activity licenses for working with children, and a child's legal representatives.

The planned date for the law to enter into force is 1 June 2030.

World.title: Warnings before mobile traffic cameras reduced fines by 90 percent
World.content:
Speeding fines have dropped nearly 90% since July's higher intervention threshold and the August rollout of warning signs before mobile speed cameras. But the police says safer road design, not enforcement, is the real key to improving traffic safety.

The higher intervention threshold for speeding, which took effect in July, brought a drop of more than half in speeding violations. The impact of the warning signs introduced in August in front of mobile speed cameras has been even more noticeable — according to data from the first full month of use, the detection of violations has decreased by approximately 90 percent.

If in September of last year mobile speed cameras issued 26,228 fines, then in September of this year mobile cameras across Estonia issued a total of 2,939 fines, according to police statistics.

"This September there were two fewer cameras operating compared to last year, and part of the working time was spent installing warning signs, but this does not change the overall picture — the number of fines today is very small," said the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) spokesperson Uku Tampere.

Most drivers comply with speed limits

PPA traffic‑supervision chief Taavi Kirss explained that placing warning signs before mobile cameras has made their effect similar to stationary speed cameras.

"At the specific location where there is a speed camera with a warning sign, speeds are correctly reduced, and it is safer there, and violations generally do not occur," Kirss said. At the same time, he noted that once drivers leave the camera's area of influence, they often accelerate back to their usual speed. "If traffic supervision is not visible, there is no risk of being caught," he said.

Taavi Kirss. Source: ERR

According to the Transport Administration's latest survey, 77 percent of drivers comply with the speed limit, but for the rest, speeding remains a problem, Kirss noted.

According to Kirss, installing warning signs has not been without practical issues. Problems have been identified with placing signs in the landscape, and there have been situations where large trucks passing by have knocked the signs over.

The reduction in fines — and thus fine revenue — does not concern the police. "We have not looked at it, and fine revenue is not important from the police perspective. Our goal is directed at safety and reducing traffic accidents," Kirss emphasized.

Asked whether the police, having lost one effective method of catching speeders, plan to bring more patrols onto the roads or use alternative measures, Kirss answered no.

"The number of patrols will not increase; it remains the same as it has always been," he confirmed. Traffic will continue to be calmed with existing tools: mobile and stationary speed cameras and daily police patrols.

A mobile speed camera on the side of the road in Estonia. Source: ERR

Safe infrastructure replaces supervision

The police's main expectation for lawmakers is to make the traffic environment and infrastructure safer. According to Kirss, logical and safe infrastructure reduces the direct need for police supervision, because movement in such an environment is inherently safer and more understandable for drivers.

As a successful example, he pointed to Tallinn, where speed limits in the city center were lowered in 2024.

"Initially, this reduced pedestrian‑related traffic accidents by about 50 percent. Today it has remained around 30 percent, and I think that is a very good number," Kirss said.

On highways, the police consider most important the construction of roads where lanes are separated and the risk of head‑on collisions is minimized.

"Places where different road users can move in their own lanes are significantly safer than those where speeds differ and the risk of collision is high," he added.

Since 1 July, the PPA raised the intervention threshold for mobile speed cameras. Mobile cameras now issue fines only starting from 6 km/h over the limit (previously 3 km/h), to avoid penalizing momentary carelessness. The change applies only to PPA‑operated mobile speed cameras, of which there are eight across Estonia. Stationary cameras still intervene starting at 3 km/h over the limit.

In May, three MPs — Valdo Randpere, Madis Timpson, and Marek Reinaas — initiated a law amendment requiring the police to use a warning sign before a mobile speed camera. The amendment was adopted despite police objections and entered into force on 1 August.

World.title: Expert: Longer lifespans should mean longer working lives
World.content:
The retirement age in Estonia must rise together with life expectancy so that the pension system remains sustainable and different generations spend roughly the same amount of time in retirement, says Lauri Leppik, professor of social and population policy at Tallinn University.

"If people live longer, then they must also work longer. We see that as of 2026, Estonia has about 315,000 old‑age pensioners. If we add other types of pensions, then almost every fourth person in Estonia is a pensioner," Leppik said.

"Of course, this is a burden on the state. If the retirement age had not been raised, then soon every third person here would be a pensioner. So this decision was necessary from the standpoint of the burden on the working population."

In 2026, the retirement age in Estonia is 65, applying to people born in 1961. Starting next year, the retirement age will be tied to the expected life expectancy of people aged 65.

"This means that if 65‑year‑olds live longer than before, then the retirement age will rise accordingly. In other words, it is specifically the life expectancy at age 65 that is taken into account," Leppik explained.

A nuance that was overlooked

When the law on old‑age retirement was adopted, a transition to a new system was also foreseen, where the retirement age is determined by calendar years. The minister of social affairs approved the retirement age for the next two years: 65 years and 1 month in 2027, and 65 years and 3 months in 2028.

"But it turns out that only people born from January to November 1962 can retire in 2027. Those born in December 1962 will reach retirement age only in 2028, when it will not be 65 years and 1 month, but 65 years and 3 months. This means they can retire only in March 2028 — their retirement age is two months higher," Leppik said.

"It's hard to say why this happened; I did not participate in those discussions, but it seems that when the transition to the new system was being discussed, this nuance was not noticed," he added.

Lauri Leppik. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Out of 100 men, 80 will reach retirement age

After the restoration of Estonia's independence, women retired at 55 and men at 60 for some time. Now the ages have equalized.

"Women's retirement age has risen by 10 years during this period, and men's by five. But average life expectancy has also risen significantly over 30 years. In 1995, women lived an average of 74 years, and now more than 83. For men, average life expectancy in 1995 was only 61 years, and now more than 75. So women's average life expectancy has increased by almost 10 years, and men's by 14," the professor explained.

According to Leppik, men's chances of reaching retirement age are now much higher — almost 80%. That means out of 100 men, 80 will reach retirement age, and for women the figure is 91%.

"Of course, people's lives differ: there are long‑lived individuals who reach 100, and there are those whose lives are quite short. There are significant individual differences in life expectancy," he added.

Historically, women's retirement age in Estonia was lower than men's. Now the ages have equalized because Europe follows the principle of gender equality.

"At the same time, men who reach 65 have about 16 years left based on average life expectancy. Women have more than 20. So in retirement age, the difference in life expectancy is about five years," Leppik said.

Estonia has a lot of working retirees

Estonia ranks among the top European countries in employment rates among people of retirement age.

"In many cases, people are forced to work to ensure a sufficient standard of living. On the other hand, people with higher education — for example teachers or doctors — can continue working and choose to do so in retirement. There are also many in Estonia who lose their jobs before reaching retirement age and cannot continue working either for health reasons or because they cannot find work," he said.

"It is also true that the indicator of healthy years is low. But subjective factors influence it as well — for example, Estonian residents tend to be quite critical when assessing their own health."

Leppik noted that no sharp improvements in Estonia's state pension system are expected, so people must prepare themselves and use all available opportunities before reaching retirement age.

World.title: Northeastern Estonian cities question value of participatory budgeting
World.content:
Narva and Narva-Jõesuu are both reconsidering participatory budgeting as residents' proposals continue to prove too costly or vague to carry out.

Narva-Jõesuu has run the process nine times, spending €30,000 a year on projects including sidewalk repairs, fountains and a shorefront Wisdom Trail dotted with display boards featuring quotes from famous figures. But city officials say public interest is waning, ideas are getting repetitive and many proposals are simply too expensive.

"Over the past three years at least, the same proposal has come up again and again: let's renovate the resort hall," Mayor Maksim Iljin said, noting that €30,000 is nowhere near enough to overhaul the long-abandoned building.

"It's clear participatory budgeting has run its course in Narva-Jõesuu," he added.

Iljin said the city should instead focus on supporting local nonprofits and community organizations.

Narva, meanwhile, has spent up to €300,000 a year on participatory budgeting, but some winning projects have proved too expensive to complete, including Paju Park on Rakvere tänav and a boat ramp on Jõe tänav.

No new big projects

The city paused the collection of new proposals two years ago and now believes the annual participatory budget should be slashed to a tenth of its current size to focus on smaller projects.

"That's the problem — people come up with these big ideas that end up requiring public procurements and quotes," said Narva City Council chair Urbo Vaarmann.

He argued that unfinished projects should be completed before the city starts over with a new approach focused on "nice little projects."

In Narva-Jõesuu, the fate of participatory budgeting is on the city council agenda later this month. Narva city officials, meanwhile, are expected to make a decision within the next four months.

World.title: Defense Intel Chief: Russia targeting Ukraine's railways and Dnipro bridges in escalating strike campaign
World.content:
Moscow has introduced a new tactic and is attempting, through extensive long‑range strikes, to break Ukraine's infrastructure and the population's psychological resilience, says Col. Ants Kiviselg, head of the EDF Intelligence Center.

Kiviselg said at Estonian MoD briefing on Friday that in the battlespace, the downward trend in the number of combat contacts has continued, Russia continues to suffer heavy losses, and both sides continue long‑range strikes into each other's rear areas.

During this week, about 200 combat contacts per day have taken place, he noted.

"The most intense fighting has occurred in the same areas as in recent weeks: in Donetsk, the Pokrovsk and Konstantynivka directions; in Kharkiv oblast, the Southern Slobozhanske direction; in Zaporizhzhia, the Hulyaipole direction; and in Donetsk also the Lyman direction. Ukraine's counterattacks have continued in the Kupiansk direction in Kharkiv oblast, and in Donetsk in the Sloviansk, Lyman, and Kramatorsk directions," Kiviselg said.

"Losses of the Russian Federation have remained at an average of around 1,700 soldiers per day, which means the sixth consecutive week with more than 10,000 killed or wounded fighters per week. In response, Russia is slightly changing its behavior pattern: attempts are being made to break Ukraine's unity with intensive and very long‑lasting long‑range strikes," the military intel chief said.

Kiviselg pointed out that on 4 October Russia announced its intention to intensify long‑range strikes on Ukraine, and during the past 241st week such strikes hit various targets in 13 Ukrainian oblasts, followed in many places by power outages.

Ukraine setting up air defenses

Russia also repeatedly attacked bridges over the Dnipro River — both in Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia — attempting to intimidate civilians, hinder everyday life in Ukraine, and thereby affect the economy.

"In Kyiv, air‑defense systems operating with artificial intelligence have begun to be placed to protect the bridges, and alternative solutions are being sought in case traffic on the bridges is halted for a longer period; the possibility of installing pontoon bridges over the Dnipro river is also being examined," Kiviselg said.

Kiviselg noted that according to Ukrainian data, about 330 educational institutions in Kyiv have been damaged in airstrikes during the war — roughly one‑third of all educational institutions there — and in the first eight months of this year, 107 educational institutions have been hit.

"Ukraine's rail transport is also in a very difficult situation. More than 500 locomotives have been damaged during the war, and this year alone 60 percent of them have been hit. Attacks against railway infrastructure are 40 percent higher this year than during the entire year 2025. So we see that Russia has intensified attacks both against educational institutions and against railway and transport hubs," Kiviselg said.

"Ukraine, for its part, has carried out medium‑ and long‑range strikes against Russian fuel‑industry facilities in Volgograd, Nizhny Novgorod, Samara, and Moscow oblast. Military‑strategic targets have also been attacked in occupied areas in Krasnodar, and in Bryansk and Oryol oblasts, and in the Republic of Adygea," he said.

Russia's fuel exports diminished

According to Kiviselg, the impact of Ukraine's long‑range strikes has begun to clearly appear in Russia's fuel exports. If in 2025 Black Sea ports exported an average of 200,000 tons of fuel per week, then according to public data this transport fell to zero in the third week of September. "Russia's diesel and gas‑oil exports are currently taking place through the Baltic Sea port of Primorsk and amount to about 81,000 tons," Kiviselg said.

Kiviselg said that between 1 and 30 September, Ukraine liberated, according to public sources, 25 to 80 square kilometers of territory, compared with last September, when Russia occupied 258 square kilometers.

"The trend is changing significantly, and last September Russia did not suffer such extensive losses as this year. Speaking of Operation Vivaldi, which began by the Ukrainians in late spring, it is likely that much larger areas have been liberated there — we are talking about more than 100 square kilometers," Kiviselg said.

Kiviselg emphasized that the Russian Federation has not come any closer to its stated goal of occupying the entire Donetsk oblast.

"Large personnel losses reflect rather that unit leaders and commanders on the ground are trying to fight their way to lines that have already been reported to higher leadership as occupied areas. We will likely see similar intensity in the coming weeks — perhaps intensity will decrease, but personnel losses on the front will continue. From this we also see that Putin's statements, as if Russians had additionally occupied 1,300 square kilometers during September, are not true; these are rather doomed attempts by commanders to achieve previously advertised results," Kiviselg commented.

World.title: ICC Iraq joins Saudi corporate social responsibility forum ahead of Baghdad event
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The International Chamber of Commerce in Iraq (ICC Iraq) is planning to hold a forum on corporate social responsibility and business sustainability in Baghdad on November 1 after its participation in a major international conference in Saudi Arabia.

An ICC Iraq team attended the Global CSR Forum 2026, which took place in Riyadh on October 5-6 and was organized by Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development.

The event drew over 3,000 attendees and 100 presenters from across the globe, with over 40 sessions addressing corporate social responsibility, sustainable business practices, and international collaboration.

ICC Iraq said that its participation was intended to develop ties with foreign organizations and share experience ahead of the Iraqi Forum for Social Responsibility and Business Sustainability, which is set for November 1 in Baghdad.

The next workshop is planned to provide a venue for conversations about how Iraqi firms may integrate social responsibility and sustainability into their operations.

The program comes as Iraq strives to enhance its private sector and attract foreign investment, with a focus on corporate governance, environmental norms, and firms’ role in economic growth.

ICC Iraq’s presence at the Riyadh event demonstrates attempts to link Iraqi firms with international organizations and offer worldwide expertise in responsible business practices to the local market.

World.title: Asian stocks mixed amid AI concerns, oil dips after surge
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks headed into the weekend on a mixed note on Friday with tech weighed by renewed concerns about the AI investment boom, while support came from a drop in oil prices after Donald Trump ruled out a pre-election strike on Iran.

The outlook for artificial intelligence has provided a fresh boost to the tech sector in recent weeks, with some optimism for the upcoming earnings season. Chip titan Nvidia this week hit a record high and closed in on the $6 trillion market capitalisation.

That was dealt a blow by a Financial Times report saying OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, expected to make $50 billion in annualised revenue this year, far less than the $70 billion flagged previously.

“For most of this boom, the market has been happy to follow the money going in. Bigger data centres, more GPUs, more memory, more power, more debt, more capex,” wrote Stephen Innes at SPI Asset Management.

“Every fresh spending commitment became another brick in the bullish wall because the assumption underneath it was simple enough: if the industry is prepared to spend this much, the demand will eventually justify it.

“Then OpenAI handed the market a number that made traders look at the other side of the ledger.”

Wall Street’s Nasdaq ended more than one percent lower, with Nvidia down nearly three percent, while Microsoft, AMD and Amazon among others sharply lower.

However, Chris Weston at Pepperstone added that “the discrepancy may reflect differences in revenue measurement rather than an outright deterioration in OpenAI’s underlying business”.

Still, he said, “in a market where valuations are increasingly dependent on ambitious revenue and cash flow projections, the headlines have been enough to trigger a meaningful one-day repositioning”.

In Asia, Tokyo sank with tech investing titan SoftBank losing more than four percent, while Kioxia and Advantest were also well down.

Shanghai and Singapore were also down, though Hong Kong, Sydney, Wellington, Manila and Jakarta were all up.

Seoul and Taipei — both heavily weighted with tech firms — were closed for holidays.

Traders took a little heart from a dip in oil prices after US President Donald Trump ruled out hitting Iran before the midterm elections, saying Washington was holding “productive discussions” with Tehran.

His remarks came after reports said the White House had asked the Pentagon to draw up plans for a possible attack ahead of the November 3 vote, hoping a show of strength might help struggling Republicans’ chances.

Both main contracts were down around 0.7 percent Friday, though that is after they fell as much as four percent on concerns about increased Iranian strikes in the Strait of Hormuz.

That comes on top of Yemen’s Houthis taking aim at Riyadh airport with missiles and warning staff at oil facilities in Saudi Arabia to leave to avoid being targeted as hostilities escalate.

Comments from Fed officials cemented expectations for another interest rate hike before the end of the year, though this month appears unlikely.

Governor Christopher Waller said more tightening was likely necessary to bring prices under control, while St. Louis Fed boss Alberto Musalem eyed increases over the next six to nine months.

Still, National Australia Bank’s Ken Crompton said: “Whilst this is a touch hawkish relative to his (Waller’s) recent record, he’s still in close accord with (Vice Chair Philip) Jefferson and (New York Fed chief John) Williams last week, who collectively (in addition to the inflation data) helped cool market pricing of an October hike from 15 basis points to less than five basis points.”

World.title: James shines in pre-season debut for re-tooled 76ers
World.content:
New York – NBA superstar LeBron James delivered a solid first half in his first pre-season game for Philadelphia on Thursday, but the new-look 76ers fell 114-108 to the Nets in Brooklyn.

James, the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, announced in July that he had signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the 76ers, ending weeks of speculation over where the four-time NBA champion would land as a free agent after eight seasons and one title with the Los Angeles Lakers.

The 41-year-old superstar, entering a record-extending 24th NBA season, won two titles with Miami, another with Cleveland and a fourth with the Lakers and is aiming to help the Sixers win their first title since Julius Erving led the club to the crown 43 years ago.

Thursday’s game marked his first chance to line up alongside new teammates Joel Embiid, VJ Edgecombe, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown — a new arrival from the Boston Celtics.

James scored 10 points, connecting on his lone shot from the floor and making all eight of his free-throw attempts. He added four rebounds, five assists and a steal in 18:04 minutes in the first half.

Brown led all scorers with 18 points. Julius Randle had 14 for the Nets, who out-scored the Sixers 37-23 in the third quarter to take control.

But all eyes were on James, starting with his first signature pre-game chalk-toss in a 76ers uniform.

James smoothly directed the Sixers offense in his time on the floor, making all five of his assists in the first quarter and combining effectively with Maxey.

“I think there was some really good things happening, you know, right off the bat,” 76ers coach Nick Nurse said after seeing his starters together for the first time.

“A bunch of back cuts and good passing et cetera … there were segments where obviously we turned the ball over a lot … just the little clunky segments, too. But, again, it’s pre-season, first time they’re together.

“I think you look at it as what’s good and what are the learning experiences, things that we can improve.”

The 76ers have two more pre-season games, both against Boston, before opening the NBA regular season against the defending champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on October 20.

James’s arrival has already found the 76ers battling outside “noise.”

James took to Instagram to refute a report from a play-by-play announcer during the team’s first pre-season game on Monday that James had admonished Embiid for being late to a practice.

“He ain’t been late, so stop the lie,” James posted.

James had acknowledged at the team’s media day last month that such outside hubbub around the 76ers would be “doubled, tripled and quadrupled now that I’m here.”

World.title: Tech scammer Elizabeth Holmes focus of documentary by absurdist Nathan Fielder
World.content:
Los Angeles – The private life of disgraced Silicon Valley startup founder Elizabeth Holmes will soon be aired to the public in a startling new documentary filmed in the 34 days before she went to prison.

The buzzy film from Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, out in US theaters October 16, captures the reclusive former executive’s world in the month before her incarceration for fraud at her now-defunct health technology company Theranos, whose lofty promises it couldn’t deliver.

Theranos falsely touted technology capable of performing medical tests using only a few drops of blood.

The project took Silicon Valley by storm in the early 2010s, as young entrepreneur Holmes drew investors — including Henry Kissinger, Carlos Slim and Rupert Murdoch — to her project.

But her fall proved just as rapid.

The sensational trial of Holmes ended in her 2022 sentencing to more than 11 years in prison for fraud and conspiracy.

The scandal fueled a media circus and was chronicled in a book, multiple podcasts, and the biographical mini-series “The Dropout” that starred Amanda Seyfried.

Holmes herself shied from the public eye, making the surprise release of the documentary “You Can See Everything” all the more astonishing when it debuted to high praise at the Telluride Film Festival in September.

– ‘Really sad and hard’ –

The film follows her life at home with partner Billy Evans and their two children, a hybrid of documentary and reality television portrayal that drew laughter, gasps and applause at a Los Angeles screening this week.

The Canadian comedian, writer and producer Fielder is famous for harnessing the power of awkwardness, cringe and deadpan wit to great, if unsettling, comedic effect.

He and Oppenheim said it was Holmes who initiated conversations with independent entertainment company A24 about documenting her daily life.

After a few meetings with the filmmakers, they said she invited them into her California home.

And things got strange.

Tuesday’s screening was attended by celebrities including Zach Cregger, Hannah Einbinder, Meg Stalter, Aziz Ansari and Hasan Piker, and during a discussion afterward the directors described their experience as “really sad and hard at times.”

“I still am not sure to this day, like, what I experienced, and it’s one of the reasons I’m excited for it to like come out and more people see it, because it was just a small group for so long,” Fielder said.

“Maybe it being out there, like everyone could help me understand what I went through a little bit.”

– ‘Uncomfortable’ –

Oppenheim said neither Holmes nor Evans voiced familiarity with his work when they opened their doors.

Fielder — the comic behind hit series like “The Rehearsal” and “Nathan For You,” shows that blur the line between reality and fiction — said there was “never a great explanation” as to why he should helm the project, “or why you would want to spend your last month of freedom in a decade with this guy.”

“I like to see myself as like a nice person overall, but still, I wouldn’t choose me.”

Fielder is a constant presence in the documentary, a decision made on the fly, the filmmakers said.

Close-up shots of him face-to-face with Holmes have ricocheted across social media and already become the stuff of meme gold.

Oppenheim said as the process rolled out it began to feel like “the only way, maybe, to actually make this is also to have someone kind of confront, you know, their delusions on certain aspects.”

In early images released by A24 Holmes is shown maintaining intense, unnerving eye contact with Fielder, scenes that made even him “uncomfortable,” he said.

“But I also felt like I was — these moments were so odd, and I was the one, like, ruining them or, like, bailing on them,” Fielder continued.

“At a certain point, I was like, ‘I’m not going to stop.’ If she’s looking at me, I’m just going to keep looking at her.”

The directors said living under the same roof as the documentary subjects created tensions and even saw Evans, who hasn’t seen the film, try to exert control over production.

But the filmmakers were never thrown out.

Like her partner, Holmes also hasn’t seen the finished product, Fielder and Oppenheim said. She remains in prison.

World.title: Trump’s ‘super intelligence’ rebrand to sell AI faces uphill battle
World.content:
Washington – Donald Trump’s campaign to rename artificial intelligence as “super intelligence” is unlikely to win over a wary public and could make matters worse, experts say, even as the US president threatens to treat holdouts as enemies.

On Thursday, he warned that anyone refusing to adopt the term would be considered an “ENEMY” by the White House, without saying what that would mean.

He had floated the name change in September before the UN General Assembly, saying it sounded much better.

“The use of the word artificial makes intelligence fake. It makes it sound fake, and it is not fake. It’s actually amazing,” he said.

He later signed an executive order mandating the term in government communications.

According to Jean-Pierre Dube, a marketing professor at the University of Chicago, there is a genuine concern at the White House that the backlash against AI and data centers could “stifle one of the key drivers of economic growth right now” and “cede technological dominance to China.”

However, “the idea that a re-brand that mis-characterizes the technology will turn around some of the public sentiment seems like wishful thinking,” he told AFP.

– ‘Poor choice’ –

But expert opinion matters little to Trump, who wrote in his book “The Art of the Deal”: “I don’t trust fancy marketing surveys. I do my own surveys and draw my own conclusions.”

He even polled users on Truth Social, where “super intelligence” beat out the other option, “superior intelligence.”

Americans see Trump as overly enthusiastic about artificial intelligence, which many already use but whose consequences for safety and jobs they fear, while also worrying about the rapid construction of massive data centers.

In a recent Quinnipiac University poll, only 25 percent of voters said they were satisfied with how the 80-year-old Republican is approaching AI, against 58 percent who were dissatisfied.

“If we believe that ‘artificial’ already encourages fear, ‘super’ seems like something far more worrisome,” said Dube, calling it “a poor choice of new brand.”

For Ronald Kline, a historian at Cornell University, “the phrase ‘super intelligence’ means more than simulating human intelligence, it means going beyond human intelligence,” he told AFP.

The term “artificial intelligence” was born in 1956 at an austere summer workshop at Dartmouth College.

Deliberately abstract, it was chosen to bring under one banner the research of scientists from varied backgrounds — mathematicians, psychologists and engineers driven by the same ambition: teaching computers, at the time enormous calculating machines, to “think” like humans.

Seen by some as a catch-all, the term never won unanimous support from the scientific community, which nonetheless came to accept it — as did Herbert Simon, winner of the 1978 Nobel Prize in Economics, who wrote as early as 1969: “‘artificial intelligence’ seems to be here to stay, and it may prove easier to cleanse the phrase than to dispense with it.”

For Kline, the name truly took off when it became the acronym AI, associated with the stratospheric growth of companies such as OpenAI.

The ChatGPT maker is not forced to change its name by Trump’s executive order, which applies only to the federal government.

But some of the sector’s top executives have chosen to follow the president, who closely tracks whether his various unilateral name changes are adopted.

The Associated Press news agency drew his wrath for refusing to adopt the name “Gulf of America” in place of “Gulf of Mexico.”

The term “super intelligence” has appeared in communications from Meta, Mark Zuckerberg’s group.

Elon Musk, a Trump ally, enthusiastically supports the name change and uses “super intelligence” in his posts on X.

A Washington industry lobbyist interviewed by AFP predicted a pragmatic approach from companies.

“I think you’ll see it used when it has to be used, i.e. when you’re communicating with the administration,” he said. “Insisting on ‘AI’ versus ‘super intelligence’ isn’t a fight you need to pick.”

World.title: Man City face Anfield cauldron after guilty Premier League verdicts
World.content:
Manchester – Manchester City are set for a hostile reception at Liverpool on Sunday in their first outing since being found guilty of over 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City have appealed and proclaim their innocence, but the Premier League leaders’ place in the division is now at threat following findings they used “sham” sponsorship deals to inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion).

Manchester United and Tottenham are both badly in need of a win when they meet at Old Trafford, while Arsenal aim to bounce back at home to Leeds following a rare defeat.

AFP sports looks at the pick of the action as the English top-flight returns after a three-week international break.

City face the music

City’s transformation into the dominant force in English football since an Abu Dhabi-backed takeover 18 years ago has cost Liverpool more than most.

The charges labelled against City cover the period between 2009 and 2018, but the foundations they built in that time ensured they remained the Premier League’s top dogs during the bulk of Pep Guardiola’s subsequent time in charge.

Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool twice missed out on the title to Guardiola’s side despite amassing over 90 points.

Those battles to be crowned champions of England over the past decade have turned this fixture into the Premier League’s marquee match-up and the eyes of the football world will be on Anfield again come Sunday.

City have won every game since Enzo Maresca replaced Guardiola, but their title challenge is likely to be ruined by a sanction unless they can overturn the verdict of an independent commission.

Liverpool will seek to capitalise on City’s uncertainty and kickstart their own campaign.

Andoni Iraola remains unbeaten as Liverpool manager but draws against Newcastle, Nottingham Forest and Fulham have left the Reds six points off top spot.

“I think it’s a big game and I think everyone is expecting to play, to watch, to be part of that game,” said Iraola.

“We know we will have to be at our best and also I know that the people will be looking to help the team.”

Pressure on Carrick

City’s scandal took the attention away from a difficult start to the season on the other side of Manchester.

United have taken just five points from what appeared an inviting opening five fixtures and now face a difficult run.

Just months after being handed the job as

manager on a permanent basis, Michael Carrick is the latest United boss facing scrutiny over his ability to turn around the fortunes of the ailing English giants.

After Saturday’s visit of Spurs, the Red Devils travel to Atletico Madrid, Leeds and Como in a nine-day period and also face Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa before next month’s international break.

Tottenham spent over £300 million on new players during the transfer window, but still had to endure the past three weeks rooted to the foot of the table after taking just two points from their opening five games.

Arsenal just getting started

Defending champions Arsenal are aiming to strike back when Leeds visit the Emirates in Saturday’s early kick-off.

A perfect start to the campaign for the Gunners ended in dramatic fashion with a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in their last outing.

But developments in the City case have reinforced Mikel Arteta’s men as bookies’ favourites to retain the title.

Arsenal manager Arteta extended his contract till 2030 this week and is determined that a first league title in 22 years is only the beginning of a golden age for the north London club.

“This is only the beginning of what we can achieve together,” said the Spaniard.

World.title: CNN, MS Now, Politico urge judge to extend White House access
World.content:
Washington – CNN, MS NOW and Politico urged a federal judge on Thursday to extend White House access to the three media outlets which President Donald Trump is seeking to ban.

District Judge Timothy Kelly prolonged until Tuesday the temporary White House access he granted to the news organizations last month and said he expected to issue a ruling by then.

Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House on September 18 for distributing what he called “fake news” and “fiction and lies.”

The three outlets filed a joint lawsuit asking for a temporary restraining order (TRO) against the ban on the grounds that it violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which upholds the right to a free press.

CNN, MS NOW and Politico appeared in a downtown Washington court on Thursday to ask that the judge transform his TRO into a preliminary injunction prohibiting Trump from barring them from the White House while the case proceeds.

Theodore Boutrous, a lawyer for the media outlets, said Trump issued the ban “because of what he perceives as negative, false, bad, not positive enough reporting.”

The Republican president, Boutrous said, apparently “got up on the wrong side of the bed and declared a ban on these news organizations.”

“He doesn’t like scrutiny of his policies. He doesn’t like the reporting. He wants more good press,” he said. “If your press pass is at risk because President Trump decides something you said is false, that’s a very, very dangerous, chilling doctrine.”

Justice Department attorney Michael Velchik, urging the judge to uphold the ban, accused CNN, MS NOW and Politico of violating “journalistic standards” and endangering national security by revealing classified information.

A skeptical Kelly asked Velchik whether it was a “a violation of minimum journalistic standards to portray the administration in a negative light?”

In his ruling last month temporarily restoring the White House credentials of CNN, MS NOW and Politico, the judge, who was appointed by Trump during his first term, said the ban “likely violated their constitutional due process rights.”

Trump has long attacked media that have aired critical coverage of him, repeatedly blasting the press as the “enemy of the people.”

Following the judge’s order, CNN, MS NOW and Politico were granted access to the White House grounds and the briefing room but have been kept out of the Oval Office and Air Force One.

In a rare move, the top five US broadcasters — ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox and NBC — halted pool coverage of the White House — where a broadcaster films on behalf of all television outlets for the day — in solidarity with CNN.

World.title: OpenAI says Iran, Russia influence ops busted
World.content:
Washington – OpenAI on Thursday said it shut down two influence operations — from Russia and Iran — that used ChatGPT to push fake journalist personas and run a “think-tank” to covertly peddle anti-Ukraine propaganda.

OpenAI’s report is the latest illustration of how state actors can easily exploit widely available AI tools to peddle sophisticated propaganda against adversaries on a mass scale.

The American AI giant said it banned a cluster of ChatGPT accounts that originated in Russia and Iran and were used to support “false front” entities for geopolitical and conflict-related messaging.

The Iranian operation involved seven “journalist” profiles, each purporting to be from Western countries including the United States, that were used to plant long-form articles in media outlets around the world.

“We identified almost 100 articles published or syndicated under the operation’s bylines across roughly a dozen online outlets around the world,” OpenAI said.

“These were small to medium outlets, generally focused on international affairs, geopolitics, and events in the Middle East.”

The earliest article identified by OpenAI was published in July 2025, and the latest in October 2026, with the frequency of reports increasing after the US-Iran war broke out earlier this year.

The operation also generated social media comments on topics related to the US-Iran war, it added.

One of the personas named Ervin B. Hoskins, whose bio claimed to be “an American freelance writer,” had social media accounts across tech platforms including Elon Musk’s X and Meta-owned Instagram.

X’s transparency information showed the account was connected via a “West Asia android app” and Instagram’s transparency information showed the account was based in Iran, according to screenshots provided by OpenAI.

Both accounts appeared to be suspended.

The Russian operation co-opted “unwitting people” in Latin America to run a “think-tank” — called the Social Research Center (SRC) — used for covert activities aimed at undermining Ukraine’s reputation in the region and to influence local politics, the company said.

“The available evidence indicates that the SRC’s employees in Latin America were not aware that they were working for a Russian group,” OpenAI said.

“The SRC appears to have produced a majority of original content via its co-opted staff. This stands out as the most complex attempt to run a front identity that we’ve disrupted over the past two and a half years.”

World.title: SC: Nothing wrong in deleting dead or those who've shifted
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday said there is nothing wrong in deletion of names of the dead, and those who have either shifted out from the ward or duplicate names during Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls but said that on the date of notification of elections, the voter list which is final - either the post-SIR list or the one on Jan 1, 2026, would be used for local body polls in Andhra Pradesh.

A bench of chief justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to entertain YSR Congress Party's appeal against Andhra Pradesh high court's decision rejecting its plea for deferment of local body elections till finalisation of SIR of electoral rolls.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The bench said SIR is a necessity as those who have passed away or shifted cannot be allowed to vote in the wards. The duplicate voters' names also are required to be struck down, and these are the anomalies that are taken care of through SIR, it said.

On the plea that HC has directed finalisation of post-SIR voter list by Oct 16, the bench said as per the legislations governing the panchayat, municipalities and municipal corporations, the elections would be held based on the final voter list available on the date when the EC notifies the elections.

When the SEC said that the election dates have not been notified and that it would be bound to take the final voter list available on the election notification date, the bench agreed and said if for some reason the post-SIR final electoral rolls are not published prior to the election notification, then the EC would consider holding polls based on the voter list as finalised on Jan 1, 2026.

World.title: No correlation between SIR deletions & assembly poll results: Bengal CEO
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The chief electoral officer of West Bengal Friday dismissed as "misleading and speculative" claims made in an "analysis" posted on YouTube that deletions made during special intensive revision in the state had a direct bearing on the outcome of the recent assembly elections.

In a post on X, the CEO quoted the analysis by DeKoder and countered it with electoral data from five West Bengal seats that saw the highest SIR deletions - four of them were won by

and one went to BJP. As for the five constituencies with the lowest SIR deletions, BJP ended up winning in all.

Refuting the claims made in the YouTube video - which relied on electoral data from 25 seats with the highest and lowest SIR deletions, and pointed to -10.5% and -5.3% swings respectively, for TMC - West Bengal's top electoral officer said "the electoral data...

does not support the political narrative".

The officer also dismissed the claim that women accounted for 62% of the electors deleted through SIR in West Bengal. "The claim... is unverified. As per the total data on deletion of invalid entries (excluding adjudication), around 50% or half of the deletions related to women," he posted on X.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Regarding the DeKoder claim that deletions of Muslim electors were 52% more than those of non-Muslim electors, the CEO pointed out there was no data based on religious identity of the voters.





"Hence the analysis claimed is based on mere unverified assumptions," he posted.

"...The facts do not support the allegations," the officer stated and asserted that no voter could be deleted without due process. "Issuance of notice, an opportunity for hearing and a speaking order by the ERO (electoral registration officer) are part of the safeguards. Appeals are available at two levels," he added.

The CEO said SIR was not about deleting genuine voters but about protecting the integrity of the electoral roll and was being conducted in accordance with Article 324 of Constitution and Section 21 of R P Act 1950, with due process and safeguards. "SIR is a lawful, transparent and ongoing exercise to ensure that every eligible elector is on the roll and that ineligible entries are removed. Electoral rolls must be based on facts - not speculation," he noted.

World.title: SC: Prioritise WB challenges to deletions over pleas for deletion
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections due in Dec and lakhs of appeals challenging post-SIR deletion and inclusion of names pending, Supreme Court Friday said the tribunals set up to examine claims should prioritise the challenges to deletions.

"There is a large chunk of appeals which seek deletion of names... These can be pushed behind the appeals which seek inclusion of names," said a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. They said they would consider on Oct 16 how to expedite hearings on petitions.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The bench's observation came after advocates Prashant Bhushan and G Sankaranarayanan complained that pendency of lakhs of appeals would result in disenfranchising a large number of voters in the municipal elections.

It would be appropriate to allow those who have appealed against deletion of their names to vote, they said.

The bench said, "We are already working on the issue of pendency of appeals before the tribunals... Probably, we will find a via media soon... Why the tribunals are taking time is intrinsically related to issues which require to be fixed including architecture of the software, etc."

World.title: Amid Form 7 bulk filing row, Election Commission limits it to 10 per elector
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Election Commission Friday, to discourage bulk submissions of Form 7 (objection to inclusion of an elector in the electoral roll), capped the maximum number of these applications that may be filed by an individual elector during the claims and objections period of special and summary revisions to 10.

For Form 7 applications filed by an individual elector during the period of continuous update of the electoral roll, the upper limit shall be five per month.

The ceilings - which follow Congress flagging bulk filings across many constituencies in Karnataka, including Ballari where a single BJP worker allegedly submitted 7,561 Form 7 applications - will apply to filings by individual electors both in online and offline modes.

In a letter to chief electoral officers of states and UTs, EC explained that while the number of applications to be filed online by an individual elector had been fixed as six at a time, subject to disposal, the number of physical forms presented in bulk had not been defined and was left to the judgement of electoral registration officers (ERO). The new limits seek to remove any scope for ambiguity, an EC officer told TOI.





According to Rule 13(2) of Registration of Electors Rules (RER) 1960, every objection to the proposed inclusion of name or application for deletion of name in the electoral roll of a constituency is to be referred only by a person whose name figures in the roll of that constituency.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

For the SIR period, EC has allowed booth-level agents of political parties to submit to a booth level officer Form 7 applications in bulk, with a limit of 50 forms per day before the draft publication and 10 forms per day thereafter.

The poll panel Friday said any claim or objection not lodged within the specified period or in the form and manner specified in the rules, shall be rejected by ERO, who will also verify the applicant's name in the electors' list.

Once a Form 7 application is found in line with norms, the ERO shall first issue a notice to the objector, hear him personally, record his statem-ents separately for each Form 7 and satisfy himself about the validity of the objections.

EC directed EROs to take action against false and fabricated Form 7s, including prosecution of the applicant under R P Act 1950 for knowingly making a false statement or declaration in writing.

World.title: Chemists, wholesalers may need government nod to advertise prescription drugs
World.content: NEW DELHI: Chemists, wholesalers and drug distributors may soon have to seek Centre's approval before advertising certain prescription medicines, with health ministry proposing to extend existing curbs on s of Schedule H, H1 and X drugs to those involved in their sale and distribution.The proposal assumes significance as regulators have raised concerns over promotion of potent prescription medicines, including antibiotics, hormonal preparations, psychotropic drugs, anti-cancer medicines, narcotic drugs and life-saving injectables.The ministry has now proposed inserting a new sub-rule under Rule 65 of Drugs Rules, 1945, stating no  of drugs specified in Schedule H, H1 or X shall be made without previous sanction of central govt. The provision would apply to those holding licences to sell, stock, exhibit, offer for sale or distribute such drugs.Importantly, the proposal does not mean that s of these medicines are currently freely permitted. Drugs and Cosmetics Rules already require prior govt sanction for s of Schedule H, H1 and X drugs.

World.title: Bypolls win shows deep connect with people: PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lauding BJP's winning show in Lok Sabha and assembly bypolls as a reflection of people's "deep-rooted connect" with his alliance's good governance agenda, PM Narendra Modi thanked people and said their mandate will further strengthen NDA.

"This mandate will give us added strength as we work for the welfare of people and to fulfil their aspirations for a brighter and more prosperous future," he said as BJP swept Nagaon Lok Sabha seat in Assam, and Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats in West Bengal. Its ally AINRC picked up Thattanchavady assembly seat in Puducherry.

Union minister Amit Shah seized on the results coupled with NDA's win in the recent local body polls in Rajasthan and Tripura to assert that people have rejected the INDIA bloc.

"Despite the lies, confusion and disinformation of Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc, BJP is winning one poll after another under PM Modi's leadership. Having lost their support base, these parties raise questions on institutions after defeat but people have recognised their character," he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

With the win coming in the middle of street protests govt is facing from Congress and its allies besides activist groups over the SIR row, BJP trumpeted it as "democracy's resounding message to the mob".





BJP's Smriti Irani said Rejinagar has 71% minority (Muslim) population. Nagaon also has a big Muslim population and had elected in 2024 a Congress MP, whose defection to BJP caused the bypoll. "While some believe in noise, these results show not only the collective wisdom of voters but also that our Constitutional framework is robust to deliver on the promise of democracy."

She noted that Congress ally TVK was poised to win both assembly seats in Tamil Nadu and wondered what the main opposition party has to say about this amid its "shrill campaign" over the alleged collusion between EC and govt to help the governing alliance. TNN

World.title: Congress stays away, Left & AAP to join CJP stir against CEC
World.content:

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party's invitation to all opposition parties to join its Oct 10 demonstration against EC's functioning under CEC Gyanesh Kumar saw only the Left, Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool and AAP openly backing its agitation. While the Left and AAP have announced their participation, it was not clear till Friday night whether Mamata's party would be part of the CJP protest.Before she reached Delhi, Mamata had told reporters that she may join the Oct 10 protest at Jantar Mantar, but added that nothing could be confirmed as yet. "We have maintained a relationship with them (CJP) and have extended our support, while any further decision regarding our participation will be taken later," she had said.The Left, Mamata TMC and AAP had earlier backed and participated in the CJP-led student agitation over the NEET-UG paper leak issue, which led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal will be joining with his family.Amid all this, Congress is keeping its distance from the CJP protest, with Rahul Gandhi to be in Chennai for the next edition of 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' Saturday."I appeal to everyone in the country to reach Jantar Mantar in the largest possible numbers. This is not about any one individual or political party; this is about the country. The protest at Jantar Mantar begins Saturday. I will be there, and my entire family will join me. Everyone should come there," Kejriwal said.On Friday, CPM general secretary MA Baby went all out to file a petition in Supreme Court challenging the restrictions imposed ahead of Saturday's protest, while TMC national spokesperson Saket Gokhale wrote to acting Chief Justice of Delhi HC seeking suo motu cognisance of cancellation of railway services and closure of metro stations.Sharing the letter on X, Gokhale extended "full support" to CJP and "every citizen demanding free and fair elections". TMC Rajya Sabha MP Derek O'Brien also put out a post strongly supporting CJP. Left parties CPM, CPI, CPI(ML)L, RSP and All India Forward Bloc issued a joint statement asserting that the right to assemble and protest is a fundamental right."We have been in the protest all these days. That will continue tomorrow too," Baby told TOI emphasising that the Left will be present in full force at the protest.

World.title: BJP: Musk must remember India's not a banana republic
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Slamming LoP

after he and

said this was evidence of hobnobbing with foreign players against national interest.

BJP said Musk must remember that he is not dealing with a banana republic. "He is dealing with a big country which is respected, whose leadership is respected globally. He should also be respectful towards this country and its leadership. This is Modi govt. Everything will happen in a transparent and non-discriminatory way," Party's Ram Madhav said, recalling the corruption allegations in the spectrum-allocation which had dogged the previous Congress-headed UPA govt.

"What is significant is that it is not the first time

Congress

netas have sought international support against the democratically elected govt in India," BJP's

Smriti Irani

said. BJP also recalled that Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh had once raised national security concerns if India approves the entry of Starlink, the satellite internet service offered by Musk-owned SpaceX.

Former Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan said Rahul is a flag-bearer of political opportunism.

Now, Congress has reversed its own position on an issue it once opposed on national security grounds. What changed in a year? Principles cannot be discarded for political convenience.

World.title: Karnataka Govt. writes to SLBC instructing against adjusting Gruha Lakshmi amount for loans
World.content:
The State government wrote to the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) on Friday (October 9, 2026) ordering that the monthly installment of ₹2,000 deposited into women’s accounts under the Gruha Lakshmi scheme should not be adjusted towards any loans, interest or other dues.

Additional Chief Secretary and Development Commissioner Uma Mahadevan has written to the SLBC convener in this regard.

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar had issued directions on these lines following a representation by MLC and State vice-president of Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority Dinesh Gooli Gowda.

In the letter, Ms. Mahadevan has issued guidelines that all commercial banks, cooperative banks, regional rural banks and other financial institutions in the State must compulsorily desist from adjusting the Gruha Lakshmi monthly amount against loans. The banks are also directed against auto debiting this amount from the beneficiaries’ accounts.

Money already deducted towards loan dues without clear written consent of beneficiaries should be immediately re-credited to respective women’s accounts, the letter said.

World.title: More taluks to be added to drought list by Karnataka
World.content:
Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara on Friday said that eight to 10 taluks more could be added to the list of drought-affected taluks before a final memorandum is submitted to the Centre.

While the State has already declared 217 taluks out of 240 in the State as drought-hit, ground truthing exercise is being undertaken in the rest 23.

“We are expecting that eight to 10 more taluks are likely to fall within the guidelines and will be declared as drought-affected. We want to take an all-party delegation to the Centre to seek compensation but the Opposition will not come. We will invite them again. Otherwise we will go and submit the memorandum.”

World.title: Dry spell pushes rice and toor dal price to new highs
World.content:
Amid a rain deficit of 35% between June and September in Karnataka, the prices of rice and toor dal have increased. The price of rice had already increased twice in two months between August and October.

This has impacted household budgets, while hotels are now weighing their options of increasing their rates.

For instance, the price of the Sona Masuri variety which was ₹75 per kg, has now increased to about ₹80, Basmati has gone up from ₹110 to ₹140 per kg, bullet rice from ₹80 to ₹100, Kolam rice from ₹75 to ₹100, and Rajamudi rice from ₹125 to ₹150, on an average, as per traders The Hindu spoke to.

The price of toor dal varieties have also increased by ₹10 to ₹15 per kg from what it was 10 days ago. The Gulbarga fatkar variety is priced at ₹145 per kg, from ₹125.

According to the Department of Agriculture, the target area for paddy cultivation for the kharif season was 10 lakh hectares while the sown area was only 6.2 lakh hectares. Last kharif season, it was 10.43 lakh hectares. The target area for toor dal this kharif was 16 lakh hectares while the sown area was 13.35 lakh hectares. Last year, the sown area was 14.16 lakh hectares.

Chamarasa Malipatil, president of Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha (KRRS), said: “The government did not release water from reservoirs in major paddy cultivation areas of Karnataka, including Ballari, Raichur, Gangavati, Mandya and a few districts of Malnad region, at the right time. It is the same with toor dal cultivating districts mainly in Kalaburagi. Hence, there is crop failure, no stock in market, and demand surge leading to hike in price.”

Mr. Malipatil pointed out that not all farmers benefit from price hike. Those who have stored the harvest from the rabi season will benefit as they can now sell it in the market, he said.

G.R. Denesh, Professor of Agronomy and Scheme Head at All India Coordinated Research Projects (Rice) run by Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), explained: “According to our estimation, more than 50% crop loss is likely to be recorded in paddy cultivating districts of Karnataka. It is a water-intensive crop and needs sufficient water and rains. Both were not available this year. If we get good rains by the end of October and November, then the price of rice and toor dal might stabilise or it will only increase.”

Shivakumar, general secretary, Karnataka State Rice Mills Association, said: “There are 700 rice mills operating across the State, but the stock of rice is low in the market. Two months ago, mill owners procured paddy at ₹3,500 per quintal which has increased to ₹4,600 to ₹4,700 per quintal. Neither the State nor the Union governments can regulate the price of rice here because they cannot ask farmers to decrease the price of their harvested crops.”

Muniswamy S., scientific officer, Directorate of Research, University of Agriculture in Raichur, said that Maharashtra and Karnataka are the leading producers of toor dal in India. “Even though there is toor dal yield in the State, the quality is not as expected because of less moisture in the atmosphere and infertile soil. Flowering is also delayed because of extreme heat in Kalaburagi.”

Mr. Muniswamy pointed out that floods in Kalaburagi last year was another reason for the price hike. “Floods impacted the production of toor dal in approximately 1.7 lakh hectares,” he said.

World.title: New scientific studies should be guided by previous research for better results, says former IISc director
World.content:
Any new scientific study should be guided by the history of studies that were done many years ago to obtain better results, said P. Balaram, former director, Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, on Friday evening.

In his inaugural address at the 11th International Cell and Gene Therapy Conference (CGTCON 2026), which was organised by Centre for Stem Cell Research (CSCR) at CMC in Vellore, Dr. Balram said that exhaustive research on various areas of specialisation of healthcare has been done many years ago. Such research findings should be the foundation for young scientists to conduct new research. “The history of research that was done over all these years remains a guiding light for young researchers to take their studies to new heights,” he said.

The former IISc director highlighted the importance of conducting more detailed and intensive research on blood disorders. Basic research by scientists would play a key role in finding ways to treat blood disorders, he said.

Earlier, Biju George, Director, CMC, said that it was way back in 1986, Mammen Chandy, who headed the Department of Haematology in CMC then, established Haematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT) as a curative form of treatment. “Matched sibling donor transplants were performed for a number of malignant and non-malignant haematological diseases. Unfortunately, a fully matched sibling or family donor can be identified in only 25% of families,” he said.

This year’s conference, that would end on October 10, will showcase developments across major disease areas, including haematological, ocular, diabetic and metabolic, neurological, cardiovascular, and dermatological disorders. It will also cover organoids and disease modelling, nucleic acid delivery technologies, and the industry, manufacturing, and regulatory aspects of advanced therapeutics.

The CGTCON 2026 aims to strengthen collaborations between clinicians, scientists, industry partners, and regulatory stakeholders.

World.title: Vellore Corporation begins providing drainage connections to households in town
World.content:
More than a decade after it was proposed, the ₹1,000-crore Underground Drainage (UGD) project in Vellore town has taken root as Vellore Corporation commences the process of providing drainage connections to individual households.

Corporation officials said that the multi-crore project was being implemented under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 2016-17 in four phases. “The Corporation has started providing drainage connections to households in areas under phase 2 and 3 of the UGD project. Most of the areas will be covered under these two phases of the work,” A. Catherine Saranya, Commissioner, Vellore Corporation, told The Hindu.

Corporation officials said that of the 1.41 lakh households in the town, around 71,000 drainage connections would be given under phases 2 and 3 of the project. Areas like Alamelumangapuram, Sathuvachari, Shenbakkam, Konavattam, Kaspa and Velapadi will be covered. “The connections provided to households under the UGD project will prevent discharge of wastewater into stormwater drains. It will also help towards improvement of hygiene in the area,” said S. Padma, a resident.

Divided into four phases, the project covers around 750 km of sewer lines, 16 pumping and lifting stations and two large STPs. Tricky spots, including 32 km on the service lane of Chennai - Bengaluru Highway (NH 48), 16 railway crossing spots, and State Highway stretches (7 km) have been completed.

Sewage treatment plants have been built at Muthu Mandapam near new bus terminus and at Sarkar Thoppu near Katpadi to handle at least 60.5 MLD. The civic body has built a pipe carrying bridge, which is 650 metres long, along the Palar river, to carry household sewerage from 32 wards, mostly from Old Town areas to the newly-constructed STP near Katpadi. The bridge is being built at a height of 20 feet from the river bed to prevent inundation during monsoon. The new STP has a capacity of 50MLD.

Civic officials said that the new drainage network would help to prevent inundation of Vellore town during monsoon as wastewater from houses would now get discharged into the drainage network.

In other words, illegal discharge of wastewater into stormwater drains would stop, thereby allowing free flow of excess rainwater in the drains that would get discharged into the Palar river.

Corporation officials said that each household connection, on an average, would cost around ₹7,000. However, the deposit amount would be collected in instalments from consumers after adding it to property tax.

World.title: flydubai co-pilot intended to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport, UAE prosecutor says
World.content:
The axe-wielding co-pilot who attacked the captain of a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv last month intended to seize control of the airplane and fly it into the passenger terminal at Israel's main international airport, authorities in the United Arab Emirates said Friday (October 9, 2026).

The suspect, an Omani national, did so “with the intention of causing the greatest possible number of human casualties,” the UAE's top prosecutor said in a statement carried by the state news agency WAM. Most of the 174 passengers on the flight were from Israel.

The statement said the co-pilot “drew inspiration” from the Sept 11, 2001 attacks in the United States and used two previous flights from Dubai to Tel Aviv to “familiarise himself with the flight route and the airport”.

It said none of flydubai's security or professional checks had indicated that the pilot, who was identitifed by The Associated Press as 29-year-old Hamam al-Hammami, harboured extremist views or plans to carry out an attack.

Mr. Hammami “admitted that he had acted alone, without the involvement of others,” the statement said, adding that he “provided a detailed confession outlining his motives and the stages of planning and execution” in the presence of his lawyer.

It also suggested he was radicalised at a mosque in Australia while attending the Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology in 2017.

The update from the public prosecutor Friday (October 9, 2026) was the most comprehensive since the UAE took over the investigation shortly after the incident on Sept 30. flydubai is a government-owned airline.

The crisis unfolded suddenly in the skies above Jordan and Saudi Arabia, when Mr. Hammami attacked the Indian captain, Smit Machchhar, with a crash axe in the cockpit. Bloodied and beaten, Mr. Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, alerting passengers and crew to the assault.

Passengers detained Hammami and helped steady the aircraft, which had plunged roughly 14,000 to 16,000 feet in less than a minute. Two reserve pilots then guided the plane to an emergency landing at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Katie Zacharia picked as White House press secretary
World.content:
Katie Zacharia, ‌a communications adviser for President Donald ​Trump’s Truth Social platform, has ⁠been offered the position of White House press secretary following Karoline Leavitt’s ‌departure from the role in August, a White House ‌official said on Friday (October 9, 2026).

Ms. Zacharia ‌did ⁠not immediately respond to ⁠a request for comment, but if she accepts the role, she would fill ​a critical role ‌in the Trump administration before next month’s midterm congressional elections.

The New York Times first reported ‌the news.

Ms. Zacharia briefly served ​as a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security before ⁠departing in March.

The conservative commentator is a senior communications adviser ‌for Truth Social and the Trump Media & Technology Group, according to her LinkedIn page.

Ms. Zacharia previously worked as a legal adviser for Fix California, a conservative ‌group that aims to address what ​it described as “the left’s stranglehold” on state politics. The group ⁠was founded by Richard Grenell, ⁠who has served as Mr. Trump’s envoy to Venezuela and is ‌the interim president and executive director of the Kennedy ​Center in Washington.

World.title: Magnitude 7.6 earthquake shakes Panama, USGS reports
World.content:
A second powerful 6.6 magnitude earthquake struck Panama Friday (October 9, 2026) afternoon following a series of aftershocks, the US Geological Survey said. It came after a magnitude 7.7 quake shook the Central American country, collapsing buildings near its epicenter and prompting evacuations.

The quake, which was felt as far away as neighboring Colombia, was centered about 10 kilometers (6 miles) southwest of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, in the central province of Herrera, the U.S. Geological Survey said. It struck at a depth of 10 kilometers (6 miles).

The USGS initially reported the quake as magnitude 8, then revised it to 7.6 and later to 7.7.

Visibly shaken residents of Panama City gathered outside as they waited for news of the quake’s impact on Friday (October 9, 2026).

“We felt it very strongly. It knocked things over in the kitchen, but we’re okay, though we’re very scared,” Rosendo Domínguez, 60, who is from Herrera province, where the earthquake struck, told The Associated Press by phone. “Everyone is outside, scared.”

Multiple aftershocks continued to rattle Panama, including several measuring magnitude 5.8, 5.5 and 5.2. Seismologists at the University of Panama recorded more than 45 aftershocks, though many were too weak to be felt.

Calls for calm and reports of collapsed buildings

Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino called for calm on Friday (October 9, 2026), writing on X: “What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder.”

Omar Smith of the National Civil Protection Service said on the Telemetro Reporta news channel that damage was concentrated in the central provinces of Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos. He said there were no reports of damage in the capital, which is known for its hundreds of skyscrapers.

Mr. Smith said several injuries have been reported, including one person struck by debris from a partially collapsed structure in the city of Penonomé, around 93 miles (150 km) from the capital. He confirmed a partial collapse and cracks at the cathedral in the district’s main square, as well as damage in the governor’s office building and the Dos Continentes hotel. No casualties were immediately reported.

Local news outlets also reported that the Church of San Atanasio, a colonial-style Catholic church in Panama’s Los Santos province, had collapsed. The church was declared a National Historic Heritage Site in 1938. Elsewhere, including in Veraguas province, large fissures ran along roadways.

Tocumen International Airport in Panama City, one of the region’s busiest airports with more than 20 million travelers in 2025, said it would temporarily suspend operations and activated evacuation plans. It said operations would resume once security conditions have been checked.

The Panama Canal Authority said operations were continuing normally along the key global trade route. It said its priority was the safety of employees, vessels and crews and that specialized technical teams were inspecting facilities for possible damage.

Tsunami warnings as far as Chile’s Easter Island

The last major earthquake to cause widespread damage in Panama struck in 1991. A magnitude 7.4 quake, centered in nearby Costa Rica killed 23 people, injured 559, and left thousands of people homeless in the border Bocas de Toro region.

Earthquakes are common, especially along Panama’s border with Costa Rica and its Pacific coast, because of the interaction of several tectonic plates, including Cocos, Nazca, and Caribbean plates.

Panama lies along the “Ring of Fire,” a 40,000-kilometer (25,000-mile) arc of volcanoes and fault lines around the Pacific Basin, where most of the world’s earthquakes occur.

The National Weather Service issued a tsunami warning Friday (October 9, 2026) for the coasts of Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Guatemala. It warned that waves ranging from 3 to 9 feet (1 to 3 meters) above tide may occur in some coastal areas of Panama.

Alerts were also issued in El Salvador and as far as Chile’s Easter Island, about 3,500 kilometers (2,175 miles) off Chile’s mainland coast. Chile’s government placed the island under a precautionary advisory.
